detail.abstract: We study whether the timing of quote revisions contains information about liquidity stress that is not captured by the magnitude of price movements. We develop a subordinated-Lévy framework that separates return variation into a diffusion component and a component associated with irregular business time. The clock-dispersion parameter measures how unevenly price revisions occur over calendar time. Using S&P 500 index quotes around stress and policy events and 779 trading days of SPY National Best Bid and Offer data from 2007-2025, we find that clock dispersion is related to the dispersion of mid-quote revisions and rises sharply around FOMC statements. The response is concentrated in the statement window, while changes are not observed around CPI and employment releases. We find little evidence that clock dispersion forecasts liquidity conditions. The results support the interpretation that timing irregularity can help describe liquidity stress within an event window, while its forecasting role remains limited.

detail.abstract: Regulators, content platforms, and academic journals increasingly require creators to disclose the use of artificial intelligence (AI), yet how audiences respond is unmeasured. In an incentivized virtual-reality art market, 205 participants valued identical paintings under randomly assigned attributions; AI attribution reduced willingness to pay by 22.6% of the reference price. In 132,883 reviews on an online fiction platform, AI-attributed books were both less likely to be chosen to be read and were rated 1.6% lower. The penalty is concentrated in private valuations, not in social expectations; it declines with a consumer’s cumulative exposure to labeled work; and it is largest for creators without an established reputation. AI disclosure therefore changes what consumers will pay for identical work, and the design of the rule determines which creators incur the loss.

detail.abstract:
Organizations are created to make a difference. But meaningful impact today does not guarantee that an organization will remain capable of making that difference tomorrow.

Enduring Impact: Designing Organizations Built to Last in a Volatile World examines what leaders can do to build organizations capable not merely of achieving impact, but of sustaining, protecting and deepening that impact over time. Endurance is not the natural reward of success; it is a distinct objective that requires deliberate design.

Organizations operate in an environment of persistent political, economic, technological, demographic and social change. Strategies, funding sources, leadership teams and operating models that work well today may become sources of vulnerability tomorrow. The challenge is therefore not to predict or eliminate volatility, but to build organizations capable of adapting to it without losing sight of why they exist.

Drawing on research, organizational experience and practical examples, Enduring Impact develops a framework for meeting that challenge. It explores mission anchoring, governance for the long horizon, financial resilience, culture as an institutional shock absorber and strategic optionality. It then turns to leadership: how leaders can navigate uncertainty, resist mission drift, manage succession and preserve institutional knowledge beyond the tenure of any particular founder or executive. The final chapters ask leaders to look even further ahead. The Thirty-Year Test provides a practical approach to stress-testing organizational design against futures that cannot be confidently predicted, while measures of institutional durability help identify emerging weaknesses before they become crises. The book concludes by reframing endurance as an act of stewardship. Leaders are responsible not only for what their organizations accomplish while they are in charge, but also for the capabilities, relationships, knowledge and choices they leave to those who follow.

For leaders of nonprofits, social enterprises, businesses and other mission-driven organizations, Enduring Impact offers a practical guide to building organizations that can change with the world without surrendering the purpose they were created to serve.

title: Why Organizations Remember Events but Repeat Their Causes Causal Reactivation, Reopening, and Authority in Recurrent Organizational Failure
affiliations: Hoopoe Holding Ltd.

detail.title: Why Organizations Remember Events but Repeat Their Causes Causal Reactivation, Reopening, and Authority in Recurrent Organizational Failure

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

detail.abstract: Organizations can document a failure in extraordinary detail and still reproduce the conditions that caused it. The problem is not always forgetting. An incident report may remain searchable while the causal account it contains is no longer recognized, qualified, routed to the actor who can change the producing relationship, or tested after intervention. This article develops Corrective Memory as a temporal and institutional capacity: the ability to preserve a qualified causal account of a consequential episode and reactivate it when a comparable situation returns. The account must retain the conditions under which it was formed, the uncertainty and competing explanations that limit it, the authority and responsibility relevant to intervention, and the evidence that would confirm, revise, or retire it. The construct is positioned against organizational memory, organizational learning, sensemaking, routines, knowledge boundaries, error management, and organizational forgetting. Its contribution is deliberately narrower than any of these literatures. Corrective Memory concerns the conversion of retained history into future reality-testing and structural action. The article specifies a memory-to-correction cycle of capture, causal reconstruction, qualification, retention, reactivation, authority routing, intervention, and verification with reopening. It develops nine propositions, a formative audit architecture for empirical work, rival explanations, boundary conditions, falsification tests, and a conditional account of generative AI as either a provenance-preserving retrieval aid or a causal-compression device. The paper is conceptual and reports no original empirical observations. Its central claim is that organizational intelligence is incomplete when an institution can remember the event but cannot carry forward a contestable explanation of why it mattered, recognize when that explanation applies again, and connect the account to a legitimate path of intervention.

detail.abstract: Zero-day attacks exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities or use attack behaviors that have not been adequately represented in existing security rules, making them difficult for conventional signature-based intrusion detection systems to identify. Machine learning-based behavioral analysis provides an alternative approach by learning patterns of normal and abnormal network activity and identifying deviations that may indicate previously unseen threats. This paper examines a machine learning-based behavioral analysis framework for detecting zero-day threats in enterprise networks. The proposed approach combines network traffic collection, feature extraction, behavioral profiling, anomaly detection, and continuous model adaptation. Algorithms such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Isolation Forest, and neural-network-based anomaly detectors can be applied to identify suspicious deviations in network behavior. Behavioral analysis is particularly relevant because zero-day detection cannot depend exclusively on previously generated attack signatures. Research has shown that machine learning has potential for zero-day detection, although challenges remain in data quality, generalization, false positives, adversarial manipulation, and real-time deployment. (NIST)

detail.abstract: In fragile and conflict-affected settings, insecurity diagnostics routinely rely on single perspectives-event data, administrative reporting, or population surveys-treating divergence across sources as measurement error. This paper advances a different proposition: insecurity is not only a level to be measured, but a relationship to be diagnosed. We develop and apply a multi-actor diagnostic framework that treats systematic divergence between resident and authority assessments of insecurity as an analytically meaningful outcome rather than a residual. Using harmonised survey instruments across Niger and Mali, we construct a parsimonious Core Insecurity Index capturing current insecurity and perceived change over time, and operationalise misalignment through signed gaps, absolute divergence, and quadrant configurations. The comparative results reveal sharply different structures of misalignment. Niger exhibits wide dispersion and frequent off-diagonal configurations between resident and authority assessments, while Mali shows substantially lower divergence and stronger convergence, with meaningful sub-national variation. These patterns are robust to alternative index constructions and sampling sensitivities. Substantively, the findings demonstrate that insecurity diagnostics fail most predictably where insecurity is lived as anticipatory constraint-through mobility restriction, uncertainty, and everyday adaptation-rather than as administratively visible incidents. Methodologically, the paper reframes triangulation from a logic of validation to one of inference, showing how disagreement itself can function as a diagnostic signal of information asymmetry, governance incentives, and legitimacy conditions. The study contributes a portable diagnostic approach for insecurity measurement in fragile settings, with implications for research design, policy targeting, and security governance.

title: THE CHRISTIAN ETHICS OF DATING PREFERENCES

detail.abstract: Dating preferences sit at the intersection of freedom, attraction, moral judgment, culture, embodiment, prudence, and human dignity. They are often discussed in two inadequate ways. One treats every preference as morally innocent because attraction is personal; the other treats every exclusion or boundary as a verdict on another person's worth. This paper develops a biblical and interdisciplinary framework that rejects both reductions. It argues that no person is entitled to another person's romantic interest, courtship, or marriage, and that a prospective partner may exercise genuine freedom in discerning whom to date or marry. At the same time, preferences are not morally sealed from examination. They can be shaped by prudence, vocation, attraction, shared faith, life stage, capacity, family obligations, cultural familiarity, fear, status competition, stereotypes, pornography, contempt, prejudice, or social pressure. Christian ethics therefore should neither command involuntary attraction nor exempt the formation and expression of preferences from moral scrutiny. The paper distinguishes intrinsic dignity from desirability, preference from moral judgment, attraction from action, compatibility from superiority, non-negotiables from conveniences, prudential boundaries from contempt, and private partner selection from the obligations of justice owed to all neighbors. It integrates biblical theology, Catholic teaching on dignity and free matrimonial consent, and psychological research on ideal-partner preferences, speed-dating, similarity, online dating, and the imperfect relationship between stated preferences and actual romantic desire. The central proposal is a four-level ethics of dating preference: persons may notice what attracts them, examine how those attractions were formed, decide responsibly in light of vocation and evidence, and communicate boundaries without humiliation. Dating freedom is real; romantic entitlement is not. Moral discernment is legitimate; human ranking is not. Christian courtship is most faithful when freedom, truth, chastity, prudence, equal dignity, and neighbor-love remain together.

detail.abstract:
Purpose: Cleaner-production programmes in industrial clusters are routinely judged by demonstrated technical performance, yet environmental improvement persists only if firms implement, co-invest and embed the practices in institutions that outlive the project. This study assesses how far that transition proceeded, and where its evidence ends, in the Kanpur-Unnao leather cluster, India, through an ex-post assessment of a seven-year programme in a cluster of more than 400 tanneries in the Ganga basin.

Methodology: An ex-post desk assessment of the FDW16007IN cleaner-production programme was conducted using an evidence-triangulation and claim-evidence protocol. Programme-reported quantitative indicators were examined alongside the independent endline evaluation, programme documentation, regulatory records and relevant scholarly literature. Differences in evidence provenance, measurement basis, denominator and verification status were retained rather than reconciled. The assessment therefore distinguishes documented outcomes from findings that cannot be established from the available evidence.

Findings: Project monitoring reported a 41% average reduction in water consumption across 40 pilot tanneries, while self-monitoring by 20 companies indicated a decline from 45-50 to 28 m³/t. Reported raw-effluent chromium, BOD, COD and TSS declined by 74.4%, 61.3%, 65.6% and 91.1%, respectively. Recorded industry contribution was approximately €301,231 against €50,000 planned, including €83,386 in own-cost replication. A 2023 National Green Tribunal order corroborated regulatory embedding of specified cleaner-production measures and independently documented a subset of relevant installations in the cluster. However, no counterfactual was available, and the independent evaluation considered the post-demonstration period insufficient to assess replication systematically.

Originality/value: The study provides an evidence-disciplined assessment of a cluster cleaner-production programme while distinguishing environmental improvement, implementation, institutional embedding and durable diffusion. It demonstrates the value of separating these stages when evaluating cleaner-production programmes where programme records combine different evidence sources and levels of verification.

detail.abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of negative relationships among employees on job performance through a systematic and analytical review of recent literature and empirical studies. The study adopts an integrated theoretical framework combining Social Exchange Theory and Conservation of Resources Theory to explain the mechanisms through which negative relationships translate into performance deterioration. Findings indicate that negative relationships negatively affect job performance with regression coefficients ranging between β =-0.42 and β =-0.48, and that this effect operates through multiple mediators including emotional exhaustion, lowered perceived organizational support, and perceived organizational isolation. Results also show that certain organizational factors, such as task interdependence and high-quality social exchange, are capable of neutralizing the negative effects of strained relationships. The study presents an integrated conceptual framework distinguishing between direct and indirect effect mechanisms, along with practical recommendations for organizations seeking to protect their performance from the erosion caused by negative relationships.

keywords: Ma. Cecilia. 2026. Abandonment and Covenant Responsibility: A Biblical and Interdisciplinary Theology of Desertion

detail.abstract: This working paper examines abandonment as a problem of covenant responsibility rather than as a mere synonym for physical departure. It argues that Christian moral reasoning must distinguish unjust desertion from legitimate separation, temporary absence, safety-related withdrawal, migration or work-related distance, incarceration, illness, and other conditions in which physical presence and moral responsibility do not map neatly onto one another. In marriage, abandonment is best understood as a serious and potentially asymmetric failure of covenantal presence and duty: a spouse may withdraw cohabitation, fidelity, support, parental responsibility, truthfulness, or willingness to sustain the marital common good without adequate cause, while the other spouse may remain bound to responsibilities that the deserter has refused. Scripture gives particular attention to marital fidelity, care for one's household, truthful covenant keeping, and the case in which an unbelieving spouse departs in 1 Corinthians 7:15. Catholic teaching likewise distinguishes the ordinary duty of conjugal living from legitimate separation and explicitly recognizes the moral difference between the spouse who unjustly abandons a marriage and the innocent spouse who is abandoned. The paper develops a category-separation framework that distinguishes departure from abandonment, initiation from culpability, physical absence from functional desertion, forgiveness from restored access, reconciliation from unilateral return, and the abandoned person's remaining duties from responsibility for the other's breach. Interdisciplinary evidence on relationship dissolution, initiator status, ambiguous separation, and post-separation adjustment is used descriptively rather than as a substitute for moral theology. The central thesis is that covenant responsibility can become morally asymmetric: one spouse's abandonment can impose real burdens on the other without transferring the abandoning spouse's guilt or unfulfilled duties to the abandoned spouse. Christian care must therefore hold together covenant seriousness, protection from harm, truthful attribution of agency, continuing duties to children, possibilities of repentance and repair, and the dignity of every person involved.

title: Robust Multi-Item Demand Autobidding Auctions
affiliations: ,  and Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) - Sloan School of Management

detail.title: Robust Multi-Item Demand Autobidding Auctions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Yifeng Teng is an employee of Google Research.
declarations.funderStatement: Yifeng Teng is an employee of Google Research.

detail.abstract:
Over the last decade, advertising platforms have increasingly adopted autobidding interfaces in which advertisers only submit high level campaign objectives rather than individual, granular bids within each auction. In this paper, we study sponsored shopping, where distinct product listings compete for ranked positions for the same user and one advertiser can win several slots. Each bidder submits one pacing multiplier-a common factor multiplying the values of all of its advertisements to determine their bids. We compare the welfare price of anarchy (PoA)-the worst equilibrium welfare divided by optimal welfare-of generalized first-price (GFP), generalized second-price (GSP), and the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves mechanism (VCG) when bidders may be either quasi-linear (QL) utility maximizers or value-maximizers (VM). 

Our main finding is that GFP maintains a constant 0.4569 PoA whilst both GSP and VCG have a PoA of 0. We further obtain bounds that are tight in the equilibrium support. These bounds show precisely how rapidly the welfare guarantee decays as a function of the minimum and maximum multipliers. That being said, our PoA results are contingent upon equilibrium existence, which is not guaranteed due to the returnon-investment (ROI) constraint. Nevertheless, we show that a smoothed version of our auction guarantees equilibrium existence and maintains the original auction PoAs up to vanishing error terms. We then prove that there exists an efficient no regret learning algorithms over the space of all possible mixed strategies. Using these algorithms, we simulate the learning dynamics and find that the threat of low worst-case welfare in GSP and VCG is real: the dynamics can often fail to escape low welfare regions. In stark contrast, the dynamics of GFP consistently escape these low welfare regions and often do significantly better than its 0.4569 lower bound, as well as generating more revenue. 

Managerial Insights. Among the three mechanisms, GFP is universally robust-it achieves a constant fraction welfare guarantee over a broad equilibrium class in spite of the challenges of multi-item demand, mixed bidder objectives, and randomized deviations. In contrast, even in very simple settings, GSP and even VCG can yield nearly 0 welfare and, as seen in our experiments, low revenue. Our analysis shows that these welfare guarantees weaken as multipliers become more extreme, motivating platforms to match advertisers' intended spending pace and reduce the need for sharp corrections to return-on-investment targets and bids.

detail.abstract:
State and local governments across the United States have filed suit in state courts against major fossil fuel companies, seeking compensation for climate-related damage to their infrastructure, public resources, and communities. These suits allege that the defendant companies knew for decades that their products were driving catastrophic climate change, concealed that knowledge, and ran sophisticated deception campaigns to protect their profits. The companies and their supporters contend that the Clean Air Act and the Constitution foreclose the claims. The Supreme Court's grant of certiorari in Suncor Energy, Inc. v. Board of County Commissioners of Boulder County will require the Court to decide whether these preemption arguments succeed.

This essay argues that they clearly do not. The Clean Air Act's savings clauses affirmatively preserve state remedies, and American Electric Power Co. v. Connecticut expressly left the state-law preemption question open; the presumption against preemption in this area of traditional state authority applies with full force and has not been rebutted. Neither the Act's text, nor its occupation of any field, nor any conflict with its objectives forecloses state common law claims for climate-related harm—from nuisance, negligence, and trespass to fraud and concealment. The claim that the Constitution's allocation of foreign affairs authority to the federal government preempts such suits misreads relevant precedent, has no limiting principle, and has been rejected by the courts that have considered it. And the fraud and deception allegations at the heart of many of these suits are further still from any basis for preemption: they address conduct the Clean Air Act does not regulate and that no federal statute has ever been held to preempt.

The essay also advances several arguments that the parties' briefs do not reach. First, damages and locally confined relief lack the extraterritorial reach that alone could justify centralizing authority over emissions. Second, the Trump Administration's 2026 rescission of the greenhouse gas endangerment finding removes the regulatory predicate on which the "speaks directly" rationale, and thus the preemption theory, depends. Third, after Loper Bright, courts owe no deference to any agency claim that federal inaction preempts state law. Finally, preserving overlapping state and federal authority provides significant governance benefits. Communities that have endured the costs of climate harm—caused by corporations that allegedly knew the consequences and hid them—are entitled to their day in court. The Constitution simply does not shield polluters from paying for the harms they cause.

keywords: Ma. Cecilia. 2026. Injury Is Not Inferiority: A Biblical and Interdisciplinary Theology of Betrayal

detail.abstract: This working paper examines a recurring moral error: the conversion of injury, deprivation, victimization, disability, rejection, trauma, illness, or poverty into evidence that a person is lesser. It argues that Christian anthropology requires a strict distinction between what has happened to a person, what capacities may have been affected, what responsibilities may remain, and what the person is worth. Human dignity is not a reward for remaining uninjured, independent, socially desired, economically secure, psychologically untroubled, or physically able. It is grounded in the human person's creaturely status, the image of God, and, in Christian theology, redemption in Christ. The study therefore rejects both dehumanizing pity and sentimental denial. Injuries can be grave; disability can alter functioning; trauma can disrupt memory, trust, affect, and bodily regulation; poverty can constrain options; wrongdoing can incur responsibility; and suffering can produce enduring losses. None of these realities, however, establishes ontological inferiority. Drawing on biblical theology, Catholic teaching on human dignity and suffering, disability-rights frameworks, trauma scholarship, stigma research, and capability approaches to poverty, the paper develops a disciplined framework for separating dignity from functioning, victimization from culpability, impairment from worth, dependence from lesser personhood, social exclusion from moral defect, and healing from eligibility for respect. It also cautions against the opposite error of romanticizing suffering, demanding resilience, or treating post-traumatic growth as an obligation. The paper proposes a twelve-gate Injury, Dignity, and Response Assurance framework for pastoral, community, relational, and institutional discernment. Its governing conclusion is that injury may change needs, risks, capacities, responsibilities, and forms of support, but it does not lower the human person's rank as a person.

title: The Queue Was the Arbitrage: What 147 Days of Tick-Size Asymmetry Were Worth

detail.title: The Queue Was the Arbitrage: What 147 Days of Tick-Size Asymmetry Were Worth

The order-book recordings and the live window detector used in the paper are the author's own. The author holds no position that depends on the paper's findings, received no payment from any exchange, data vendor or other party, and has no relationship with the venues beyond that of an ordinary retail customer. detail.abstract: On 14 April 2026 Venue A cut the tick size of USDC/USDT from 0.0001 to 0.00001. Venue B did not follow until 8 September. For the 147 days in between, two of the largest spot venues for the same pegged asset quoted it on grids differing by a factor of ten, with zero trading fees on both. This paper measures what that asymmetry was worth. It was worth almost nothing, and the reason is instructive. Measured on both venues' published trade tapes, the cross-venue price difference reached half a basis point 41.5% of the time during the window and 0.10% of the time after it closed, a four-hundredfold change with a single overnight break and no trend on either side of it. The gap was therefore real, large and persistent. It was also, for practical purposes, untradeable, by two independent measurements. First, a taker-to-taker bound built only from prices that actually printed yields an upper bound of 4.3% a year when the two legs are allowed to be a second apart and 0.1% a year when they must be within ten milliseconds; the apparent opportunity is mostly price drift inside the matching window, and it is larger after the window closed than during it. Second, a queue-realistic replay of the obvious strategy over 91 coarse-grid days, resting a passive quote on the coarse venue and hedging each fill on the fine one, earns $3.14 a day on a $10,000 quote for a participant who joins the back of the queue, about 5.7% a year on the inventory the two legs require, and 130 times that for one who is first in line at every re-price and thereby absorbs a fifth of the venue's entire volume. The mechanism is that a coarse tick does not create an arbitrage; it creates a rent, and the rent belongs to whoever is at the front of the queue. Across the whole window the coarse grid's one-basis-point effective spread splits into about 0.62 to 0.66 bp realised by makers and 0.34 to 0.39 bp of price impact, against 0.03 bp and 0.07 bp on the fine-grid venue over the same days: an adverse-selection share of a third to two fifths on the coarse book against two thirds on the fine one. The split is computed by reconstructing each venue's mid from its own trade tape, an identity that holds because both venues quote a one-tick spread almost always, and it is verified against the coarse venue's own published order book on 86 days, where the two methods differ by half a hundredth of a basis point. The result replicates. The larger venue cut its own tick on 14 April and the smaller on 8 September, five months apart on the same asset, and each venue's realised spread falls by a factor of about twenty at its own change. The transfer is large in dollars and small per trade: venue A's takers paid $1.0 million of queue rent in thirteen coarse-grid days and venue B's paid $0.64 million over 147. Narrowing the tick removed the rent, the queue and the gap together, multiplied the venue's volume fourfold, and, for the first time, made its mid price move often enough for price discovery to be measurable at all.

detail.abstract: Humanitarian and early-recovery finance is increasingly expected to show not only where needs are greatest, but whether interventions accelerate recovery and generate measurable economic value. We combine monthly satellite data with georeferenced programme records in difference-indifferences designs to evaluate early-recovery interventions after the 2025 Myanmar earthquake and during the ongoing crisis in Gaza. In Myanmar, nighttime luminosity in UNDP-supported townships was 19-23% higher than in comparison townships after implementation. Converting this gain into economic output implies that approximately US$5 of local economic activity was brought forward per dollar of programme spending. In Gaza, radar backscatter reveals a consistent localized signal across four nearby comparison bands, providing evidence of physical change associated with recovery work. These results are robust under different model specifications and after adjusting for seasonal fluctuations. By linking satellite-observed recovery to programme expenditure, the framework provides timely, independently observed evidence for evaluating early recovery and informing outcome-linked finance for post-disaster reconstruction.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether the timing of an assessment changes the proficiency it records. It exploits student-level random assignment to mirrored test forms in PISA 2025 that place Learning in the Digital World (LDW) in either the first or second hour of the same testing session, while reversing its order with science, reading or mathematics. The analysis covers 205,114 students across 84 participating education systems and accounts for student sampling weights, Faymodified balanced repeated-replication weights and ten plausible values. Assigning LDW to the second hour reduces measured LDW performance by 0.093 within-system standard deviations, equivalent to approximately 8.3 PISA points. The estimated effect is negative in 78 of 84 systems and is robust to alternative support restrictions, weighting procedures and leave-one-system-out analyses. The mirrored assignment simultaneously raises performance in the paired conventional domain when that domain is moved to the first hour, producing an even larger shift in measured comparative advantage across domains. Process outcomes indicate lower credit at the learning, application and demonstration stages, fewer observable actions, shorter time investment and increased disengagement. The penalty is attenuated among students with greater perseverance and amplified among those reporting greater digital distraction. These results show that assessment schedules can alter both measured proficiency and the relative skill profiles attributed to students. The "second-hour tax" represents the total effect of randomized test position rather than pure physiological fatigue.

detail.abstract: Ukraine cannot change its geographical position, but it can change the strategic meaning of that position. This book argues that postwar reconstruction should do more than restore destroyed assets: it should create productive, scientific, technological, infrastructural and institutional capabilities that embed Ukraine more deeply in international networks. It develops a progression from buffer to bridge and from bridge to strategic hub-a country whose value derives not simply from location or transit, but from functions that international partners consider important and difficult to replace. The analysis connects capability-creating reconstruction, experimental governance, science and technology policy, strategic embeddedness and distributed international stakeholding. Drawing selective lessons from Shenzhen, and examining Ukraine's scientific and engineering potential through a prospective synthetic-diamond case study, the book explores how reconstruction can generate specialised capabilities and durable international relationships. It then develops the concept of deterrence by embeddedness: the possibility that distributed economic, technological, scientific and infrastructural interests may raise the external costs of renewed aggression. This mechanism is conditional and supplementary; it cannot substitute for military capability, alliances or formal security guarantees. The book concludes with a policy framework for selecting difficult-to-replace capabilities, building research-to-production systems, attracting embedded investment and sequencing institutional transformation. Its central proposition is that reconstruction can strengthen Ukrainian agency by creating capabilities, relationships and international stakes that make the country's stability consequential to a wider community of partners.

detail.abstract: I test whether a TSX Venture Exchange (TSXV) stock's trailing illiquidity predicts its forward return, using 1,127 companies from January 2016 to December 2024 and a 70/30 ticker holdout locked away before any result was computed. I measure illiquidity five different ways. Four of the five, the Amihud (2002) price-impact ratio, the share of no-trade days, share turnover, and dollar volume, agree: the least-liquid fifth of stocks beats the most-liquid fifth by roughly 25–65 percentage points over the following year, out of sample, monotonically across quintiles, and robust to a full battery of stress tests. The fifth measure, the Corwin-Schultz (2012) high-low spread estimator, points the opposite way. I show this is not a contradiction: on this exchange, the spread estimator is negatively correlated with the other four and behaves more like a volatility proxy than a trading-cost proxy. The activity-based result replicates out of sample but is very likely inflated by survivorship bias, the sample is limited to companies still listed today, and is concentrated in two speculative booms (2016 and 2020–2021) rather than showing a steady premium. A separate cost- and turnover-aware simulation shows the effect does not survive as an actual tradable strategy. The contribution is a disciplined, holdout-validated picture of how returns relate to illiquidity at the very bottom of the North American market, and a demonstration that the answer depends on which illiquidity measure is used.

publicationDetails.detailsText: NHH Dept. of Business and Management Science Discussion Paper No. 2026/11

detail.abstract: Europe's move toward renewable energy has sped up as the need to cut emissions has become closely linked with the need to secure energy supply. The EU's Fit for 55 package proposed a 40% renewable energy target for 2030 [16]. The REPowerEU plan later raised the ambition to 45% in May 2022 in response to the need to reduce dependence on Russian fossil fuels [17]. Besides the significant contribution of renewable energies to the generation mix, they have created a dichotomy in electricity prices. An abundance of renewables can create extremely low prices and high volatility. On the other hand, their absence or insufficiency turns the gas-fired units or some fossil fuels on, which can create extremely high power prices. This phenomenon, in combination with geopolitical factors, has generated a binary fat-tailed distribution in electricity prices, which motivated us to study it more closely. Therefore, in this paper, we analyse the determinants of extreme electricity prices by modelling the conditional tail index. Additionally, we extend the analysis by [18] to a more recent sample period. We show that observable market conditions, such as TTF prices, load, and renewable generation in Germany and Italy from 2018 to 2023, affect the heaviness of the price distribution tail, a dimension of risk that is not captured by standard approaches such as quantile regression.

detail.abstract: This paper examines a structural limitation in signature-based spyware detection. The dominant model compares observable artifacts against a curated list of known indicators of compromise. A match proves that a known thing was present. The absence of a match is compatible with two very different situations: nothing is wrong, or something is wrong that nobody has yet described. The delay between an attack's first use and its first published indicator is exactly the period in which signature-based detection reports nothing on an infected device. This paper argues that the correct unit of analysis is not the signature, and not the vulnerability, but the trust assumption the system was built on. When the assumption fails, the entire class of attacks that exploit it is enabled. The paper examines eight attack vectors in order of sophistication, zero-click exploit chains, messaging and app-specific chains, baseband and signalling attacks, kernel-level persistence, cloud-side compromise, living-off-the-land abuse, supply chain, and physical access, identifying for each the trust assumption that fails. It then explains why signature-based detection cannot close the resulting gaps and proposes a four-layer framework for what remains observable from a device the user controls. It states plainly what device-side detection cannot do. The paper does not propose a solution to the hardest problems; it identifies them and states their limits. Its credibility depends on this honesty.

detail.abstract: Grammatical consistency patterns in child-directed speech are typically analysed pooled across caregiver and child utterances, a choice that leaves open a basic question about mechanism: is a given pattern something caregivers do to children, actively shaping the input, or is it a property of the shared communicative register that both members of the dyad participate in equally? This paper answers that question directly for a specific, previously established grammatical pattern, that copula-governed word-class slots are more categorially consistent than preposition-governed slots, by splitting the Manchester and Providence CHILDES corpora by speaker role before re-analysis. A broader pattern, that relator-governed slots generally are more consistent than noun-or verb-governed slots, is significant in maternal speech (t = 2.73, p = .006) but not in the child's own speech (t = 1.31, p = .19), consistent with an account in which caregivers actively shape this broader pattern. The copula-specific contrast tells a different story: it is significant independently in both speakers (mother: t = 6.41, p < .0001; child: t = 4.63, p < .0001), ruling out a purely caregiver-driven account for this specific, more robust pattern. Children's own copula-governed speech carries the same grammatical signature their mothers' speech does, at high significance, on their own utterances.

detail.abstract: This paper is the third in a series that began with An Ideal Society, which argued that a fair, just, and prosperous society must channel human nature, the drive for gain, status, and power, rather than suppress it, and set out four pillars for doing so: collective channeling of power and gain, equality of opportunity, equality of dignity, and civilizationally-grounded liberty. Architecture of Civic Counteraction applied that framework to citizen-side accountability of power-holders. This paper applies it to the organization itself. It surveys five existing alternatives to the standard shareholder-first firm, cooperatives, employee ownership, B Corp certification, German codetermination, and steward ownership, and finds that each solves for one dimension (ownership, voice, or a values commitment) while leaving untouched the more basic question of how people are placed into roles. It proposes a mechanism built on three reinforcing outcomes: opportunity distributed by demonstrated ability, organizational efficiency from correct placement, and a culture of dignity and belonging that itself improves performance. It argues that technology now available makes a continuous, longitudinal record of demonstrated ability practical in a way it never was when older models were designed, and it tests that claim against four organizations, Bridgewater Associates, Google, Netflix, and Valve, that already implement pieces of it, extracting a documented failure mode from each. It then states, without euphemism, which risks this design solves, which it manages without eliminating, and which remain open. The paper closes by weighing these benefits honestly against the risks that remain open, and by offering, grounded in that honesty rather than in spite of it, a vision of what life inside this organization could feel like, together with a call to the founders, managers, and organizational designers who have the power to build it.

detail.abstract: Well-timed and precise predictive quality control is gaining significant importance in the smart manufacturing and Industry 4.0 environment, where manufacturers need faster, more precise, and continuous ways to detect deviations in the processes and to communicate quality of the products (Çınar et al., 2020; Md. et al., 2022). This trend has promoted the end of traditional inspection and the adoption of machine-learning-based inspection methods that facilitate quality prediction, monitoring processes, classification, and automatic detection of defects (Tercan and Meisen, 2022; Galindo-Salcedo et al., 2022). The paper discusses the potential of machine learning to detect quality deviation and provide this information before it turns into a major manufacturing error, focusing on predictive quality models, manufacturing quality data, machine-learning algorithms, and defect detection strategies (Abualsauod, 2023; Bharot et al., 2024). The criteria of the analysis are the predictive accuracy, early detecting defects, constant monitoring in the process, data quality and operational efficiency. The results suggest that the machine-learning-driven quality control has the potential to enhance the ability to identify abnormal conditions of the process timely and make more proactive manufacturing decisions. But it works only with the help of good figures, real-time sensing, connection with the production processes and proper human control. Thus, predictive quality control can be perceived as an inherent manufacturing ability but not an algorithm itself (Franko and Varga, 2021; Awujoola et al., 2024).

detail.title: Dynamics of Electricity Price Spreads in MISO and Manitoba Hydro: Evidence from Structural Breaks and ARMAX-GARCH Models

publicationDetails.detailsText: NHH Dept. of Business and Management Science Discussion Paper No. 2026/12
publicationDetails.journalName: Norwegian School of Economics, Department of Business & Management Science Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: In this paper, we examine the impact on price spreads in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) wholesale electricity market due to a 2015 rule change that allowed bi-directional trade between the MISO and the neighboring Manitoba Hydro balancing area. We employ an ARMAX-GARCH model to measure the impact of this rule change on price spreads between the day-ahead and real-time market prices (DART price spreads) throughout the MISO market footprint. After controlling for extreme weather during the 2014 Polar Vortex and fluctuations in real-time generation quantities, we find that average DART price spreads decreased in both the northern region of the MISO (MISO North) and Manitoba Hydro after the implementation of the 2015 rule change. This result provides evidence that this rule change led to improved market alignment between MISO North and the Manitoba Hydro balancing area, possibly via improved utilization of joint network infrastructure.

title: Converting Constraints into Centrality: A Process Theory of Strategic Transmutation under Geopolitical Turbulence

detail.title: Converting Constraints into Centrality: A Process Theory of Strategic Transmutation under Geopolitical Turbulence

detail.abstract: How do firms strategically navigate geopolitical turbulence in globally interdependent industries? Strategy research assumes that persistent turbulence undermines competitive advantage, yet the global semiconductor industry presents a theoretically anomalous pattern: as geopolitical tensions intensified through export controls, technology restrictions, and industrial policy interventions, the strategic position of certain firms strengthened rather than eroded. Through a longitudinal archival case study of TSMC and the global semiconductor industry (2017-2024), drawing on annual reports, earnings call transcripts, and contemporaneous industry and policy sources, we identify three recurring mechanisms-reinforcing operational continuity, reconfiguring technological and commercial boundaries, and repositioning within geopolitical supply-chain structures-through which the firm translated geopolitical pressures into commercial and operational strategy. We conceptualize this process as strategic transmutation: a qualitative transformation in which geopolitical pressures enter the firm as political constraints and exit as commercial capabilities. The structural outcome is strategic centrality-a condition in which a firm becomes indispensable not because it controls critical resources, but because it converts geopolitical turbulence into reliable technological production that other actors cannot replicate. This study contributes to strategy research by challenging the assumption that turbulence primarily threatens advantage, by introducing strategic transmutation as a process concept that explains how the nature of external pressures is transformed through firm-level action, and by developing strategic centrality as a structural concept specifying how firms become indispensable through the cumulative processing of geopolitical turbulence. By introducing strategic transmutation and strategic centrality, this study provides a processual explanation for how geopolitical turbulence can be qualitatively transformed-not merely absorbed or adapted to-through firm-level strategic action.

title: The Two-Thirds Denominator in Philippine Impeachment

detail.title: The Two-Thirds Denominator in Philippine Impeachment

declarations.ethicsApproval: Because this is documentary and legal-constitutional research with no human participants, interviews, experiments, or identifiable personal data collection, you may enter: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it is based exclusively on publicly available legal, constitutional, institutional, and documentary sources and did not involve human participants, interviews, experiments, or collection of private personal data.

detail.abstract: Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Philippine Constitution provides that no person may be convicted in an impeachment trial without the concurrence of "two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate." The apparent simplicity of that command conceals a difficult denominator problem when one or more senators remain legally in office but are detained, medically absent, beyond the Senate's coercive reach, in hiding, voluntarily inhibited, unsworn as senator-judges, or otherwise unable or arguably unqualified to participate in the final judgment. The controversy became concrete in September 2026 when the Senate impeachment court reconsidered an existing interpretation requiring 16 votes from a 24-member chamber. Retired Chief Justices Hilario Davide Jr., Artemio Panganiban, and Reynato Puno advanced approaches under which the operative base can change in specified circumstances, while retired Associate Justice Adolfo Azcuna defended a membership-centered reading under which sitting senators remain in the denominator unless membership itself ends. This paper does not decide the political merits of any impeachment case and does not assess the guilt, innocence, fitness, or electoral prospects of any official. It instead develops an outcome-invariant constitutional decision pathway for the denominator question. The pathway separates five concepts that are frequently collapsed: Senate membership, seat vacancy, legal capacity to perform senatorial functions, qualification to act as a senator-judge, and actual participation in the evidentiary record. It then requires an independent legal trigger before any person who remains a senator is excluded from the constitutional base. The paper argues analytically that the central danger is not a variable denominator as such, nor a fixed denominator as such, but result-oriented denominator engineering: changing the counting rule because of the anticipated direction of particular votes. The proposed framework therefore uses ex ante rule fixation, symmetry, status-specific findings, anti-sabotage safeguards, and a written record of reasons. It also explains why Avelino v. Cuenco, the 2001 treaty-vote episode, and participation-based theories are relevant but not automatically controlling. As of 19 September 2026, the Senate impeachment court had not finally resolved the dispute; oral argument was scheduled for 23 September 2026.

detail.abstract: The study, examined the uses of the major resources over which conflicts arise within floodplain, and explained how competing claims on land, water, pasture, and fishery resources translated into recurrent tension among resource-user groups. It has achieved the aim through a mixed method where 384 samples were analysed in survey, 28 participants in FGD and twelve in KII. The findings were major resource-use patterns identified arable land as the primary contested resource, and is used mainly for farming. Fishing resource vandalism was the most prevalent, while grazing on cultivated land, expanding farm sizes, and fishing and sailing within private farm boundaries drove most tensions and disputes. People perceived resources as abundant, though scarcity linked to high population density arose when demand exceeded supply, with availability peaking between September and December amid a broader shift reflecting diminishing resources, population pressure, and socio-economic change. Land use and land cover data traced this trajectory: 1995 showed minimal human interference, 2005 marked modest land conversion, and by 2024 forest loss and cropland expansion had intensified. Resource competition was highest from September to December, it was minimal between 1995 and 1999, then intensified from January to April, with lower population size correlating with reduced use and population growth driving irregular, unsustainable resource use. Boundary disputes were the predominant and severe conflict type, confirming that resources in the study area are unevenly distributed. The study recommends seasonal, adaptive governance, advocates for multidimensional strategy to include; sustainable resource development, capacity building for stakeholders, temporal and targeted conflict resolution, environmental conservation and user education.

detail.abstract: Although the strategic management literature offers numerous frameworks for evaluating strategic alternatives, less attention has been paid to the methodology integrating these frameworks into an effective planning process. This paper presents a practice-based strategic planning methodology for SMEs, developed and iteratively refined through application in approximately 25 SME engagements over more than two decades, and grounded in the strategic management literature. The methodology is organized as a seven-stage process, governed by explicit decision points, that integrates management preparation, organizational readiness, and strategic communication into a coherent framework for developing and executing strategy. The paper argues that effective strategic planning depends on a disciplined methodology combining managerial judgment, objective evidence, and facilitated participation. Its application is illustrated through nine documented case engagements spanning diverse industries. As a practice-based contribution grounded in sustained field application, the paper offers a structured methodology to assist leaders, facilitators, and consultants in strategic planning and implementation.

detail.abstract: Research on strategizing and organizing as practice (SOAP) has illuminated how strategy work unfolds in meetings, workshops, and routines, but it has rarely examined how leaders' public disclosures shape long-term trajectories. This study conceptualizes leaders' strategic disclosures (LSDs)-annual reports, shareholder letters, and sustainability statements-as disclosure-as-practice. Drawing on two decades of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) disclosures, we trace how leadership narratives are reiterated, reframed, and hybridised into governance instruments such as PDKs, committees, CAPEX rules, and external certifications. Multi-level coding and temporal bracketing reveal distinct pathways: capability-related disclosures sediment through reiteration, disruption-related disclosures accelerate institutionalisation through reframing, and supply-chain disclosures embed hybrid forms that combine rhetorical assurances with boundary-spanning rules.The study contributes in three ways. First, it extends SOAP by repositioning disclosure as a constitutive practice linking strategizing and organising through recursive cycles of narration, instrumentation, and auditing. Second, it enriches institutional theory by showing how LSDs translate geopolitical and politico-economic shocks-from the global financial crisis and U.S.-China trade tensions to sustainability standards such as RE100 and ISSB-into firm-level routines, compressing institutionalisation cycles under volatility. Third, it advances global supply-chain governance by demonstrating how disclosures orchestrate legitimacy across regulators, customers, and investors, codifying standards and metrics as infrastructures of coordination.Contextualising the case of TSMC in Taiwan further illustrates how, in small and high-risk economies, disclosures are not optional communications but existential practices. In East Asian cultural settings, where public words are normatively expected to be honoured (yan chu bi xing, 言出 必行), disclosures carry binding authority, helping explain why decoupling was rare in our findings. Overall, the study reconceptualises leaders’ disclosures as catalytic practices of strategy, showing how they crystallise capabilities, accelerate institutionalisation under shocks, and orchestrate governance across global supply chains. It also provides methodological guidance for treating corporate texts as practice traces in longitudinal SAP research.

detail.abstract: Cambodia's digital media sector has experienced substantial transformation alongside the expansion of internet connectivity, social media, e-commerce, digital payments, and technology-enabled business practices. This changing environment creates strategic challenges for locally established digital enterprises seeking to sustain growth while responding to technological disruption, workforce capability constraints, evolving consumer behaviour, regulatory requirements, and competition from global digital platforms. This study examines how transformational leadership contributes to strategic innovation and organizational adaptability within Cambodia's emerging digital media sector, drawing on the organizational experience of BizKhmer Digital Media between 2020 and 2025. Developed from research undertaken as part of a PhD by Portfolio, the study adopts an organizational casebased approach integrating portfolio evidence, organizational experience, and secondary academic, industry, and policy sources. Transformational leadership provides the principal theoretical lens, complemented by strategic-management perspectives concerning organizational capabilities, continuous improvement, competitive positioning, and adaptation. The analysis focuses particularly on leadership practices related to employee empowerment, delegation, workforce development, knowledge transfer, technology adoption, and strategic responses to changes in Cambodia's digital business environment. The analysis indicates that transformational leadership within the organizational case is closely connected with efforts to strengthen employee participation, continuous learning, digital capability development, and organizational adaptation. The study further highlights the importance of contextualizing leadership practices within Cambodia's cultural, institutional, and market environment, particularly where interpersonal relationships, trust, workforce capabilities, regulatory conditions, and rapidly changing digital technologies influence strategic decision-making. The article proposes an integrative framework connecting transformational leadership, employee empowerment and knowledge development, digital capability, and strategic innovation and organizational adaptability. It contributes a context-sensitive perspective to the study of leadership and digital transformation in an emerging economy while providing practical implications for digital-media entrepreneurs and organizational leaders operating in Cambodia and comparable developing-market environments.

detail.abstract: This article argues that the interpretation of constitutional article 54 adopted by the Superior Chamber of the Electoral Tribunal of the Federal Judiciary in the file c which applies overrepresentation limits to political parties individually and not to coalitions as a unit-is systematically inconsistent with the purpose of the provision, contrary to the jurisprudence thesis P./J. 70/98 of the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation, and produces democratically unacceptable effects by allowing a coalition to obtain, with 54.72% of the vote, 72.8% of the seats in the Chamber of Deputies, equivalent to an overrepresentation of approximately 18 percentage points. It is argued that a systematic and functional interpretation of article 54-consistent with the principles of democratic pluralism of articles 40 and 41 of the Constitution-required applying the overrepresentation limits to the coalition as a political unit, and that this correction did not require constitutional reform but a different interpretive decision by the competent body. Furthermore, two reform proposals are formulated: the first, to constitutional article 54, to explicitly extend the overrepresentation limits to coalitions as a unit; the second, to article 135, to introduce an aggravated constitutional reform procedure applicable to matters of special institutional transcendence.

detail.abstract: Veterans affairs policy has increasingly developed beyond traditional compensation-based approaches towards broader governance frameworks focused on wellbeing, social reintegration, participation, and longterm societal contribution. This transformation reflects a growing recognition that veterans support systems must address complex and interconnected needs throughout the post-service lifecycle. This article examines veterans affairs policy in Georgia through a comparative analysis of selected countries in Eastern Europe and the South Caucasus. Using a comparative case study methodology, institutional analysis, and document-based policy research, the study explores approaches to veterans policy development in Croatia, Serbia, Poland, Ukraine, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia. The analysis identifies several recurring governance themes across different national contexts, including institutional coordination, comprehensive rehabilitation, social and economic reintegration, veterans’ participation, accessibility of services, and outcome-oriented evaluation. Based on these comparative lessons, the article develops the concept of a National Veterans Ecosystem as an analytical governance framework for understanding and strengthening modern veterans policy systems. Using Georgia as the primary case study, the article examines how veterans policy modernization may be approached through coordinated governance rather than isolated institutional interventions. The proposed framework emphasizes the interaction of government institutions, healthcare providers, veterans organizations, educational and employment actors, research institutions, and international partners, supported by service navigation mechanisms and evidence-based evaluation. The article further explores the transition from welfare-oriented support towards wellbeing-oriented approaches, including the relevance of the Welfare to Wellbeing© perspective and the conceptual foundations of the Georgian Veterans Social Return Index (GVSRI) as a potential framework for assessing broader policy outcomes. The study contributes to comparative veterans policy research by demonstrating how international experience can inform context-sensitive governance approaches in post-conflict and transitional societies. Rather than proposing a universal model, the article presents Georgia as a case through which broader lessons on veterans policy modernization can be examined.

detail.abstract:
Every year, thousands of students sit down to find a research question and are told to look for a gap. The advice is executable, defensible, and mostly useless.

A gap is a fact about a literature, not about the world: an absence of papers, and most things go unstudied for excellent reasons. The gap is a muse with a literature review attached – something you can call out to for three years while filing all your paperwork on time.

This paper offers the alternative. Significant research questions are not invented and not granted. They are found, in a small number of predictable places, by people who know what to look for. It sets out where to look – four forms an anomaly takes; why good questions stay hidden – three recurring mistakes (false homogeneity, false opposition, false certainty) that keep anomalies unsolved long after they are visible; and what to do once you have one – two questions and five moves that turn an anomaly into a research question. Six worked examples from management and innovation research, three weak questions repaired on the page, a test for telling a real anomaly from a gap in your own reading, and a section for readers with a graduation clock running make it usable the day you read it.

Written for MSc and PhD students, their supervisors, and any researcher looking for a question worth years of work. Forty minutes, straight through. You should finish able to write one sentence beginning "What bothers me is…" and know what to do with it.

Nothing is coming. Go and look.

detail.abstract: We develop an analytical model featuring two public signals on a terminal payoff: an early public signal (e.g., a social-media signal or an alternative-data signal) and a later official disclosure. Both signals arrive before a …nal payo¤ in an incomplete market characterized by investors with heterogeneous prior precisions. We demonstrate that error correlation across these public signals is a first-order driver of speculative surplus, price variance, and trading volume. This correlation determines the incremental informational value of the official disclosure relative to the early public signal, and the incremental precision is U-shaped in the error correlation. Moreover, a precision paradox might exist in the modern Big Data era in which early public signals (e.g., an aggregate alternative-data signal) can be more precise than official disclosure: increasing the official signal's precision under high error correlation can paradoxically reduce its marginal value. We investigate information design by studying how a regulator trades o¤ investors' welfare (speculative surplus) against market stability (price variance). We discuss how to implement an optimal information design and show that changing the error correlation via, e.g., changes in disclosure timing, verification protocols, or measurement methodology, can be cheaper and more effective than simply increasing the official signal precision.

detail.abstract: SDG monitoring faces a persistent data-policy disconnect: indicators measure outcomes but rarely trace the policies, budgets, and institutions shaping them. This limits accountability and weakens evidence-based learning. We introduce Policy-Metadata Coherence (PMC), a framework that embeds policy linkages as structured metadata within national statistical systems, aligned with SDMX/GSIM standards and ISO 9001 quality-management principles. PMC operates through three stages-ex-ante policy analysis, metadata structuring, and ex-post coherence diagnostics-supported by AI-assisted linkage discovery using Small Sovereign Language Models (SLMs). The framework is demonstrated through an SDG 6.1 (safe drinking water) simulation calculating eight coherence indicators (metadata completeness, horizontal and vertical alignment, contradiction frequency). A 90-day pilot protocol illustrates how National Statistical Offices can implement PMC within 1-5 years, transforming their role from data compilers to coherence-assurance authorities. By operationalizing SDG 17.14 (policy coherence) and SDG 17.18 (statistical capacity), PMC provides governments with a practical pathway to evidence-based, quality-assured and coherent SDG governance. Note on methodology: This paper presents a deployment-ready framework with illustrative scenarios demonstrating PMC's application.

title: Do Renters In Deprived Neighbourhoods Pay More? Rental Yields And The Poverty Penalty: Evidence From England And Wales
affiliations: and London School of Economics

detail.title: Do Renters In Deprived Neighbourhoods Pay More? Rental Yields And The Poverty Penalty: Evidence From England And Wales

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known financial or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding has been received for this research.

detail.abstract: This article examines whether renters in deprived neighbourhoods face a poverty penalty in private rental markets. Using a new dwelling-level dataset, linked to granular deprivation data across more than 35,000 neighbourhoods in England and Wales, we estimate the relationship between rental yields-measured as annual rent as a share of property values-and neighbourhood deprivation. We reveal that rental yields are significantly higher in deprived neighbourhoods; tenants in these areas pay more relative to the value of the homes they occupy. To investigate the mechanisms behind this finding, we control for landlord risk factors and capital gains and find that they are associated with yields in theoretically expected directions, but the deprivation-yield gradient persists even after accounting for these factors. We further show that yields are higher where access to social housing is scarce. Taken together, our analysis provides new evidence for a poverty penalty in private rental markets.

title: Function over Fidelity: Coral Reefs and The Future of Conservation Law
affiliations: , University of Chicago - Law School, Northeastern University (USA), University of Texas at Austin - Department of Integrative Biology and Miami University

detail.title: Function over Fidelity: Coral Reefs and The Future of Conservation Law

declarations.declarationOfInterest: n/a
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract:
Coral reefs are among the first ecosystems to cross a major climate-induced threshold soon to be imposed on many more habitats—when ecological function cannot be maintained by remaining fully faithful to recent historical state. In Florida, two of the keystone species—elkhorn and staghorn coral—that built shallow reef structures are now functionally extinct in the wild, and restoration of reefs to historical baselines is no longer feasible. Yet the international, federal, and state laws that govern coral conservation embed a powerful preference for historical fidelity and native composition, discouraging or prohibiting forward-looking interventions—from assisted gene flow to the introduction of non-native ecological replacements—that have better chances of preserving the reef’s ecological function.
Using Florida’s Coral Reef as a frontline case study, this Article argues that unconditional fidelity to historical and “natural” baselines is no longer a defensible default for conservation law. It surveys the full spectrum of possible interventions and the scientific, legal, and ethical tradeoffs each entails, and it contends that the law should move from categorical native/non-native prohibitions toward a structured, risk-assessment-based framework—one that authorizes interventions in reversible stages, invites meaningful public and cross-jurisdictional participation, and adapts as it learns. Coral reefs are the leading case, but the problem, and the framework we propose, extends across conservation law.

title: Fragmented by Design: Why Current AI Regulation Fails to Address Systemic Risk

detail.title: Fragmented by Design: Why Current AI Regulation Fails to Address Systemic Risk

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this paper, as the research involved purely desk-based comparative policy analysis and literature review, with no human participants, animal subjects, or private personal data utilised.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or non-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The governance of artificial intelligence has entered a phase of legislative acceleration. In the space of three years, the European Union enacted the world's first comprehensive AI regulation, the United States published a voluntary risk management framework, the G7 produced an international code of conduct, and more than seventy countries initiated national AI policy processes. Yet speed of production has not translated into depth of coverage. A systematic comparative analysis of eight major AI regulatory instruments - the EU AI Act (2024), NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (2023), ISO/IEC 42001:2023, OECD AI Principles (2019, revised 2023), G7 Hiroshima Process (2023), the UK's pro-innovation framework, China's Generative AI Interim Measures (2023), and India's emerging MeitY policy framework, reveals three structural failures that no existing instrument resolves.

First, accountability diffusion: when AI systems cause harm, no framework provides an unambiguous, enforceable chain of liability from developer through deployer to user. Second, dynamic risk invisibility: risk classification is performed at the point of deployment, while AI systems evolve, fine-tune, and drift post-launch without any binding obligation to re-assess. Third, a cross-border enforcement vacuum: AI systems are global; governance instruments are jurisdictional. No binding multilateral enforcement mechanism exists, and soft coordination frameworks such as the OECD Principles and G7 commitments produce normative alignment without operative effect.

This paper argues that these three gaps are not incidental oversights correctable through incremental amendment. They are architectural features of how AI governance has been designed, jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction, framework-by-framework, in the absence of a shared foundational theory of AI liability, risk continuity, or international enforcement. The paper draws on a comparative matrix applied to all eight instruments, identifies four secondary gaps that compound the foundational failures, and proposes a tiered set of policy recommendations spanning immediate (0–2 year), medium-term (2–5 year), and long-term (5+ year) horizons. The central long-term proposal is the establishment of a global AI governance body with narrow but binding enforcement authority, modelled on the institutional architecture of FATF for financial crime and the IAEA for nuclear safety, precedents that demonstrate that technically complex, cross-border risk can be governed multilaterally when political will exists.

title: The Making of China's Industrial Base: Personal Liability and the Laolai Paradox

detail.title: The Making of China's Industrial Base: Personal Liability and the Laolai Paradox

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
China’s industrial strength is visible not only in the accumulation of capital, large firms, infrastructure, and manufacturing capacity, but also in the extraordinary density of independent production organizers. Numerous small firms can constitute large-scale production when they perform specialized tasks, transact repeatedly, and remain connected through industrial networks. This paper asks a narrower institutional question within that larger phenomenon: how can people who possess technical knowledge, business experience, and the capacity to organize production, but not the wealth required to own all necessary inputs, become independent producers?

Existing research on Chinese industrial clusters shows how specialization, trade credit, informal finance, local public goods, and market proximity can reduce entry barriers. A residual question concerns the individual entrant: how are productive resources connected to a person who has not yet accumulated sufficient wealth? This paper proposes, but does not yet empirically establish, that personal guarantees may complement trade credit, leasing, equipment installments, customer advances, and other financing arrangements. Conditional on credible orders and viable production, a personal commitment may allow creditors to consider not only current assets and expected enterprise cash flow but also a legally bounded obligation undertaken by the operator.

The proposed mechanism operates across two time horizons. Before production, a credible personal commitment may improve access to resources for some asset-poor operators. After failure, a separately assumed guarantee may, within applicable legal limits, continue to affect the individual’s subsequently acquired assets and income even after the enterprise has ceased operating. The productive life of a firm and the economic life of its owner need not end at the same time. A liability most visible after failure may therefore have had an ex ante credit function before production began.

Laolai is a pejorative colloquial label, not a unified legal category. Business failure, ordinary insolvency, personal-guarantee liability, and formal designation as a dishonest judgment debtor are not interchangeable. The term is used only as an observational reversal: it directs attention from the visible failure end of a credit relationship back toward the conditions that may have enabled industrial entry. The ultimate object of explanation is not debt default, but the formation, connection, and reproduction of organizers of industrial production.

title: Dali or Dall-E? The Value of Human Authorship in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology - Scheller College of Business and Emory University - Goizueta Business School

detail.title: Dali or Dall-E? The Value of Human Authorship in the Age of Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest to report.
