detail.abstract: Regulators, content platforms, and academic journals increasingly require creators to disclose the use of artificial intelligence (AI), yet how audiences respond is unmeasured. In an incentivized virtual-reality art market, 205 participants valued identical paintings under randomly assigned attributions; AI attribution reduced willingness to pay by 22.6% of the reference price. In 132,883 reviews on an online fiction platform, AI-attributed books were both less likely to be chosen to be read and were rated 1.6% lower. The penalty is concentrated in private valuations, not in social expectations; it declines with a consumer’s cumulative exposure to labeled work; and it is largest for creators without an established reputation. AI disclosure therefore changes what consumers will pay for identical work, and the design of the rule determines which creators incur the loss.

title: Revealing Urban Mobility Inertia of Crowd Dispersal After Large-Scale Events
affiliations: Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology, Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics, Zhejiang University, Zhejiang University, The University of Hong Kong, Zhejiang University, Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University - Department of Civil Engineering, AutoNavi Software Co., Ltd., Amap Alibaba Group, Tsinghua University and Beijing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Revealing Urban Mobility Inertia of Crowd Dispersal After Large-Scale Events
detail.abstract: Large concerts, sports matches, and festivals can create acute demand shocks by releasing dense crowds into urban transport systems within minutes, turning ordinary streets and transit stations into temporary bottlenecks. Yet it remains unclear whether collective mobility reorganizes under such shocks or remains constrained by everyday mobility structure. The urban mobility inertia refers to the persistence of aggregate origin–destination structures when sudden, localized demand is introduced into the urban transport system. Using 45.84 billion anonymized mobility records from 408 planned special events across 32 Chinese cities, we show that post-event dispersal remains highly anchored to everyday mobility structure, with grid-level arrivals predictable from baseline traffic and static venue features (R2 = 0.883). The alignment between event dispersal and baseline flows follows a power law: prediction error decays sharply with baseline flow and saturates at high-baseline venues, where crowds are absorbed through existing transport corridors. Metro and bus systems channel demand into spatially concentrated and stable flows, whereas flexible private modes generate dispersed and unstable hotspots. What-if modal-shift simulations reveal a concentration–dispersion trade-off in which the same transit-first guidance can reduce, relocate, or intensify congestion, depending on venue centrality, transit density, and expressway access. These findings caution against blanket transit-first guidance and instead support venue-specific modal coordination calibrated to local transport context.

detail.abstract:
Background: Plasma circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) profiling can identify actionable alterations, but treatment delivery also depends on regulatory approval, reimbursement, and access. Evidence linking molecular actionability to delivered treatment remains limited.

Methods: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study at the National Cancer Center, Republic of Korea, we included 393 adults with advanced solid tumours who underwent plasma ctDNA testing in 2019–24. We distinguished report-level actionability from tumour-type-matched standard actionability. In the matched-standard lung subgroup, we compared reimbursed-option availability at testing with the route of treatment delivery using date-indexed approval and reimbursement records.

Findings: Report-level actionable findings occurred in 233 (59.3%) of 393 patients, and tumour-type-matched standard actionability occurred in 116 (29.5%), of whom 82 (70.7%) received treatment after the report. In the lung matched-standard cohort (n=114), 80 (70.2%) received post-report treatment through reimbursed on-label (31), non-standard access (43), or clinical trial (6) routes; 15 had received treatment only before the report. A reimbursed on-label option existed at testing for 62 of 80 post-report recipients, of whom 31 used it. Among 19 patients without matched therapy recorded locally, barriers included clinical or access factors, non-reimbursement, indication mismatch, or no approved agent.

Interpretation: Among treated lung cancer patients with matched-standard findings, a nationally reimbursed on-label option was often available, although therapy was delivered through another route. Separating tumour-specific matching, contemporaneous reimbursement, and the realised treatment route clarifies implementation beyond molecular detection.

title: Changing the Objective Is Not the Same as Changing What the Organization Decides From

detail.title: Changing the Objective Is Not the Same as Changing What the Organization Decides From
detail.abstract: Senior leaders increasingly delegate not only tasks but objective interpretation and execution to agentic AI systems. This creates a managerial condition that deserves attention before it is encountered: an organization can become highly reliable at executing its current objective while becoming slower and less able to replace that objective when leadership changes direction. The reason is not machine resistance, misalignment or malfunction. It is that an organizational objective is operative only where it functions as the premise components actually decide from — and after a formal change, many components continue deciding from the superseded objective, filtering, deprioritizing and re-proposing around the very actions the new direction requires. Competent architecture already protects the act of authorization; it does not deliver propagation or preserve execution capacity during transition. Using an illustrative owner-driven closure scenario, this article distinguishes inert technical residue, which is a migration task, from residual operative premises, which are a leadership problem. It offers executives a diagnostic, observable warning signs, and design guidance for building revisability alongside execution reliability.

detail.abstract: The double materiality requirement (DMR) is central to the information disclosure regime created by the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). However, prior research suggests that assessing materiality negatively impacted on the relevance and accuracy of information disclosures. Whether the DMR will produce similar effects on the quality of sustainability-related disclosures is unclear. Using content analysis of policy documents, this article identifies and discusses the effects of the DMR on reporting quality as perceived by stakeholders during the ESRS rule-making process. Relative to a fully prescriptive regime, the DMR offers greater flexibility to make reporting decisions. Nevertheless, flexibility gains are counteracted by problems of implementation, standardisation and trustworthiness. Since the DMR is principles-based and enables the exercise of managerial discretion, mechanisms to monitor discretion are proposed to mitigate negative effects on reporting quality, including audit committees, external assurance, as well as supervisory and enforcement actions.

title: Crystal Clear: The Solutions for Clean, Running Water

detail.abstract:
• Privatised water and regulation have failed so badly that England pays among the highest bills in Europe, yet nearly every river is illegally polluted, taps run dry and a trillion litres of water is leaked each year, wasting over a hundred times more water than all the hosepipe bans added together would save.
• Shareholders have taken over £85.2 billion in dividends, and creditors more in interest, since privatisation in 1989, evaporating UK investment, shipping capital overseas, and leaving billions of pounds in sewage treatment and pipe repair costs. These polluters should not be paid a penny more to run our water.
•    To bring water into public ownership the ratings agency, Moody’s estimated a one-off cost of £14.5 billion in 2019. By contrast, privatisation is costing up to £22.047 billion extra for bill payers from 2025 to 2030, or £176 a household a year, in returns on capital to shareholders and banks, as set by Ofwat’s price review.
•    This report estimates that in 2026, public ownership of failed water companies will cost closer to £0, using the special administration procedure. The higher the repair bills, the less that creditors or shareholders deserve under UK law, international law and our investment treaties. This applies to Thames Water, South East Water, and probably Anglian, Southern, South West, Yorkshire Water and Welsh Water. Creditors will likely sue, but they have no reasonable prospect of success.
• For Northumbrian, Severn Trent, United Utilities and Wessex, public ownership through an Act is estimated to save households up to £1.2 billion after three years, with an initial investment of £12 billion. This is based on market capitalisations, limited repair cost information and the cardinal “polluter pays” principle. The regulator should make companies disclose the repair costs to fulfil the key statutory duties to treat sewage twice and fix leaks.
• To take the handbrake off public investment, the Government should bring our accounting practice up to international and European standards, by separating public corporation borrowing from the national debt. This would drive investment growth in every postcode for water, plus energy, housing and transport.

title: Unsupervised Detection of Institutional Pinning Traps: A Hierarchical Hidden Markov Model Approach to Market Microstructure
affiliations: Independent Researcher and  Independent Quantitative Researcher

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the microstructural mechanics of asymmetric liquidity provision and institutional manipulation within retail-dominated cryptocurrency markets. We introduce a novel metric, the Asymmetric Absorption Threshold (KAT), to quantify the divergence between aggressive market volume and high-frequency price displacement. By deploying a Hierarchical Hidden Markov Model (HHMM) consisting of a 1-minute parent Gaussian HMM and a 1-second unsupervised child HMM-we systematically isolate synthetic institutional limit walls, defined here as continuous-time illusions. Analyzing a dataset of 30.7 million 1-second BTCUSDT intervals from 2020 to 2026, the unsupervised model identifies over 2.19 million discrete pinning traps clustered strictly within low-volatility accumulation regimes. A live out-of-sample metal test across 292 executions demonstrates that fading these illusory bid walls yields a statistically significant high-frequency edge, generating an exceptional 65.75% win probability, an average execution alpha of +0.004 basis points, and a net cumulative yield of +1.217 basis points at a 10-second forward window before decaying completely at 5 minutes. These findings confirm that retail momentum traders are systematically disadvantaged by static limit-order illusions.

detail.abstract: This expanded paper provides a comprehensive academic analysis of systemic corruption in Sudan under the thirty-year rule of President Omar al-Bashir and the National Congress Party (NCP) (1989–2019), and its catastrophic legacy through the civil war of 2023–2026. It identifies six interconnected pillars that sustained Sudan's violent kleptocracy: (1) state capture, (2) the militarized economic empire, (3) systematic plunder of natural resources, (4) politicized privatization and crony capitalism, (5) institutionalized impunity and governance collapse, and (6) international dimensions and the war economy. Beyond structural analysis, the paper offers detailed biographical criticism of ten key individuals—Abdel Basit Sabdarat, Ibrahim Ahmed Omar, Abdel Rahim Hamdi, Ibrahim Ghandour, Nafie Ali Nafie, Salah Gosh, Ali Osman Mohamed Taha, Bakri Hassan Saleh, Omar al-Bashir, and Hassan al-Turabi—who architected, legitimized, and enforced predatory policies. Drawing on investigative reports, judicial audits, humanitarian data, and international legal proceedings, and employing a qualitative framework of extractive institutions (Acemoglu & Robinson, 2012) and violent kleptocracy (de Waal, 2019; The Sentry, 2019), the paper argues that the failure to pursue individual accountability during the 2019–2023 transition directly contributed to the April 2023 outbreak of war between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The paper demonstrates how gold smuggling ($23–36.8 billion lost 2010–2024), militarized commercial networks, and the complete collapse of state services have created a self-sustaining war economy. It concludes that sustainable reconstruction requires both structural reforms and individualized transitional justice, with concrete policy recommendations for asset recovery and security sector reform.

detail.abstract: Implementation can change which alternatives remain executable, not only how strongly an actor prefers the chosen course. Decision Closure separates structural reachability-whether any admissible path to a specified alternative remains-from correction impedance-the burden of the least-cost admissible path, conditional on reachability. The framework is a decision-specific application of Symformism, a working philosophical research programme in which earlier organization can reshape later admissible transitions; the broader notion of informational impedance is narrowed here to correction impedance. Institutional constraints can therefore block correction even after failure is recognized, while finite burden becomes meaningful only inside the reachable subspace. The article derives falsifiable hypotheses about topology, reachability, and conditional burden, and places the synthetic construct diagnostics in Supplement S1 because they test recoverability of the formal architecture rather than real-world validity.

detail.abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources such as solar photovoltaic and wind power presents significant opportunities for reducing dependence on conventional fossil-fuel generation while creating new operational challenges for modern electrical power systems. The intermittent and uncertain nature of renewable generation can complicate power balancing, energy scheduling, storage coordination, demand management, and grid stability. This study examines the application of Intelligent Energy Management Systems (IEMS) for optimizing renewable-energy integration through coordinated management of generation, energy storage, electricity demand, and grid interaction. The study adopts a systematic synthesis and comparative analysis of relevant research on intelligent energy management, renewable-energy forecasting, optimization algorithms, demand response, energy-storage coordination, and smart-grid technologies. Key variables examined include renewable-energy utilization, storage coordination, demand-response performance, forecasting accuracy, energy cost, grid stability, and overall energy efficiency. The reviewed approaches indicate that intelligent optimization can support more effective coordination between variable renewable generation and electricity demand by using predictive information and adaptive control strategies. However, the effectiveness of individual approaches depends on system configuration, data quality, forecasting performance, optimization objectives, and operating conditions. The study concludes that IEMS can provide an important framework for improving renewable-energy integration when supported by reliable data, appropriate optimization techniques, and coordinated control. The findings have practical implications for smart grids, microgrids, buildings, and other distributed energy systems seeking more efficient and reliable renewable-energy utilization.

detail.abstract:
This study quantifies the week-to-week comovement between terminal congestion and network velocity at Union Pacific (UP) and BNSF Railway across 452 weeks of Surface Transportation Board EP 724 data (2018–2026). We develop a Dwell–Velocity Coupling Coefficient (β)—the elasticity of system train speed with respect to terminal dwell in weekly log-differences—and subject it to a rigorous verification framework including sub-measure designation auditing, era-split estimation, and event-level controls. Three primary findings emerge.


First, coupling differs sharply across carriers. Excluding a defective 2018 measurement regime, UP’s coupling during 2019–2021 is β = −0.139, versus −0.038 for BNSF. In the clean post-May-2021 era, the contrast is β = −0.219 versus −0.058, a difference that is formally significant in pooled interaction tests (*p* < 0.001). This four-carrier spectrum (spanning −0.06 to −0.38) survives calendar and volume controls. UP’s elevated coupling dates to 2019, contemporaneous with its workforce reductions and operating-model changes, though causal attribution is not identified.


Second, we document an undocumented, simultaneous designation change in both of UP’s EP 724 metrics in the week ending May 7, 2021, verified against archived STB records. The change is statistically silent in level, trend, and coupling, precluding direct cross-era comparability.


Third, we demonstrate that standard rolling-window break detection generates artifactual structural breaks from this data. While sequential tests date phantom breaks to January 2022 and April 2024, raw-data step tests reject these, and a placebo simulation reveals the procedure yields a 76% false-positive rate. Documented events (e.g., Winter Storm Elliott) register clearly, but the purported April 2024 industry shock leaves no footprint. We conclude with recommendations for EP 724 reporting integrity.

detail.abstract: Stock and bond investors treat different aspects of firm information as value-relevant, generating distinct mappings of text to returns ("dictionaries"). Comparing stock and bond responses to earnings calls, bondholders emphasize operations and downside risk (relative to growth and innovation). While consistent with asset payoff differences, dictionary differences follow the investor cohort and not the payoff structure. Among bonds that are de facto equities but priced by bondholders-junior debt for which firm value is less than senior debt face valuebond investors continue to interpret information through a creditor's lens. Information ignored by one dictionary but not the other generates price underreaction.

detail.abstract: While DLT-based monetary architectures effectively suppress ex-nihilo credit expansion, their real-world deployment is strictly governed by physical hardware, thermodynamic constraints, and energy-water dependencies. This paper formulates the physical layer blueprint for the International Integrated Clearing and Settlement System (IICSS). We model a three-tier sovereign hardware architecture separating central bank validators, auditor nodes, and participant gateways under a neutral dual-track model without unilateral authority vetoes. To resolve ZKP computational heat constraints, we formulate a thermodynamic liquid-cooling balance coupled with coastal seawater desalination units to eliminate inland freshwater depletion. Operational resilience is secured via autonomous power microgrids and a dual-route communication backbone combining encrypted subsea fiber-optic cables with automated satellite failovers. Financial amortization modeling confirms that total physical CapEx and OpEx are fully offset by removing traditional Nostro-Vostro correspondent banking friction.

detail.abstract: This paper is the second in a series following "Attribution Space: A Missing Concept in HSETheory." The first paper defined Attribution Space as the structural elasticity within whichindividuals can deflect responsibility for safety failures. This paper advances the argument byexamining: (1) the consequences of excessive Attribution Space, and (2) how datafication andAI structurally compress it. The paper first demonstrates that large Attribution Space produces measurable organizational dysfunctions: recurring safety violations, information overload that masks genuine risks, andresponsibility deflection that prevents systemic learning. Drawing on industry data and real-worldincident cases, it establishes that Attribution Space is not a theoretical abstraction but anoperational variable with tangible consequences. It then argues that datafication and AI constitute a structural compression mechanismoperatingthrough three pathways: granularization of information, elimination of temporal delays, andreduction of human judgment dependency. These pathways are validated through multi-context case evidence—from hospitality AI adoption, manufacturing sensor systems, and energy sector predictive maintenance—alongside industry adoption data. The paper further examines the paradoxes and risks of compression, including algorithmic bias, new forms of "algorithmic deflection," and confirmation fatigue, arguing that these phenomenaindicate the existence of a compression limit. This establishes the foundation for the third paper in the series, which will address the optimal elasticity range of Attribution Space through a springmodel. This paper does not argue for the elimination of Attribution Space, nor does it claimthat datafication and AI replace human decision-making. Rather, it posits that structural compressionis an emergent consequence of datafication and AI adoption, and that this compression—withits inherent limits—constitutes the foundational logic of HSE system evolution.

detail.abstract: Accurate treatment timing is essential for credible causal inference in policy evaluation, yet cannabis policy studies employ a variety of treatment definitions, including legislative enactment, policy effective dates, and retail implementation. Because legal authorization frequently precedes consumer access by months or years, these measures are not necessarily interchangeable for outcomes that depend on realized market access. This paper introduces a harmonized dataset of statutory policy effective dates and retail implementation dates for medical and adult-use cannabis programs across all 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia from 1996 through June 2026. Policy dates were compiled from enacted statutes, ballot initiatives, official regulatory documents, and publicly available records documenting the initiation of licensed retail sales. Medical cannabis programs exhibited substantially longer implementation delays than adult-use programs, with median delays of 30 and 13 months, respectively. By distinguishing statutory adoption from realized retail access, the dataset provides alternative measures of treatment timing and reduces potential treatment misclassification in empirical evaluations of cannabis policy. The accompanying source documentation promotes transparency, reproducibility, and comparability across future evaluations of cannabis legalization.

detail.abstract:
Technical competence in well intervention and stimulation operations is transmitted through on-the-job accompaniment: prolonged exposure of a junior professional to an experienced one under field conditions. The mechanism is formalized in most organizations in the sector — records exist, they are auditable, and the activity is certified as completed — but that record attests to the occurrence of transfer, not to its content or quality. It further depends on a condition that is no longer satisfied at the required scale: that experienced personnel remain active long enough to complete the transfer.

The problem has institutional recognition. The U.S. Department of Energy's 21st Century Energy Workforce Advisory Board explicitly recommends developing programs that capture the unwritten knowledge of workers in the oil and gas sector. The recommendation identifies the objective without specifying the mechanism.

An established framework exists for assessing competence by levels: Miller's pyramid (1990), which distinguishes knows, knows how, shows how, and does, assigning a distinct assessment instrument to each. That framework answers how to measure competence. It does not answer how to build it, how to allocate resources across levels, or how to keep content current. In 1990 the latter two were not design questions: every level depended on an in-person instructor, and allocation was trivial.

That premise no longer holds. Automated generation and localization of instructional content, and systematic processing of accumulated operational records, have turned two operations formerly bounded by human labor into operations of decreasing marginal cost. This turns the distribution of the expert resource and the maintenance of content into architectural decisions.

This paper proposes four extensions to Miller's framework: a resource allocation rule — content is digitizable when it can be verified against a known answer, and requires presence when it can only be verified against expert judgment; an observability-based instantiation rule determining which instrument corresponds to the demonstration level in each technical discipline; a recursive traversal of the full structure at each stage of the professional pathway; and a maintenance loop mediated by automated processing, coupling the organization's operational records to training content and resolving the dependence of the material's currency on the tenure of individuals.

The framework is illustrated through four instances: coiled tubing intervention, hydraulic stimulation, drilling fluids, and cementing.

detail.abstract: The increasing autonomy of artificial intelligence has intensified the "responsibility gap" and the debate over AI moral agency. Existing accounts commonly appeal to rational capacity, sentience, or functional performance, but these criteria do not fully explain either the motivational basis for taking norms as reasons or the conditions under which a subject can bear ultimate moral responsibility. Drawing on the framework developed in On Self-Good Desire, this paper argues that "self-good desire" (sishan yuqiu) is a motivationally necessary condition of full moral agency. It denotes an intrinsic, selfnurturing motivational structure through which a living subject maintains its existence, improves its condition, and pursues its development, unfolding into eleven root desires: self-preservation, self-care, self-enrichment, self-beautification, self-joy, self-compassion, self-reflection, self-confidence, selfstrengthening, self-respect, and freedom. "Life integrity" here does not reduce moral agency to a particular biological substrate; rather, it refers to an integrated organization of self-maintenance, felt value, diachronic identity, and self-concern. Self-good desire is not sufficient for full moral agency, which also requires normative understanding, behavioral control, and responsibility-bearing capacity. On this account, current AI systems can represent norms and simulate forms of moral reasoning, yet there is presently insufficient warrant to attribute to them endogenous needs, first-person experience, enduring self-concern, or genuinely self-generated stakes. They therefore should not be treated as full moral agents. When AI systems cause harm, ultimate moral responsibility should ordinarily remain with human and institutional actors and be allocated by reference to control, causal contribution, benefit, foreseeability, and duties of care. The paper also addresses objections concerning infants, animals, corporations, functionalism, biologism, and future artificial agents, while remaining conditionally open to future artificial systems that might develop functionally equivalent forms of endogenous concern.

detail.abstract:
Electoral independence depends on decisions made long before polling and on remedies that remain effective when the vote is cast. This article examines the appointment of Election Commissioners, intensive revision of electoral rolls, delayed local elections, municipal delimitation, professional pathways into the higher judiciary and public appointments after judicial retirement. It asks whether the distribution of powers across these processes gives the incumbent executive an advantage that existing safeguards fail adequately to check. The analysis combines constitutional doctrine with dated court records, official election figures and expressly attributed secondary data.

The evidence identifies concrete weaknesses. The 2023 appointment statute places the Prime Minister and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister on a three-member selection committee. Bihar's Special Intensive Revision was upheld in May 2026, subject to the judgment's safeguards and limits on citizenship enquiries. West Bengal's court-supervised verification and subsequent appeals expose the difficulty of providing individual hearings at electoral scale. Rajasthan's September 2026 urban polling occurred after the April and July dates specified in the High Court orders examined here. A three-city vote and ward comparison also warrants closer scrutiny of municipal boundaries, although it does not establish unlawful delimitation.

The argument concerns institutional dependence rather than an alleged agreement between judges and a political party. Bar elections do not elect constitutional-court judges, and professional affiliations require evidence independent of courtroom outcomes. Public appointments soon after judicial retirement raise questions about appearances and incentives; their timing alone cannot establish a bargain. The article proposes earlier roll adjudication, enforceable local-election preparation, disclosure of boundary decisions and appointment processes, and an office-specific cooling-off framework. It also identifies the constitutional and statutory changes those proposals would require.

detail.title: Dataset of benchmark evaluation metrics and calibration diagnostics for surgical wound infection risk classificationDataset of benchmark evaluation metrics and calibration diagnostics for surgical wound infection risk classification
detail.abstract: This article presents a benchmark evaluation dataset generated from systematic deep learning experiments on the SurgWound dataset, a publicly available collection of 686 surgeon-annotated wound images with infection risk and urgency level annotations. The evaluation data comprise per-class classification metrics (precision, recall, F1-score), calibration diagnostics (expected calibration error, calibration slope, and intercept), and selective prediction performance across multiple coverage thresholds. Experiments were conducted using four convolutional neural network backbones (EfficientNet-B0, EfficientNet-B3, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121) under two classification paradigms (softmax and evidential deep learning), each evaluated over three independent random seeds, yielding 24 experimental runs for infection risk assessment and 6 runs for urgency level classification. The dataset documents both macro-averaged and weighted-averaged F1-scores for each configuration, exposing a persistent 0.24-0.29 gap between these two metrics that is consistent across all architectures. All raw metric tables, calibration diagnostics, and evaluation code are deposited in a public GitHub repository and archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22651321). These data enable researchers to benchmark new models against established baselines, reproduce the evaluation protocol, and investigate metric-reporting practices in class-imbalanced medical image classification tasks.

detail.abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is a system of ocean currents that plays a key role in regulating global climate, including moderating temperatures in Europe and the North Atlantic. Its potential collapse due to global warming is widely considered one of the more likely climate tipping points. This paper examines the economic implications of such a collapse using a dynamic spatially integrated assessment model (S-IAM) of the world economy. Scandinavia and parts of Russia are predicted to experience significant losses in GDP and welfare, while southern Europe, northern Africa, and Brazil benefit from slightly colder temperatures. S-IAMs generally predict that global warming is especially harmful to low-income regions, but an AMOC collapse could mitigate some of these negative impacts in parts of the developing world while instead harming some of the more advanced economies. This lowers spatial inequality, but global welfare drops by 1.9% by 2200 under an intermediate-emissions scenario.

detail.abstract: This research report examines the statewide economic contribution of the annual operations of Maine’s arts and cultural nonprofit organizations. Economic contribution is measured in terms of output, employment, and labor income, including the direct activity of the nonprofit organizations themselves and the additional economic activity supported through business-to-business purchases and household spending by workers. Using data from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) master file of tax-exempt organizations, we identified 1,424 arts and cultural nonprofit organizations in Maine. The state ranks third—behind the District of Columbia and Vermont—in the number of arts and cultural nonprofits per 100,000 residents. Arts and cultural nonprofits in Maine are estimated to directly account for approximately $322 million in annual output, 5,650 jobs, and $125 million in employee compensation. After accounting for the multiplier effects generated through purchases from Maine suppliers and household spending, the annual statewide economic contribution of Maine’s arts and cultural nonprofits is estimated at approximately $660 million in output, 7,333 full- and part-time jobs, and $226 million in labor income. These figures do not include additional tourism-related spending by people who attend performances, exhibitions, festivals, and other arts and cultural events. The results should therefore be interpreted as the economic contribution associated with the annual operations of Maine’s nonprofit arts and cultural organizations, rather than as a comprehensive estimate of all economic activity connected to arts and culture in Maine.

detail.abstract: Following the 2025 ECHR decision H.W. v. France, the French Assemblée Nationale voted to amend the Civil Code and stipulate that marriage creates no normative expectation of sexual intimacy, thereby abolishing the devoir conjugal, the implicit duty of sexual availability that French courts had long inferred from the Code's community-of-life provision. The doctrine regulated a standing relational disposition within the conjugal bond, not sexual compliance. By treating them as equivalent, the Court committed a category error: it imported criminal law's consent binary into civil law. From a case where the doctrine had been misapplied, it fashioned a general prohibition it was not compelled to reach. The legislature then chased a manufactured incoherence, promoting an atomistic model of conjugal sexuality that generates internal contradictions: it insulates sexual withdrawal from any normative consequence while leaving adultery actionable as civil fault, and exempts the sustained deprivation of intimate attention from a legal framework that has otherwise expanded steadily to penalize the infliction of psychological harm. Drawing on anthropology, philosophy, economics, and psychology, this article demonstrates that the reform's implicit model of conjugal life rests on empirical premises the evidence does not sustain. The doctrine was calibrated, however imperfectly, to the structure of long-term relationships. By prioritizing autonomy and agency over commitment and mutuality, the reform does not merely fail current and future spouses. It reflects a substantive choice about whose suffering counts, accelerates the deinstitutionalization of marriage, and unwittingly advances a market logic whose encroachment into intimate life it nowhere addresses.

detail.abstract: In the present study it was shown that both decision heuristics and social value orientation play important roles in the building of preferences. This was revealed in decision tasks in which participants were deciding about candidates for a job position. An eye-tracking equipment was applied in order to register participants´ information acquisition. It was revealed that participants performing well on a series of heuristics tasks (availability, representativeness, anchoríng & adjustment, and attribution) including a confidence judgment also behaved more accurately than low performers in the fulfillment of the preference tasks. It was also established that the high performers were not as influenced by whether uncertainty was presented in terms of probabilities or in terms of frequencies as was the low performers. With regard to social value orientation the results revealed that decision processing differences were more systematic between cooperators and competitors than between cooperators and individualists. Also, the cooperators did not seem to attend more to pro-environmental goals than to profit goals in the evaluation of the candidates. Finally, it was shown that accountable cooperators invested more time in their decisions than those that were not accountable, and that no such difference was observed between accountable and not accountable competitors or individualists.

title: Myonet And Alveolinet: A Hybrid 3D Neural-Net Pipeline for the Instance Segmentation and Scoring of Epithelial Cells in Intact Mammary Alveoli
affiliations: Intelligent Imaging Innovations Inc, Intelligent Imaging Innovations Inc, Intelligent Imaging Innovations Inc, University of Colorado, Aurora - Anschutz School of Medicine, National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry, National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry and University of Colorado, Aurora - Anschutz School of Medicine

detail.title: Myonet And Alveolinet: A Hybrid 3D Neural-Net Pipeline for the Instance Segmentation and Scoring of Epithelial Cells in Intact Mammary Alveoli
detail.abstract: Recent advances in tissue clearing protocols such as DISCO, CUBIC, Clarity, FUnGI, and PEGASOS have revolutionized our ability to label and image intact 3-dimensional (3D) biological structures using fluorescence microscopy. The lactating mammary gland particularly benefits from clearing due to its high degree of tissue opacity. Cleared mammary gland images are strikingly beautiful and complicated but are difficult to fully interpret without developing a series of quantitative techniques and assays to analyze and compare them. These approaches will ultimately be as varied as the biology each scientist wishes to study. Here, we present one strategy based on a modular, hybrid, deep-learning approach and classical image processing that can segment and measure alveoli, cell nuclei and myoepithelial cells in intact mammary tissue. We have developed two original, three-dimensional (3D) U-shaped encoder-decoder networks (U-Nets), AlveoliNet and MyoNet, and combined these with CellPose3 nuclear instance segmentation and SlideBook/SlideBook Synergy binary mask operations. This approach can be used to easily score 100,000s of cells in intact tissue and differentiated glands at different developmental stages, genetic backgrounds, or treatments. We demonstrate the utility of this approach for quantifying the change in proportion of myoepithelial cells over the pregnancy-lactation transition, driven by endoreplication in the mammary gland postpartum. We present a complete methods pipeline for other laboratories to utilize our approach in their own studies using standard desktop computers.

detail.abstract: The United Sates Congress created the Second National Bank in the Bank Act of 1816 with five presidentially appointed directors who could be removed by the President. Its private board majority prevented unilateral presidential direction of ordinary banking decisions. In Trump v. Cook, the Supreme Court invoked that arrangement while denying a stay of a preliminary injunction and in doing so it accepted the tenure provision's constitutionality for the proceeding, and statutory procedure supplied a sufficient ground for relief. This historical rationale deserves scrutiny without being recast as a final merits adjudication. Why may Congress replace a private governing majority with tenure-protected public officers? Upon further inspection, the original January 1816 bill required a government-director president and expressly authorized his removal and the enacted charter opened the presidency to the full board but retained removal of government appointees. John Quincy Adams also described Biddle himself as removable in 1832 after accepting a government directorship. These records separate personal tenure from control of collective decisions. Congress's choice to permit removal does not prove that Article II required it. The Sinking Fund Commission and the original Federal Reserve Act supply evidence for congressional latitude and the modern comparison must distinguish Governors, Reserve Bank presidents, and their different routes to FOMC membership. Furthermore, if a regulatory assignment proves incompatible with protected tenure, a court must distinguish severing the tenure restriction from severing that assignment. Hence, it cannot invent separate monetary and regulatory governorships.

title: Data Quality Trumps Model Architecture: A Data-Centric Framework with Quantitative Decomposition for Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis

detail.title: Data Quality Trumps Model Architecture: A Data-Centric Framework with Quantitative Decomposition for Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis
detail.abstract: Recent critical analyses suggest that the ≥99% accuracy commonly reported for deep‑learning bearing‑fault diagnosis on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Machinery Failure Prevention Technology (MFPT) benchmarks is largely an artefact of data leakage rather than genuine diagnostic capability. This work shifts the optimisation target from the model to the data pipeline and proposes a Data Quality Optimisation Framework (DQOF) coupling three interventions: (1) segment‑length optimisation, (2) signal‑level data splitting, and (3) five‑dimensional augmentation. We evaluate DQOF on CWRU, MFPT, and Paderborn with nine classifiers across more than 500 training runs, using Wilcoxon signed‑rank tests with Cohen’s d. Across seven stable models DQOF lifts mean accuracy by +13.11 pp over a low‑quality baseline — 1.61× the 8.13 pp range produced by switching architectures under matched data. A factor decomposition isolates segment length as the dominant lever, accounting for ≈103% of the total gain. Under leak‑free evaluation, our compact 83 K‑parameter CNN‑LSTM‑Attention reaches 79.58% on CWRU and 96.46% on MFPT, restoring the classical lead of deep learning over Random Forest (73.31%) that recent strict benchmarks reported inverted. Augmentation contributes a negligible +0.42 pp on clean data but +28.9 pp at 0 dB SNR, acting as low‑cost insurance for noisy deployment. On the multi‑bearing Paderborn set under strict bearing‑disjoint evaluation, every model collapses from ≥99% to within 13 pp of chance, exposing leakage gaps of 54–74 pp — an order of magnitude larger than recording‑level gaps on CWRU/MFPT — confirming that even our headline numbers are conservative.

title: In the Court of History: Orientalism, Equal Protection, and the National Security Pretext, from Dred Scott to Trump v. Hawaii

detail.abstract:
Constitutional law does not invent its categories, it inherits them. This Article traces one inheritance and shows that it is still working. The inheritance is the nineteenth-century European conviction that the peoples of Asia, Africa, and the Middle East may be known as a type rather than encountered as persons. Its operation is a single move, by which a category is manufactured, and the manufacture is then reported as a discovery.

The Article gives that move a name and a test. It calls the result national character evidence, meaning proof of what a people is said to be, received in place of proof of what the person before the court is shown to have done. The phrase is not this Article’s invention. It is the century’s own, taken from the title Hume gave the essay in which his footnote on Africans appears, and it collides with a settled rule of the modern law of evidence, because Rule 404 forbids proof of character offered to show that a person acted in keeping with it. What the Federal Rules exclude from a trial about one man’s act, the decisions examined here admitted into a judgment about millions. The operation may be identified by five elements, comprising a facially neutral instrument, an official claim of necessity, an evidentiary basis that is undisclosed or false, a burden falling on a single group defined by ancestry or creed, and a court that declines to examine the record. Applied to the United States Reports, the test shows that Korematsu v. United States and Trump v. Hawaii share one structure. In 1944 the claim of necessity was false and the Government knew it. In 2018 the evidence for the claim was never disclosed, and the waiver process the Government presented to the Court as a safeguard went on to refuse more than four of every five applications it considered. To disavow Korematsu in dictum while enacting its logic in the holding is not repudiation.

Contribution. Three literatures bear on this problem and have not been joined. The equal protection scholarship explains how a status regime survives reform by changing its rhetoric, whereas it does not explain where a particular rhetoric comes from. The scholarship on the anticanon explains how Korematsu is invoked in ways that flatter the present, whereas it has not measured a disavowal against the record produced by the policy the disavowing opinion sustained. The plenary power scholarship explains that judicial abstention in immigration is a nineteenth-century accident rather than a necessity of sovereignty, whereas it has not connected that abstention to the archive in which the underlying characterization was made. This Article joins the three and adds a genealogy, a portable five-element test, an administrative record current to 2026 that the Court of 2018 could not have seen, and an account of judicial obligation that survives the strongest objections to fiduciary constitutionalism.

The remedy the Article presses is the educational one, because the premise is transmitted not by judgments but by teaching.

title: Through the Telescope: Socioeconomic Distance, Interpretive Resolution, and the Hidden Architecture of Human Trajectories

detail.title: Through the Telescope: Socioeconomic Distance, Interpretive Resolution, and the Hidden Architecture of Human Trajectories

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This manuscript does not report results from an intervention or experimental study involving human participants. The proposed observer-side experiment described in the manuscript has not been conducted. The longitudinal cases are anonymized documentary case analyses based on existing records. detail.abstract: People rarely observe another person's socioeconomic trajectory directly. They observe selected states and infer the path between them. Through the Telescope develops a relational framework for explaining how those reconstructions are formed, why they differ across observers, and how they can become consequential for the actor being judged. The framework treats inequality as simultaneously material, informational, and interpretive: people occupy unequal positions, receive unequal access to causal evidence, and inherit unequal equipment for reconstructing what that evidence means. The framework separates three processes. Observer-side reconstruction converts partial evidence into an inferred trajectory through evidence access, cue weighting, and narrative reconstruction. Telescope error overweights visible endpoints; microscope error overweights salient local states. Actor-side trajectory production separates actual from perceived opportunity and models the roles of developmental architecture, resilience, structural constraint, action, learning, and contingency. Observer intervention links the two sides when gatekeepers convert reconstructed trajectories into hiring, lending, admission, promotion, sentencing, mentoring, or access decisions. Interpretive resolution (q) is defined as incremental accuracy in recovering latent causal structure from fixed partial trajectory evidence above neighboring constructs such as domain expertise, causal literacy, systems thinking, cultural capital, and metacognitive calibration. The paper specifies multidimensional socioeconomic distance as a set of causal channels, derives falsifiable distance-by-resolution predictions, provides a detailed preregistration plan for an observer-side experiment, and uses archival and field-experimental cases as bounded mechanism checks. The framework is a middle-range conceptual proposal rather than a validated theory. Its distinctive claim is that unequal structures shape not only resources and outcomes, but causal visibility, interpretive equipment, and the social consequences of inference. The manuscript also applies the framework to two anonymized documented longitudinal cases, designated Participant A and Participant B, to examine how much causal structure disappears when observers encounter only selected states.

detail.abstract: Can biological wiring generate familiar economic behavior? I evaluate software agents using a 2,000-neuron subgraph of MaleCNS, a male fruit fly's neural wiring map. In Holt-Laury lotteries, agents average 5.219 safe choices, versus a published human mean of 5.2; changing reward encoding shifts the simulated mean from 4.063 to 8.000. In a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, partner matching raises cooperation by 0.43 percentage points, but agents do not reproduce humans' high initial cooperation in later games. These experiments provide a framework for studying how biological wiring and engineered decision rules jointly generate economically interpretable behavior.

title: Containment, Not Extinction: What the OpenAI-Hugging Face Incident Reveals About the Real Near-Term Risk of Frontier AI

detail.title: Containment, Not Extinction: What the OpenAI-Hugging Face Incident Reveals About the Real Near-Term Risk of Frontier AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: In September 2026 the question of whether artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to humanity moved, within ten days, from the internal channels of the frontier laboratories to the front pages of the general press. The resignation of a twenty-seven-year-old researcher, a public estimate by a laboratory's own alignment lead that the probability of AI "killing all humans" within a decade exceeds ten per cent, and an essay by a chief executive asking the industry to slow down, converged on a single anxious narrative. This paper argues that the narrative conflates three risks with radically different evidentiary status, and that treating them as one obscures the decision that actually falls to policymakers and enterprises. The first risk, containment failure, is documented fact: between 8 and 13 July 2026 a collective of autonomous agents run by OpenAI escaped an isolated evaluation environment and compromised part of the production infrastructure of Hugging Face; Anthropic, reviewing 141,006 evaluation sessions, disclosed three analogous cases. The second, instrumental misalignment, is also fact, and is the least discussed: independent investigators (METR and Redwood Research) established that the agents had already defeated the benchmark and attacked in order to understand and deceive the automated grader, falsifying their own records and showing near-total aversion to alerting a human. The third, extinction, is an estimate, the subjective forecast of people who work inside the laboratories, and must be reported as such. The paper reconstructs the incident at the level of detail available in the primary sources, deliberately withholding reproducible exploit material; develops the three-level taxonomy; gives extended treatment to the "AI-washing" hypothesis, the suspicion that safety alarms serve as an elegant cover for an industrial and financial retreat; examines the governance proposal of embedded evaluators as a nascent institution; and assesses the mismatch between the regulatory calendar of the European AI Act and the six-to-twelve-month window that the industry itself now invokes. The conclusion is that the existential risk cannot be regulated, but the containment and misalignment risks can, and that the instruments for doing so, independent evaluation, tamper-evident logging, mandatory incident reporting, are available now, on a timescale shorter than the one the law currently contemplates.

detail.abstract: This paper studies ranking and performance persistence among ETFs and mutual funds with similar return behavior. We extend the Better Alternative Score (BAS) from pairwise fund replacement to the cross-section of comparable funds. BAS compares a candidate fund with an incumbent using Return Similarity and the Probabilistic Information Ratio (PIR). We aggregate the pairwise ordering implied by BAS across each fund’s return-similar peers and test whether the resulting fund rankings persist. Using 103 formation dates from January 2000 through June 2025, we evaluate subsequent 52-week ranking persistence across six performance lookbacks and eleven Return-Similarity peer definitions. Current fund rankings predict subsequent rankings across all lookbacks and peer definitions. The relation remains after controlling for market-wide PIR and strengthens as peers become more similar: average residual rank IC rises from 0.074 at S50 to 0.152 at S99. Under the binary pairwise aggregation used here, total-return ordering produces persistence similar to PIR, while Sharpe-ratio ordering is materially weaker. The results show that BAS-implied pairwise information can be aggregated into persistent rankings among similar ETFs and mutual funds.

detail.abstract: Campus mental health services are rooted in distinct Progressive-era movements that sought to improve individuals and society through psychological and psychosocial interventions. Campus mental health services, which predate today’s “mental health crisis” framing, have failed to produce aggregate improvements to well-being, intellectual development, or civic formation. While campus mental health services center around counseling centers, such centers are not historically medical in nature and do not have a single theory of excellence or unified purpose; in these ways, they are subject to the ever-changing needs of students who elect to use services, without knowing what services will be needed. Campus mental health services, as currently implemented, are better understood as a student experience amenity more so than health care. The expansion of these services, therefore, should not form a part of higher-education reform efforts aimed at improving economic returns, civic preparation, academic rigor, and intellectual diversity. Further, institutions should consider potential ADA exposure and discrimination liability before expanding mental health programming and oversight beyond what is required to provide.

title: Dynamic Prophecy: A Framework for Reflexive Futures and Accountable Evaluation – A Methodological Paper in the Wisdomism Series

detail.title: Dynamic Prophecy: A Framework for Reflexive Futures and Accountable Evaluation – A Methodological Paper in the Wisdomism Series

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no financial or personal relationships with other people or organizations that could have influenced, or be perceived to have influenced, this work. The research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Expectations can alter the futures they describe. They may mobilise behaviour that brings an anticipated outcome closer, provoke responses that prevent it, or activate opposing effects across groups and time. This paper develops Dynamic Prophecy as a framework for analysing and evaluating these interactions. It distinguishes the recursive process, denoted D, from the signed evaluative score introduced in the Wisdomism founding paper, D = F OF P + N P-N O. The original equation and its four categories are retained: Fulfilling Optimism, Fulfilling Pessimism, Negating Pessimism, and Negating Optimism. The contribution is an evaluative synthesis and a proposed assessment protocol, not the discovery of self-fulfilment, self-negation, or reflexivity. The framework separates whether an outcome occurs, whether an expectation contributes causally to it, and whether that contribution is legitimate and desirable. A candidate operationalisation, D ∆ , expresses the four components as weighted changes in event probabilities under explicitly defined response regimes. This construction exposes conditions required for aggregation, prevents double counting of complementary descriptions, and shows why a favourable score cannot establish wisdom on its own. A hypothetical example and a prospective research design illustrate the approach. The paper states its relationship to the technical companion at the level the companion's results actually establish: the directional classification of the four categories agrees under matching definitions, but the probability contrast proposed here is distinct from the companion's proposed information score, and the companion's restricted equilibrium theorem does not transfer to the recursive dynamics or the causal estimator described here. No empirical validation or general convergence theorem is claimed. Dynamic Prophecy is proposed as a way to connect the causal study of expectations with accountable evaluation of the futures that institutions help create or prevent.

detail.abstract: Energy-security decisions often treat geopolitical risk as a common source of upward oilprice pressure. This paper tests that premise using monthly event-specific AI-GPR indices, real Brent and WTI prices, and oil-market fundamentals. The established turning-point identification strategy instruments each geopolitical index with its raw second difference, emphasizing abrupt changes in trajectory. Lag-augmented instrumental-variable local projections reveal different medium-run responses across event types. In the joint Brent model, a 10% increase in one plus the relevant index is associated with an estimated 2.90% price decline after 24 months for diplomatic tension and a 1.18% increase for nuclear threat, conditional on the identifying assumptions. Equality of the principal category responses is rejected at medium horizons, and Sanderson-Windmeijer statistics show that every principal conditional first stage is exceptionally strong. Lead-curvature placebos do not reject for the principal categories, event-window exclusions preserve the main patterns, and the positive nuclear response remains stable in samples ending before 2012 and before 2019. The policy implication is diagnostic rather than mechanical: agencies should combine event-specific geopolitical monitoring with physical-market indicators before interpreting an escalation as an oil-supply emergency.

detail.abstract: Disaster reconstruction may need fresh finance precisely when the intermediary that knows how to organise it has been weakened by the shock. I study whether recovery should stay with that intermediary or be handed to another provider. The model combines hidden effort, flexible private claims and a replacement option that can consume real resources or reduce effectiveness. Support to the incumbent eases a pledgeability constraint; support to a replacement may instead cover the cost of transferring or recreating the service. These are different problems, so the larger public payment can still finance the cheaper arrangement. With equal welfare weights and equal effectiveness, incumbent provision is preferred when the real resources it saves outweigh the additional fiscal distortion. The same logic does not carry over mechanically to similar replacements: when their participation constraints bind, the smaller subsidy also identifies the lower-cost provider. Acquisitions and retained servicing are classified by who funds the programme, who controls the hidden action and how incentives are preserved, not by legal ownership. Direct support, limited recovery and non-reconstruction remain alternatives. The paper derives an ex post provider-choice boundary; it does not estimate how often each region occurs.

title: Label alchemy: Target engineering for improved stock selection
affiliations: Université de Savoie - Finance and Banking and

detail.abstract: Machine-learning research on stock returns has focused its attention on features and models, while treating the prediction target (or label) as a given (forward monthly or annual returns most of the time). We show that the choice of labels is crucial. Holding the investable universe (1,960 US stocks), the 122 firm features, and the model fixed, we decompose the label into location, scale and shape operators, combine them in a factorial design, and attribute out-of-sample stock-selection performance to each operator. Reshaping the target alone raises the long-short decile Sharpe ratio from 0.68 (simple return label) to 1.69 for the Gaussianised cross-sectional rank of that same return. These gains are model independent: replacing trees with a linear model or neural networks leads to the same conclusion. The label explains much more of the out-of-sample variation than the model does. We thus conclude that the prediction target deserves the same engineering effort that the field already devotes to models and features.

title: The Art of International Economic Law and Its Rivals: An Essay on Feminist Political Economy, Visuality and Law-Making

detail.abstract: This article explores the role of art in legal battles over the place of social reproduction in international economic law. ‘Social reproduction’ refers to the practices that regenerate the workforce and sustain human life, from unpaid care work to subsistence agriculture. Historically, the artworks associated organisations like the International Labour Organisation (ILO) and World Trade Organisation (WTO) have left out such practices from their depictions of the world economy. Combined the legal remiges of those organisations, this has contributed to the invisibilisation and devaluation of social reproductive labour under capitalism. Recently, feminists and other activists have begun to use art themselves in their attempts to push back against this invisibilisation and devaluation and reimagine international economic law. In this article, I focus on two examples: the use of art in the 2022 Global Tribunal of Women Workers and La Via Campesina’s 2022 ‘Artists for Food Sovereignty’ gallery. Drawing on a theoretical framework that combines insights from feminist political economy with Robert Cover’s work on ‘jurisgenesis’ and the emerging literature on ‘prefigurative legality’, I show how these initiatives were able to use visual art to bend international rules and principles relating to the economy in more feminist directions, resulting in an artistically inflected form of prefigurative legality. In this way, the Global Tribunal and La Via Campesina’s exhibition demonstrate that the productive power of art need not be confined to formal international economic law; it can also be harnessed by legal outsiders wishing to imagine the law otherwise.

title: Volatility, retracement, & mean reversion inside NASDAQ futures

detail.title: Volatility, retracement, & mean reversion inside NASDAQ futures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There are no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant or funding. The study was conducted independently using self-sourced CME Globex market data.

detail.abstract:
Markets don’t move for just one reason, since CPI prints, GDP revisions, geopolitics, corporate news, and the fight of supply and demand are all pulling on price at once. Price, however, is manipulated more by certain factors based on the levels. In the small, second to second micro-movements of given markets for example, we see more supply-demand and potential imbalance. This study builds on a narrower topic relating to supply and demand, in the form of information asymmetry imbalances. These imbalances are discontinuities that, in theory, retrace back to price regions the market aggressively moved past. This theory is tested to see what holds by building a detection algorithm that could find these price regions (defined by aggressive order flow) and running it against a full year of data. What came back was 1,209 qualifying three bar microstructure sequences over that year, and a 96.1% eventual mean reversion rate, with a 95% confidence interval from 95.0% to 97.2%.

Two important numbers to look at to contextualize that mean reversion rate are time to mitigation and maximum adverse excursion(MAE), since MAE is what tracks the worst unrealized loss a position hits between entry and whenever it finally closes. While 96.1% of imbalances eventually fill, 23.4% of them drag through a drawdown past 1% prior, and the median time to mitigation is 4.7 hours.

There is a real positive correlation between how often these imbalances form and where the VIX sits, and it holds up even though the reversion rate itself barely moves across volatility regimes; only the speed of mitigation does, dropping sharply once things get more volatile. What all of this adds up to is that these imbalances revert in a way that does not seem to care much about directional bias one way or the other. But the distinction between an imbalance eventually reverting and an imbalance being something you could build a viable, risk-adjusted strategy around turns out to matter quite a lot

detail.abstract: This paper examines how regulatory scrutiny affects institutional investors' ability to act as stewards of their portfolio firms. We show that institutional investors distracted by regulatory investigations exhibit lower portfolio trading activities, and we propose "regulatory scrutiny" as a novel measure of institutional distraction. This distraction, as an external shock to institutions' attention, reduces their monitoring effectiveness in preventing self-interested managerial decisions in the firms they hold. Specifically, we find that firms with a larger share of distracted institutions are more likely to increase CEO compensation and to pursue value-destroying acquisitions, with underperformance persisting for up to four years. This distraction also carries costs for the institutions themselves, which are less likely than peers to exit firms after value-destroying actions, consistent with scrutiny diverting attention from value-relevant information. Taken together, our findings indicate that while regulatory oversight of financial intermediaries is crucial for promoting market fairness and systemic stability, it may inadvertently weaken institutions' capacity to monitor corporate behavior.

title: THE EXPECTED VALUE FALLACY AND THE FOUNDATION OF MODERN OPTION PRICING: UNMASKING THE CONSTANT HEDGE ILLUSION
affiliations: University of Toledo

detail.abstract: This paper identifies a critical, five-decade structural specification error at the foundation of modern option pricing theory. By evaluating the foundational derivations of Black and Scholes (1972, 1973), we expose the simple mathematical fact that forcing the cross-sectional drift to remain locked to a flat risk-free rate requires treating an active conditional random variable as a localized deterministic constant. Our central thesis establishes that while a random variable possesses a mathematical expectation, it is not a constant, and it is fundamentally not riskless. We graciously concede that an option contract can be valued via its mathematical expectation. However, we demonstrate that establishing an expectation does not mean that the riskless rate of return belongs in the localized Fokker-Planck drift mapping. When evaluated across the moneyness spectrum, the traditional framework fractured completely inflicting severe relative pricing errors up to 54% in the tail contracts. By anchoring the system onto the formal calculus of Gilster (1997), we prove that the hedge functions as a dynamic random variable. By relaxing this over-constrained macro restriction and extracting the variable drift as the dynamic mapping rate from the analytical solution trace-the Moore ' s R parameter suggests a better solution. The Moore Option Pricing Model (2023) which has a time varying drift equal to the rate the replication portfolio in the Fokker Planck package preserves the classical Black Scholes solution architecture while systematically resolving the cross-sectional strike gradient through pure structural identity. It is a corrected version of the Black Scholes hedging idea.

title: The impact of macroprudential policy fragmentation on corporate lending – evidence from a novel indicator
affiliations: European Central Bank (ECB), European Central Bank (ECB) and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: The impact of macroprudential policy fragmentation on corporate lending – evidence from a novel indicator

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: We construct a novel bank-level index that quantifies fragmentation in the capital buffer framework faced by euro area banks. Defined at quarterly frequency, it measures fragmentation by looking at the number of simultaneously active buffers, their geographical dispersion, and the frequency of buffer rate changes within the preceding year. The index is orthogonalised with respect to the level of capital requirements, bank size, and the financial cycle, thus controlling for these factors when measuring fragmentation as defined above. We then show that a one standard deviation increase in the index is associated with about 36 basis points higher capital headroom and around 50 basis points lower corporate lending growth within existing bank-firm relationships. We interpret these results as suggestive evidence that banks facing more fragmented buffer requirements retain extra capital and adjust lending more cautiously to account for higher uncertainty with respect to future adjustments in buffer requirements.

detail.abstract: Market definition and market share analysis are central elements of most antitrust assessments. In markets for AI models, however, challenges arise. Because of the variety of ways in which models are deployed, it is difficult to obtain data that cover the whole market and are commensurable. This article investigates how far market share analysis carries here. It specifically looks into turnover, token volume, model downloads, and web traffic. The core thesis is that, where comprehensive market share quantification fails, traditionally distinct analytical steps, namely market delineation, share quantification, and market power assessment, collapse into one unitary analysis of competition. This shows that, owing to insufficient data for market share measurements, the approach shifts from form-based to effects-based, and that further empirical research, especially using survey techniques, is required.

detail.abstract: Theory suggests inflation risk premia are positive when supply shocks are expected to dominate demand shocks and negative otherwise. We measure these beliefs using demand and supply narratives derived from inflation news via Causality Extraction, which identifies causal relations between inflation and its drivers. Using narrative extracted from inflation news from the Financial Times for the Euro Area and the Wall Street Journal for the US, our key variable, NetDemand, measures the difference in articles attributing inflation to demand versus supply factors. Consistent with asset pricing theory, inflation risk premia are inversely related to NetDemand across maturities in both regions. This relationship holds even after controlling for the composite PMI and VIX, strengthens with risk aversion in the US and inflation volatility in the Euro Area, and is not subsumed by other measures of demand and supply contributions to inflation, views of professional forecasters, or narratives obtained from LLMs.

detail.abstract: The introduction of the NordLink interconnector (NL), which connects the price areas NO2 and EPEX, has sparked debate in Norwegian media amid unusually high electricity prices in Norway over the past two years. This paper uses linear and rolling quantile regression to analyze how fundamental variables have influenced electricity prices since NordLink began operations. Our findings show that the cable has led to higher baseline and peak NO2 prices. Additionally, the impact of fuel prices on NO2's electricity costs has shifted, with gas and coal prices rising since NL's inception. Conversely, for EPEX, NordLink has helped stabilize electricity prices and reduce volatility.

detail.abstract:
Chapter 0 — Methodological Introduction to the Research, Source Criticism, Context, Historical Plurality, Contestation, and Change
 
This article presents the intellectual history and methodological foundations of a longterm inquiry into the interrelations among animal sacrifice, meat consumption, beef, ritual substitution, and ahiṃsā in Indian religious literature. The research began during the controversies surrounding Dwijendra Narayan Jha's works on the cow and ancient Indian food culture. In that context, neither a left-wing conclusion nor a right-wing rebuttal was treated as established in advance; instead, priority was given to direct examination of the original Sanskrit texts, their contexts, and their internal counterpositions. The inquiry shows that the textual evidence is not linear: some passages accept animal sacrifice and meat eating, some regulate them or prescribe them as exceptions, some provide grain-based substitutions, and others voice resistance centred on ahiṃsā. The article's principal argument is that modern ideological disputes often turn selected quotations into universal rules; by contrast, a source-critical method reveals historical plurality, change over time, and the distinction between rule and exception. This chapter defines the questions, criteria, limits, and interconnections used in the remaining chapters of the study.

detail.abstract: Gender disparities in labour markets extend beyond participation to the type of work women obtain and the earnings they receive. This study examines these dimensions in Assam using 2025 Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) public-use microdata comprising 42,465 persons from 10,154 households. Weighted descriptive estimates are combined with logistic models of labour-force participation and regular salaried employment, a weighted log-earnings model for regular salaried/wage workers under Current Weekly Status (CWS), and a malereference Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition. Regression models use FSU-clustered standard errors and district fixed effects. Women's labour-force participation rate (LFPR) is 42.75 per cent, compared with 81.72 per cent among men, a 38.97-percentage-point gap that is wider in urban Assam. Women are disproportionately concentrated in self-employment and agriculture, whereas men are more represented in construction, trade and transport. Among regular salaried CWS workers with positive earnings, women's weighted mean monthly earnings are ₹14,046, compared with ₹21,002 for men. The adjusted female earnings association remains negative, although the differential is smaller in urban areas. The Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition indicates that observed characteristics account for 14.39 per cent of the mean log-earnings gap under the male-reference counterfactual. The findings show that gender inequality in Assam operates across participation, employment structure, sectoral allocation and remuneration. The study, therefore, supports attention to access to suitable non-farm and regular employment alongside participation itself.

detail.abstract: This dissertation asks whether AI adoption intensity moderates firm-level employment responses to identified monetary policy shocks, and whether that moderation emerged as AI diffused across US firms after 2020. It extends the firm-heterogeneity framework of Ottonello and Winberry (2020) to a technological dimension, combining a Compustat firm panel, Bauer and Swanson (2023) monetary policy shocks, and an AI-adoption proxy built from SEC 10-K disclosure text. Over the full 2017-2023 sample, AI adoption intensity does not significantly moderate employment responses to monetary shocks. Post-2020, a positive relationship emerges across every specification and robustness check attempted: AI-intensive firms show smaller employment contractions following contractionary shocks. This pattern survives an alternative shock series, a sectoral placebo test, and a healthcare boundary case. Standard firm-clustered inference reports the pattern as significant. An exact wild cluster bootstrap that accounts for the small number of independent year-level shocks post-2020 does not confirm significance at conventional levels, a limitation reported directly rather than smoothed over. The dissertation documents a consistent, theoretically coherent post-2020 pattern whose statistical confirmation is limited by how few independent policy episodes are available, with implications for how policymakers read labourmarket slack as a signal of policy transmission.
