detail.abstract: This paper argues that the Grand Chamber's judgment in Verein KlimaSeniorinnen Schweiz v Switzerland over-extends the 'living instrument' doctrine. It converts Article 8 ECHR from a qualified negative protection into a prescriptive regulatory duty, and it does so by treating aspirational commitments under the Paris Agreement as a judicially enforceable standard. Drawing on Fuller's account of polycentric adjudication, the critiques of Lord Sumption, Lord Hoffmann and Jeremy Waldron, and Aileen Kavanagh's collaborative account of constitutional adjudication, it contends that the judgment exceeds the institutional competence of a supranational court, and contrasts it with the German Federal Constitutional Court's decision in Neubauer. It then assesses the position of the United Kingdom under the Human Rights Act 1998 (HRA). Formal parliamentary sovereignty remains intact, but acute practical pressure arises through sections 2, 6 and 7(7) HRA. The distinction between statutory review and rights-based review is central to how far that pressure extends.

detail.abstract: A client hires a sourcing agent to source goods and typically pays said agent a commission on the cost of the those goods. In the standard treatment of the principal-agent model, the principal pays the agent a commission on the revenue generated from the relationship. I show that the choice of base is irrelevant: the two contracts implement identical prices, agent effort, probability of product delivery and expected profits for any demand function, delivery technology and (private) cost of agent effort. The equilibrium price in the downstream market equals the price that a vertically integrated client would set, so the commission is a pure transfer and there is no double marginalization. Only the rate paid to the agent differs by commission base: the optimal commission rate equals the agent's compensation share of the gross profit margin times the Lerner index, and the cost-based rate exceeds the revenue-based rate by the gross markup. In contrast, in the licensing literature, where the per-unit and ad-valorem royalties (commissions) are strictly ranked. In that literature, one party (licensor) sets the royalty and the another party sets the price (licensee). In the current context, the client holds both instruments and thus sets both, making the commission base a simple normalization.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a co-evolutionary account of the socioeconomic order by examining the reciprocal constitution of institutional structure and the transcendent capacity of situated human consciousness. It reconstructs the historical transformation of labor from medieval monastic institutions, which integrated organizational continuity, rational inquiry, and religious meaning, through ascetic Protestantism's methodical conception of worldly vocation and into the secular scientific, technological, and capitalist order. Drawing on Hegelian determinate negation, Whiteheadian process metaphysics, and the adjacent possible, the paper interprets socioeconomic development as an open-ended process of institutional inheritance, path-dependent recombination, stabilization, conflict, and revision rather than as linear progress or predetermined synthesis. Parsons' structural functionalism explains how innovations become stabilized through differentiated roles, norms, and institutions, while Durkheim, Merton, Dahrendorf, Collins, Skocpol, and Kuhn illuminate the strains, conflicts, and discontinuities that functional integration alone cannot explain. Digital platforms and algorithmic governance are examined as contemporary manifestations of this process, combining expanded capacities for coordination and innovation with surveillance, classification, data extraction, and new forms of institutional power. Smith, Veblen, and Bourdieu connect these macro-institutional dynamics to prudence, productive discipline, consumption, status emulation, habitus, and class reproduction. The paper argues that production and consumption are morally ambivalent domains through which goods, knowledge, meanings, technologies, institutions, and forms of agency are continuously created and transformed. Human progress occurs when these recursive processes enlarge warranted knowledge, meaningful agency, reciprocal recognition, and sustainable cooperation; they become destructive when economic and technological systems reduce persons and nature to calculable resources. Progress is therefore contingent, contested, reversible, and institutionally mediated. The paper concludes that civilization develops, when it develops meaningfully, through the recursive activity of situated consciousness inheriting, interpreting, criticizing, recombining, and reconstructing the institutional worlds that both enable and constrain it.

detail.abstract: Colombia faces a persistent shortage of medical specialists, with especially severe deficits outside the main metropolitan areas. This paper asks whether that shortage reflects genuine training-capacity constraints or entry restriction by incumbent specialists who benefit from scarcity. I combine administrative records on physician registration, training, and formal-sector earnings to test two competing explanations. Specialist availability is highly unequal across space: in 2011 Bogotá had roughly 27 times as many specialists per capita as Vaupés. Earnings within the health sector are sharply polarized, and specialists earn about twice as much as general practitioners (×2.12 in 2022-2025). Medical-specialty graduate output has grown only gradually since 2001 despite rising real physician earnings. A reduced-form intent-to-treat design shows that Ley 1797 of 2016 did not increase admissions at newly eligible institutions, indicating that the formal accreditation margin was not the operative bottleneck. A conditional logit model of specialist location recovers strong responses to local wages, employer concentration, agglomeration, and distance costs, suggesting that supply expansion alone would not close the geographic gap between core and peripheral municipalities.

detail.abstract: A hung jury leaves a criminal accusation unresolved. The State may seek a retrial, but the defendant has no corresponding right to a new jury trial or to an acquittal if the prosecution declines to retry the case. In this paper, we examine the effects of this asymmetry. We consider granting defendants who have faced a deadlocked jury the right to request a new trial, requiring the State either to retry the case or to acquit. The analysis is motivated by the premise that the opportunity to seek a retrial is more valuable to factually innocent defendants, who prefer the finality of an acquittal to merely avoiding conviction through a deadlock. One-sided unanimity and other rules that facilitate acquittal in the first trial operate as partial substitutes for the right to retrial, reducing the occasions for exercising that right, but potentially increasing its value in the remaining deadlocked cases.

Adding the three quality attributes increases within-grid adjusted R² by 0.054 for apartments and 0.031 for houses. detail.abstract: This study aims to explore the influence of individual family values on attitudes, i.e. the degree of perceived necessity, toward marriage and childbirth by generation, gender, and marital status, and to derive policy implications. By analyzing the influence of gender role values and marriage values on attitudes toward marriage, we demonstrated that the more the agreement with traditional gender role values, the greater the tendency to feel the necessity of marriage, and that individualistic family values had a greater influence than traditional family values. Gender role values and child values that affect attitudes toward childbirth were found to be with respect to traditional gender roles and children's instrumental, social, and emotional/relational values, respectively. Through this, we suggested that policies for balancing work and family and for securing childcare rights may be effective. However, we inferred that policies that accept non-traditional family forms and extramarital childbirth can be limited to some extent. Lastly, although single women of the Millennials and Generation Z share strong gender egalitarian values, a significant proportion of them also supports traditional values, indicating that careful attention is needed in establishing and implementing policies targeting those generations.

detail.abstract: The liberal international order now faces its most acute challenge from within its own founding coalition. The second Trump administration's sweeping tariffs-including a 145 per cent rate on Chinese goods and a baseline 10 per cent levy on all imports announced in April 2025-its use of trade policy for geopolitical leverage, and its broader retreat from multilateral institutions have raised fundamental questions about the durability of the postwar economic order. Yet this crisis narrative obscures an important geographic asymmetry. The same process of economic integration that generated persistent labour-market dislocation across deindustrializing communities in advanced Western economies has produced sustained employment growth, rising incomes, and expanding middle classes across much of developing Asia. These divergent material experiences are associated with divergent political attitudes: Asia-Pacific publics remain among the world's most supportive of trade openness and foreign investment. We argue that this legitimacy constitutes a political resource. It gives governments greater headroom to sustain costly commitments, resist protectionist pressures, and deepen regional cooperation in strategically important industries such as semiconductors, critical minerals, and clean-energy manufacturing. The domestic foundations of the open economic order have not disappeared. They may instead have shifted geographically.

detail.abstract: Public and policy discussions in South Korea often describe young people as having given up on romantic relationships, and government agencies have sponsored matchmaking events as part of low-fertility policy. Yet systematic evidence on the prevalence and social distribution of dating among unmarried Koreans remains limited. Drawing on the third wave of the Korean Survey on Dating, Marriage, and Family Values (2025; N = 4,000; ages 25-49), together with time-series survey data, national statistics on marriage attitudes, and municipality-level population registers, this paper examines romantic relationships in Korea. Four findings emerge. First, about one in five respondents aged 25-49 is currently dating (including those "seeing someone"), and about two-thirds of unmarried respondents report some romantic involvement in the past year. Second, in comparisons with earlier surveys, the proportion of unmarried people currently dating peaks at a later age in 2025 (late twenties) than in 1991 (early twenties), and the share of adults with a positive view of marriage declined between 2002 and 2014 and has since ranged between about 51% and 57%; differences in survey design limit comparisons of levels over time. Third, among unmarried respondents aged 35-49, 21.4% (192 of 899) report no romantic involvement since age 20; this corresponds to about 8% of all survey respondents in this age range. In bivariate comparisons, this share differs by region, employment status, education, and subjective class, with clearer differences among men. Fourth, most respondents who dated in the past year met their partner in everyday settings such as school or work or through introductions by friends and family; among unmarried respondents with recent romantic involvement, 8.3% met through matchmaking agencies or dating apps.

detail.abstract: This paper demonstrates that the dynamics of economic deviation, such as endogenous growth, follow a law of motion that is closely analogous to Newtonian mechanics. Within this framework, specific externalities-including uncompensated knowledge spillovers, education, and environmental degradation-as well as factors such as monopolies, the underprovision of public goods, the depletion of natural resources, white-collar crime, and an upward shift in the rate of time preference, generate "forces" that drive output deviations. This study formally models how force-based economic deviation aligns with classical Newtonian laws, specifically the principles of inertia, acceleration, and actionreaction. Furthermore, the underlying real interest rate is identified as the primary point of application for these forces, with the interest-bearing period determining the transient deformation, or softness, of the economic system.

detail.abstract: Financial time series evolve across multiple temporal resolutions, challenging forecasting systems to incorporate newly available information without repeatedly recomputing unchanged representations. We introduce HARN, a Hierarchical Associative Resonance Network for event-driven multi-timeframe forecasting. HARN maintains persistent representations across temporal levels and updates each level only when its corresponding completed bar becomes available. The architecture combines causal multi-scale temporal encoding, gated associative memory, cross-level resonance, and hierarchical evidence aggregation, with forecasting performed in basis-point space and reconstructed to the original price scale. We evaluate HARN on four assets spanning equity, foreign exchange, and commodity markets using multiple random seeds and component ablations. HARN achieves competitive reconstructed-price forecasting errors against single-timeframe PatchTST and TimeXer baselines, while ablations reveal the effects of removing individual components across assets and timeframes. A code-level audit further examines consistency between the implementation and the defined event-driven causal protocol. The results position HARN as a persistent multi-timeframe forecasting framework rather than evidence of universal predictive superiority.

detail.abstract: Tactical and regime-based allocation strategies are usually judged by comparing their Sharpe ratio with that of a static benchmark over a few decades of history. I ask whether such a comparison can succeed. Using the Jobson-Korkie test with Memmel's correction, I show that the sample needed to detect a Sharpe difference depends almost entirely on the size of the difference and on the correlation ρ between strategy and benchmark, a quantity academic studies rarely report. At the correlations observed here (0.76 to 0.95), detecting an annualised difference of 0.10 at 80% power requires between 128 and 610 years of monthly data. I demonstrate the consequences with a fully real-time macroeconomic regime pipeline, built from point-in-time data aligned to publication lags, forward-filtered hidden Markov probabilities and expanding-window re-estimation, and evaluated over 535 months. No regime strategy differs significantly from a rebalanced 60/40 portfolio (walk-forward HMM: 0.655 against 0.682, p = 0.64). A factorial ablation that reintroduces three channels of look-ahead bias produces no difference that survives multiple-testing correction. Minimum detectable effects range from 0.18 to 0.36 Sharpe, above every observed difference. These nulls therefore do not show that regime models fail. They show that, at the effect sizes where allocation overlays are marketed, the question lies beyond what a backtest can resolve. I recommend that studies report ρ and the minimum detectable effect alongside every Sharpe comparison, and I release a test suite that regenerates every figure in the paper.

detail.abstract: Declining marriage in many societies has been attributed, in online and public debate, to a male withdrawal from marriage prompted by the perceived legal risks of family law. This article examines whether that attribution survives scrutiny and what law's proper response to voluntary male singleness and to male separatist subcultures should be. Using doctrinal and comparative legal analysis of Brazil, England and Wales, the United States and Japan, together with a structured synthesis of published empirical and sociological literature, it asks through which channels family law bears on the male decision not to marry. The article distinguishes three modes of non-entry into marriage (autonomous abstention, economically constrained non-entry, and ideologized separatism) and shows that each engages a different body of law. It contends that the evidence consulted supports a largely gender-symmetric deinstitutionalization of marriage with male-specific economic and perceptual components; that the causal contribution of family-law rules to male non-entry is plausible but untested; and that the most credible legal channel is the predictability of exit consequences, especially child arrangements, rather than the substantive generosity of financial remedies. Abstention from marriage is a protected liberty, while separatist subcultures become legally relevant only when they generate harassment, incitement or violence, which conduct-based law already addresses. The article proposes reforms grounded in information, predictability and child welfare rather than marriage promotion, identifies conditions under which its thesis would fail, and states the limits of a study that generates no original empirical data. detail.abstract:
This article is an English translation of the revised and integrated Japanese version of Eiji Murashima’s “Karayuki-san (Japanese Prostitutes) in Thailand: 1885–1920,” originally published in Journal of Asia-Pacific Studies (Ajia Taiheiyō Tōkyū), no. 46 (2023), together with relevant additions and corrections subsequently published in no. 49 (2024). The present English version is therefore not simply a translation of the 2023 article, but a complete translation of the revised Japanese text in which these supplementary findings have been incorporated.

The study reconstructs, as far as surviving sources permit, the history of karayuki-san—Japanese women engaged in prostitution overseas—in Siam (Thailand) from approximately 1885 to 1925. Because the number of Japanese women involved in prostitution in Siam was relatively small and surviving documentation is fragmentary, the study draws on a wide range of materials, including Japanese books and periodicals, Japanese-language newspapers published in various parts of Asia, passport-issuance registers preserved in the Diplomatic Archives of Japan, Japanese diplomatic and consular records, the Japanese Official Gazette, Thai government documents, the Thai Royal Gazette, and Thai-language publications.

The evidence indicates that Japanese brothel operators employing karayuki-san were already present in Bangkok around 1885, before the signing of the Japanese-Siamese Declaration of Amity and Commerce on 26 September 1887. The karayuki-san thus constituted the earliest identifiable group of Japanese who established a continuing residential presence in modern Thailand. From the 1890s through the 1910s, Bangkok generally contained approximately four Japanese establishments functioning as hotels, liquor shops, coffee shops, and brothels, with approximately twenty to thirty Japanese women engaged in prostitution. Their principal customers were Westerners. Japanese karayuki-san were also present outside Bangkok, notably in Chanthaburi during the French occupation of 1893–1904 and in Phuket around 1916–1917.

The article further examines the first Japanese consular trial in Bangkok involving a Japanese prostitute in 1897; Japanese graves and gravestones at Wat Sam Chin, present-day Wat Traimit; the implementation of Siam’s Venereal Disease Prevention Act of 1908; financial contributions made by Japanese women in Bangkok during the Russo-Japanese War; and the activities of establishments such as the Asahi Hotel, Fuji Hotel, and Bangkok Hotel. Particular attention is given to the woman popularly known as the “Shanghai Old Woman” (Shanhai Bāsan), who operated the Fuji Hotel for approximately thirty years. Additional evidence incorporated from the 2024 publication makes it possible to identify her as Tsunoda Machi and to examine her activities more precisely.

The Thai case provides a distinctive perspective on the broader history of Japanese female migration and prostitution in Southeast Asia. Siam remained politically independent while operating within an international order strongly shaped by extraterritoriality and unequal treaties. The history of Japanese prostitutes in Bangkok therefore illuminates not only Japanese overseas migration and prostitution but also the interaction among foreign consular jurisdiction, Siamese administrative authority, public-health regulation, and the formation of the Japanese community in modern Thailand.

title: The Female Professional in the Age of Burnout: Gender, Hyperperformance, Emotional Labor, and the Legal Treatment of Work Architecture

detail.title: The Female Professional in the Age of Burnout: Gender, Hyperperformance, Emotional Labor, and the Legal Treatment of Work Architecture

detail.abstract: Burnout is recognised in the World Health Organization's ICD-11 as an occupational phenomenon resulting from chronic workplace stress that has not been successfully managed. The legal regimes that regulate it, however, treat gender either as irrelevant (occupational health law) or as relevant only to discrete adverse decisions (anti-discrimination law). This article asks whether, and how, existing law can reach the gendered distribution of psychosocial load among female professionals. Drawing on scholarship on burnout, gendered organizations, and emotional labor, it distinguishes three channels through which exposure to work demands may differ by sex: scrutiny-driven hyperperformance, the allocation of emotional and low-promotability work, and the interface between paid work and unequal care time. It evaluates the evidence for each channel and stresses that reported sex differences in burnout are modest and context-dependent. Through doctrinal and functional comparative analysis of Brazil, the European Union, the United Kingdom, and the United States, current to September 2026, it argues that the gendered distribution of load falls between two regulatory silos. It proposes an interpretive rather than legislative bridge: psychosocial risk-assessment duties should be read to include the distribution of work demands across groups, and detriment and indirect-discrimination doctrines should be understood to reach cumulative load allocation where organizational data show disparity. The article addresses three strong objections (the universality of burnout, preference-based explanations, and the risk of hiring avoidance) and identifies conditions under which its thesis would fail. Its contribution is doctrinal and normative; no original empirical data were collected.

title: WTO Membership and Export Carbon Emission Intensity - A Difference-in-Differences Analysis Based on Cross-Country Panel Data, 2000-2020

detail.title: WTO Membership and Export Carbon Emission Intensity - A Difference-in-Differences Analysis Based on Cross-Country Panel Data, 2000-2020
detail.abstract: This paper uses fossil CO2 emissions data from EDGAR v8.0, World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI) data, and export data, combined with official WTO accession dates, to construct an unbalanced panel of 173 economies for 2000-2020. Using difference-indifferences (DiD) and event-study methods, it examines the dynamic effect of WTO membership on a country's export carbon emission intensity. The findings show that under pooled OLS, WTO membership is significantly negatively correlated with export carbon intensity; however, after controlling for country and year fixed effects, this effect is no longer significant, and this conclusion remains robust under propensity score matching (PSM), exclusion of the China sample, winsorization, and placebo tests. Heterogeneity analysis finds no significant "pollution haven" or "technology transfer" effect, and mechanism tests show that WTO accession significantly reduced only the structural channel of industrial value-added share. These results suggest that trade liberalization per se is not the primary driver of changes in carbon intensity, and that the multilateral trading system needs to embed clearer environmental rules in order to genuinely serve green development goals.

title: The impact of social preference on information search behavior
affiliations: NHH Norwegian School of Economics - Department of Strategy and Management

detail.title: The impact of social preference on information search behavior

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I don't have any personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced the study
declarations.funderStatement: Gothenburg University and the Norwegian School of Economics

detail.abstract: In the present study it was shown that social preference plays an important role for information search behavior. This was revealed in decision tasks in which participants were deciding about candidates for a job position. An eye-tracking equipment was applied in order to register participants´ information acquisition. With regard to social preference, the results revealed that decision processing differences were more systematic between cooperators and competitors than between cooperators and individualists. Also, the cooperators did not seem to attend more to pro-environmental goals than to profit goals in the evaluation of the candidates. Finally, it was shown that accountable cooperators invested more time in their decisions than those that were not accountable, and that no such difference was observed between accountable and not accountable competitors or individualists.

title: What Does Your Interval Cover? Inference on a Generated Regressor

detail.title: What Does Your Interval Cover? Inference on a Generated Regressor

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No interest.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding.

detail.abstract: An outcome regression on a score fitted in a separate first step reports an interval centered at the coefficient of that score, which can differ from the structural coefficient we want to identify. We show how to read both parts of that difference from the printed coefficient and standard error, the variance of the score after the controls, and the score's training size and dimension. The two parts are the displacement, which averages to zero over training samples, and the attenuation, which does not. The two numbers yield an approximate coverage reading that guides the reader on whether a correction is needed and whether to adjust the variance or to obtain calibration information. No summary a report carries locates the sample in hand inside the distribution of the center over training samples, and we prove the limit. Applied to three data sets, the procedure returns coverage readings from 0.01 to 0.93, the first from the printed inputs alone and the last from a first stage in hand. Where labels can be collected, an honest split returns a set that covers the structural coefficient at any calibration rank, with the label and the outcome on separate units.

title: Post-Earnings Drift in the Point-In-Time S&P 500

detail.title: Post-Earnings Drift in the Point-In-Time S&P 500

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author owns QuanterLab UG (haftungsbeschränkt), the research platform on which the walks in this paper were run, and holds no position in any security named in the paper.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received. The work was carried out and funded by the author through QuanterLab UG (haftungsbeschränkt).

detail.abstract: Post-earnings announcement drift is the oldest anomaly in the accounting literature. Recent work reading modern large caps declared it dead. That reading forms portfolios on a fixed calendar date, weeks after the companies reported, and this paper asks whether the calendar is what died. The test runs on the S&P 500 as it stood on each anchor date from 2006 to 2025. Each company is judged on its own earnings surprise, and one surprise rule is walked twice: once with five-name baskets formed at the start of each calendar quarter, the academic cadence, and once with every name that clears a trailing-year percentile bar entered at the close of the first session its own number is public, so the two arms differ in the entry date and in how the book fills. Eleven sectors, five holding periods, two portfolio shapes. Every window was registered before it ran and frozen when it landed. Formed at quarter starts, the grid loses money after costs: a sector-partitioned, five-name form of the calendar design agrees with the death notice without being the index-wide portfolio it was read on. Entered on the announcement, the same rule makes money, peaks inside two weeks and is gone by the quarter, the decay Bernard and Thomas measured in 1989. Entering on the announcement beat forming at the quarter start in 37 of the 45 cells of the nine sectors with a full record, and in eight of the nine sectors. A second grid asks who carries it, cutting the index by how predictable a company's earnings are and how profitable it is. Unhedged, predictable earners beat erratic ones widely, the answer the earnings-volatility literature would have predicted. The predictable portfolio ran net long and the erratic one net short through a rising market. Charged that exposure daily, the gap closes. What is left is a small announcement premium that costs already eat into, and a short leg that lost in every cohort. The record: 301 registered walk-forwards, 6,020 sealed one-year windows, 5,583 walked to a frozen report, 437 refused by a declared fifteen-name floor and printed as exclusions, and two declared search families of 220 and 81.

title: Off the Majors List: Legal Architecture, Historical Practice, and the Prospective Security Consequences of Venezuela's 2026 Drug-Certification Reversal

detail.title: Off the Majors List: Legal Architecture, Historical Practice, and the Prospective Security Consequences of Venezuela's 2026 Drug-Certification Reversal

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author discloses no financial relationship with any government, sanctioned individual, financial institution, or organization discussed in this paper that could be perceived to have influenced the study. The author discloses a non-financial professional background relevant to the subject matter: he is a former Venezuelan public prosecutor and the founder of a security consultancy (LISE) that publishes commentary and working papers on Venezuelan organized crime, security, and financial-crime topics, including the three prior LISE working papers cited in Section VIII of this manuscript. declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author through the Latino Institute for Security Efficiency (LISE), without grant support, sponsorship, or financial contribution from any government, organization, or third party.

detail.abstract: On September 16, 2026, the United States removed Venezuela from the category of countries that "failed demonstrably" to meet their counternarcotics obligations under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, a status Venezuela had held for twenty consecutive years. This working paper examines what that reversal legally constitutes, situates it within four decades of certification practice since the 1986 Anti-Drug Abuse Act, and asks what a limited body of political-question jurisprudence suggests about the reviewability of the determination. It then places the legal change against a concentrated cluster of enforcement and financial events in the same week: the Federal Bureau of Investigation's confirmed capture of the final name on its ten-most-wanted list, a Venezuelan national tied to financing Tren de Aragua through automated teller machine fraud; the guilty plea and cooperation agreement of Alex Saab, a central financial operator of the prior government; and sworn testimony from the Secretary of the Treasury acknowledging that the United States is receiving billions of dollars in Venezuela-linked assets without being able to identify, under direct questioning, where those funds are ultimately flowing. The paper argues that the certification reversal and the sanctions and asset-forfeiture authorities under which those enforcement actions proceed are legally distinct tracks that do not automatically activate one another, a distinction largely absent from contemporaneous commentary. It offers a framework, grounded in the certification process's own institutional history, for distinguishing what the reversal enables as a matter of law from what remains, eight months into a still-forming bilateral relationship, a matter of observed pattern rather than settled architecture.

title: Individual-plant maize phenotyping from UAV RGB and multispectral imagery using geospatial label transfer
affiliations: Northwest A&F University, Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Beijing Forestry University

detail.title: Individual-plant maize phenotyping from UAV RGB and multispectral imagery using geospatial label transfer
detail.abstract: Traditional UAV-based crop remote sensing phenotyping predominantly relies on plot-scale averages, limiting the characterization of individual-plant growth differences and intra-plot spatial heterogeneity. To address this, we propose an individual-plant maize phenotyping framework integrating UAV RGB and multispectral imagery. First, standardized plot segmentation and multi-temporal spatial alignment were achieved via geospatial label transfer, with an alignment error of 2–3 pixels (3–5 cm). Second, an improved point-supervised P2PNet model localized maize canopy centers in RGB imagery, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 3.22 and an F1-score of 0.88. Plant coordinates were geographically transferred to multispectral imagery, where individual-plant NDVI was extracted using an NDVI-Otsu vegetation mask and a dynamic region-of-interest (ROI) strategy. Results demonstrated that individual-plant NDVI effectively captured seasonal growth dynamics, peaking at 0.7277 on July 21st. Crucially, individual-level analysis revealed significant intra-plot spatial heterogeneity: inner-row plants consistently exhibited higher NDVI than outer-row plants, with the difference peaking at 0.0320. Furthermore, the population coefficient of variation (CV) evolved from 4.45% during canopy expansion to 10.35% during late-stage senescence, capturing a "variation—homogenization—differentiation" uniformity process. This framework advances plot-scale monitoring to the individual-plant level, providing a robust pathway for evaluating field trial phenotypes, correcting edge biases, and enabling precision management.

title: Does Violent Crime Affect Inflation Volatility? Evidence from South America

detail.title: Does Violent Crime Affect Inflation Volatility? Evidence from South America

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether violent crime contributes to inflation volatility by analysing the relationship between homicide rates and macroeconomic stability across South American economies between 2003 and 2015. While a substantial body of literature documents the adverse effects of violent crime on investment, productivity, and economic growth, comparatively little attention has been given to its potential influence on nominal macroeconomic outcomes. Using a panel dataset of seven South American countries, the analysis employs a two-way fixed effects framework to estimate the relationship between homicide rates and inflation volatility, while controlling for key macroeconomic, monetary, fiscal, and institutional factors. The paper further investigates whether this relationship operates through the shadow economy or government expenditure by incorporating interaction effects and assesses the robustness of the findings using alternative model specifications. The results provide no evidence of a statistically significant relationship between homicide rates and inflation volatility, either directly or through the proposed transmission channels. These findings suggest that, within the sample examined, violent crime influences macroeconomic outcomes primarily through real economic channels rather than nominal price dynamics, contributing to a more nuanced understanding of the relationship between social instability and macroeconomic stability.

title: Expected Returns and Business Cycle Synchronization
affiliations: Norwegian Business School and Aarhus University - CREATES

detail.abstract: We construct expected-return-based measures of stock market integration using a consumption habit model. A country is fully integrated when only global consumption surplus carries information about its expected return, while partial integration arises when local consumption surplus retains predictive content. Time-varying predictive coefficients reveal an upward trend in integration among developed markets and erratic dynamics among emerging markets, which remain less globally integrated but exhibit stronger regional integration. Tests show that stock market integration and business-cycle synchronization are positively associated across countries, and over time, an association that complete-markets real business cycle models do not capture.

title: Mass segregation review as a permanent fiscal-balance instrument in Brazilian public servants' pension schemes (RPPS): the structural surplus of the Funded Account
affiliations: Center for Finance and Retail Studies, FIA Business School,  and University of Sao Paulo, Retail Management Program

detail.title: Mass segregation review as a permanent fiscal-balance instrument in Brazilian public servants' pension schemes (RPPS): the structural surplus of the Funded Account

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The studies that make up the corpus of this article were prepared under the technical responsibility of the first author, an actuary, in the course of actuarial consulting work for the public servants' pension schemes examined, hired by the entities directly or through foundations and consulting firms. The analysis relies on technical documents prepared for the schemes, on regulations, and on public data, with no individual membership data, and the studies are not attributed to the consulting firms or foundations that were hired, since their results, and not the technical authorship, are the object of the examination. There was no specific funding for this research.
declarations.funderStatement: There was no specific funding for this research.

detail.abstract: In previous work by the authors, it was shown that mass segregation adjusts the financial regime of Brazilian public servants' pension schemes (RPPS) by funding the inherited liability on a pay-as-you-go basis and capitalizing only the group formed under the reformed rules. This article tests the sustainability of that architecture over time and confronts the objection that segregation would burden the entity in the long run. Through documentary analysis of 22 technical documents from 14 RPPS across five federative units, prepared between 2017 and 2026 and covering 20 review processes, and through longitudinal comparisons between projected and observed figures, three findings emerge. First, the Funded Account was in surplus in 13 of the 14 cases, with observed coverage ratios from 108.8% to 319.5%; the single exception, contaminated at implementation by members entitled to full final-salary benefits and parity, confirms the explanatory variable. Second, the actuarial result found in the funded account exceeded the one expected from the previous valuation in the five comparable cases, by ratios of 2.4 to 7.7 times in constant currency where the starting surplus was material, a pattern compatible with the conservatism of liability assumptions, although higher contribution rates and changes of assumptions prevent isolating its share; with the reviews, the observed or projected insufficiency fell below the previous projection for the same fiscal years. Third, the reviews, currently governed by article 62 of Ordinance MTP No. 1,467/2022, convert the surplus of the funded account into relief of 20.7% to 100% of the first-year insufficiency, and the surplus rebuilds after each transfer. The conclusion is that segregation combined with periodic review forms a permanent fiscal-balance architecture, incompatible with sizing amortization plans on single-mass schemes.

title: The AI Economy: Adoption, Human Validation, and Labor Demand
affiliations: Autonomous University of Barcelona

detail.title: The AI Economy: Adoption, Human Validation, and Labor Demand

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I have no conflicting personal or financial relationships related to this study.

detail.abstract: I study how human validation requirements shape the response of wages and labor demand to AI adoption. I introduce fixed, recurring validation labor into a general equilibrium task model with endogenous AI adoption. It features a validation threshold determining whether the labor created by AI adoption offsets the productive labor it displaces after accounting for demand expansions. I estimate the model using U.S. occupation-task data on human versus AI involvement at work, and AI adoption rates. The estimated U.S. validation requirement lies below the threshold, implying that productive labor displacement dominates and wages fall. For the occupations in the estimation sample, a ten year projection of declining AI costs raises adoption from 18 to 62 percent and nearly triples output, while reducing employment by 13 percent and wages by 43 percent. Extending the exercise to the entire U.S. economy attenuates the employment and wage declines to 5 and 18 percent, respectively.

title: Educator AI Literacy as Praxis in GenAI-Supported ESP Materials Development
affiliations: and École Supérieure d'Ingénieurs en Électrotechnique et Électronique (ESIEE)

detail.title: Educator AI Literacy as Praxis in GenAI-Supported ESP Materials Development

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interests
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is creating uncertainty about how educators should design, evaluate, and adapt teaching materials while developing the professional knowledge needed to use these systems responsibly. This practice-based qualitative case study examines how educator AI literacy was enacted as praxis during six months of AI-assisted English for Specific Purposes (ESP) curriculum development at a business school in France. Data were drawn from reflexive logs, curriculum artifacts, prompt archives, advisory feedback, and an anonymous learner survey combining open-text and structured responses. Inductive thematic analysis showed AI-literacy practices becoming visible through contextual framing, prompting, critical appraisal, epistemic validation, differentiated materials design, manual revision, and learner-oriented refinement. Prompting also became more economical as recurring Reader patterns stabilized; this is interpreted as a feature of increasingly routinized design practice. The study formalizes the documented process through a six-layer Human-AI Collaboration Model and a recursive AI-literacy-as-praxis cycle. The resulting heuristic foregrounds educator judgment, pedagogical accountability, and curriculum stewardship as practical responses to continuing GenAI uncertainty.

title: Predicting AI's Impact on Labor Is a Core Machine Learning Problem
affiliations: University of Notre Dame

detail.title: Predicting AI's Impact on Labor Is a Core Machine Learning Problem

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly reshaping how work is performed, organized, and valued. Predicting AI's impact on labor is an interdisciplinary scientific question that examines how evolving AI capabilities interact with adoption, organizational change, and political and economic adjustments to reshape work and labor. This paper argues that predicting AI's impact on labor is a core problem for the AI and ML community to engage with, not solely a societal or ethical question, and that ML has a distinctive role to play in the broader interdisciplinary agenda. Questions at the center of modern AI and ML research, such as prediction under nonstationarity, distribution shift, endogenous feedback, and LLM-based agent simulation, are also core questions of economics and social science. This paper reviews current approaches in economics, management, and ML, identifies technical obstacles that limit existing prediction methods, and proposes a research agenda for AI-and ML-driven labor prediction.

title: Strategic Stability in the Technology Domain: Disciplining the Use of Trade and Investment Restrictions
affiliations: University of New South Wales | China International Business and Economic Law (CIBEL) Center

detail.title: Strategic Stability in the Technology Domain: Disciplining the Use of Trade and Investment Restrictions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author previously served as Vice President of Global Government Affairs at Huawei. He is the founder of Market Access X, an independent trade intelligence and advisory service whose clients include organizations with interests in trade and technology policy. The author has no current financial relationship with any company, government or organization whose measures are discussed in this paper. The views expressed are the author's own.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding. It develops remarks delivered at the 12th International Affairs Summer Forum of the University of International Business and Economics (UIBE), Beijing, in July 2026.

detail.abstract: Governments in Washington, Brussels, Beijing and elsewhere now treat economic security as synonymous with national security, and restrictions on trade in and investment into technology have multiplied accordingly. This paper makes three arguments. First, trade and security were never completely separate domains; what ended was a quarter-century bet that closer economic integration with a rival would render security claims redundant. Second, the obvious legal discipline, the least-trade-restrictive-alternative test that the WTO applies under the TBT and SPS Agreements and GATT Article XX, cannot be carried over to the security exception: Article XXI reserves the judgment of necessity to the invoking state, the first panel to interpret it imposed only a minimal objective standard of review, and the Member whose invocations have been most extensively litigated, the United States, refuses to accept even that. Third, what remains available is a self-binding discipline grounded in the logic of strategic stability. In this paper, I propose five criteria of restraint (specificity, nexus, least-restrictive-available, reversibility and transparency) that a state should be willing both to apply to its own measures and to have others apply to them. The paper closes by arguing that the greater danger lies not in governments invoking security cynically, which is relatively easy to expose, but in fears that are genuinely held yet have no natural limit, so that the range of technologies treated as critical to national security keeps expanding without anyone necessarily acting in bad faith.

title: When Financial Stress Is Not Bistable: A Calibration of the Cusp-Catastrophe Framework

detail.abstract: Financial stress exhibits nonlinear dynamics. The cusp-catastrophe framework predicts bistability, with a closed-form escape time. Calibrating to U.S. financial stress data (1993-2026), with crisis windows 2007-2009 and 2019-2020, the bistability condition fails under normal crisis parameters. Bistability requires a transmission efficiency far above observed levels. The framework describes an extreme regime, not the ordinary crisis regime. The threshold at which bistability emerges is the contribution.

title: Agreement and Unawareness under Misinterpreted Evidence

detail.title: Agreement and Unawareness under Misinterpreted Evidence

detail.abstract: Agreement and no-speculation can survive systematic misinterpretation of evidence. On a finite state space, actual signals and their interpreted meanings form two matched partitions. Non-deludedness requires their encodings to agree pointwise; mass balance requires agreement in distribution. Mass balance restores partitional common belief and an Aumann-style agreement theorem despite individual failures of truth and introspection. The ordinary informationpartition theorem is a special case. Once the interpretation rules admit a full-support balancing measure, agreement and the stated no-speculation conclusion are robust to changes in the shared conditioning measure. More generally, a sharp bound controls disagreement by the balance defect relative to the probability of the common-belief region. We also study symmetric higher-order ignorance: under partition range, global KU requires at least five states for nontriviality, while an inclusion-antichain range rules out Boolean closure of awareness. A contracting game links these interpretation errors to strict speculative trade and identifies a second-order belief obstruction to commonly believed execution. All constructions use ordinary events and probability measures on one state space.

title: Climate Management Practices and Market Valuation: The Price of (In)credibility
affiliations: , Université Côte d’Azur and University of Paris

detail.title: Climate Management Practices and Market Valuation: The Price of (In)credibility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Chaire Énergie et Prospérité, under the aegis of the Fondation du Risque, hosted by the Institut Louis Bachelier.

detail.abstract: This study explores to what extent the implementation of managerial Climate Management Practices (CMP) adopted by large publicly traded firms is associated with Corporate Financial Performance (CFP), measured by Tobin's Q. The purpose is to assess whether financial markets perceive CMP as value-enhancing. Based on a panel of 298 firms from the S&P 500 and STOXX Europe 600 (2019-2022), we test eight CMP using regression models that include industry-year fixed effects and robust standard errors. The analysis differentiates between internal managerial CMP (Management Tools) and external managerial CMP (Transparency Practices). The results show that most CMP are not significantly linked to Tobin's Q, implying that markets largely view them as neutral with respect to value creation. Two exceptions emerge: (i) Environmental Management System certification, which correlates negatively with firm value, indicating investor skepticism about its cost-benefit balance; and (ii) greenhouse gas reduction targets, where weak commitments are penalized while ambitious goals are rewarded. These findings indicate that investors place value exclusively on practices perceived as both credible and ambitious. We complement the analysis with a risk-based proxy (𝛽) reflecting short-term market risk perceptions, which supports the previous results. These findings offer practical insights for managers, investors, and regulators, highlighting how climate management practices can be structured to better align with evolving market expectations.

title: Can a Language Model Keep a Tax Lot Straight? A Rules-Grounded Benchmark for Wash-Sale, Holding-Period and Lot-Relief Decisions

detail.title: Can a Language Model Keep a Tax Lot Straight? A Rules-Grounded Benchmark for Wash-Sale, Holding-Period and Lot-Relief Decisions

detail.abstract: Advisers who run tax-aware separately managed accounts are starting to put languagemodel assistants in front of questions such as whether a loss sale is a wash sale, what a replacement lot's basis becomes, whether a gain is short-or long-term, and which lots a trim should sell. Each has one right answer under IRS Publication 550. We build a 193-item benchmark of these decisions with exact answers from a small deterministic rules engine that reproduces every worked example in the publication it relies on. Most items are random samples of the decisions a simulated household's direct-indexing account faced in a simulated 2025, across the client's own accounts, her IRAs, her spouse's account and an adult child's account; the rest sit on the boundaries the rules draw. Local open-weight models and one hosted model answer in four settings: closed-book, with the governing rules quoted, by writing a program, and by only transcribing the trades for the engine. Unaided, the two local models that answered every item got 13% and 23% of them right, and quoting the rules helped little; the hosted model answered 31 of 35 subset items. With the decision delegated to the engine, the local models reached 98% and 100% and the hosted model 35 of 35. Version 2 asks whether the engine is more than the problem needs: a model could instead answer under the constraints themselves. Accounting identities that every correct answer satisfies, and that need no tax rule to check, reject 72% of the small models' closed-book errors and one of the hosted model's eleven, and moving a rejected answer to the nearest admissible one seldom makes it right. Wrong answers are attributed to named misconceptions where one reproduces them, and priced on the simulated household, where an unaided small model would misstate the year's tax by about three times the tax value of the year's harvest. For an adviser the practical conclusion is to use a model to read documents and the engine to make the call.

title: From Marshallian Equilibrium to Price Regions: An Empirical Generalization of the Equilibrium Price

detail.title: From Marshallian Equilibrium to Price Regions: An Empirical Generalization of the Equilibrium Price

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: The Marshallian framework represents market equilibrium as a point: a single price and quantity at which supply and demand intersect. Yet retail markets frequently exhibit persistent price dispersion, with identical products simultaneously offered and transacted at multiple prices. This paper asks what the empirical counterpart of the equilibrium price is when the market does not exhibit a single realized price. We propose a price-region equilibrium framework in which the conventional equilibrium price P* is generalized to a bounded region R^E, while point equilibrium remains embedded as the limiting case as persistent price dispersion approaches zero. Using store-level scanner data from five retail categories, we define a focal price as the price at which seller presence is greatest and construct concentration curves measuring how seller presence, realized transactions, and revenue accumulate as the region expands outward from that focal center. The focal price alone contains at least half of realized transactions in the median product-week system. The median width required to encompass 90% of transactions ranges from approximately ±5% in cereals to approximately ±8-10% in laundry products, paper towels, shampoo, and canned tuna. At a common ±5% bandwidth, the region captures approximately 69-80% of realized transactions on average across categories. Transaction concentration closely tracks seller concentration, so concentration itself is not interpreted as evidence of market clearing. Instead, the results reveal a measurable and heterogeneous regional geometry of realized exchange. The price-region framework does not replace point equilibrium; it generalizes its empirical representation from a point to a region.

title: Lexical Overfitting in Zero-Shot Retinal Diagnosis: A Study of Medical Vision-Language Models
affiliations: Ajman University, Ajman University of Science and Technology and Ajman University

detail.title: Lexical Overfitting in Zero-Shot Retinal Diagnosis: A Study of Medical Vision-Language Models
detail.abstract: The shift to multimodal Vision-Language Models (VLMs) theoretically promises improved robustness against visual data leakage vulnerabilities of convolutional architectures via aligning retinal pathology with existing medical semantics. Nevertheless, zero-shot application assumes that these models achieve genuine cross-modal reasoning rather than shallow text token-matching. To differentiate visual-semantic reasoning from gradient-driven memorization, we conducted strictly-frozen inference on the FLAIR retinal foundation model using 1,744 MESSIDOR-2 fundus images. We developed an automated high-concurrency Unified Medical Language System (UMLS) sanitization pipeline for enforcing absolute semantic neutrality and ensuring the removal of latent medical ontologies from both lay language prompts and exclusionary evaluation texts. Semantic perturbation resulted in cross-modal collapse. While baseline prompts limited only to labels yielded 56.18% accuracy (Expected Calibration Error [ECE]: 4.45%), UMLS-sanitization of expert terms to lay language dropped the performance to 29.62% (ECE: 38.70%). Further application of negative logical operators dropped the accuracy to 26.90% (ECE: 36.15%), resulting in the emergence of a 24.0% class-conditional false positive rate for Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy diagnosis among completely normal eyes merely due to the presence of pathological text tokens. Current medical Vision-Language Models (VLMs) suffer significantly from lexical overfitting and operate as fragile bags-of-words rather than reasoning agents. Under semantic perturbation, they exhibit epistemic arrogance -- a potentially fatal property in a clinical context that allows the model architecture to hide biological illiteracy from the end-user under a facade of mathematically unjustified statistical overconfidence.

detail.abstract: Uzbekistan's IT Park residency framework is often described primarily through its tax incentives, but its legal structure is broader. It is a status-based and conditional system of public-law preferences that combines tax and customs advantages with labour, foreign-exchange, export and organizational facilitations, while simultaneously restricting the resident to approved activities and to the substantive business plan on which residency was granted. This article examines that framework through the specific case of item 21 of the list of activities permitted for IT Park residents: venture financing of projects in the field of information technologies and implementation of acceleration programs. The central argument is that item 21 cannot be understood as a purely formal activity code. In the qualification process, item 21 operates through two distinct pathways-venture financing and acceleration-requiring materially different substantive disclosures. For venture financing, the analysis centres on the legal and economic structure of investment activity, including a venture-fund agreement, exit strategy, beneficiaries, management, investment stages, ticket range, committed capital and funded projects. For acceleration, it centres on the program itself, its curriculum, duration, frequency, mentors, partners, investment outcomes and portfolio of participating projects. Where both pathways are selected, both substantive models must be demonstrated. The article further analyses organizational capacity and the evidentiary relationship among the business plan, corporate documents, contracts, accounting records and actual operations. It concludes that the decisive qualification principle is coherence: residency under item 21 depends not on the label 'venture fund' or 'accelerator', but on whether the applicant can present a unified, economically credible and verifiable business model corresponding to the chosen activity and capable of being implemented by its organization.

detail.abstract: On May 13, 2024, GameStop surged nearly 74% in a single trading session after “Roaring Kitty” returned to social media. No major earnings release or product launch explained the scale of the move. Instead, millions of online users suddenly turned their attention toward the same stock. This paper investigates whether concentrated digital attention can amplify market volatility and, crucially, how such an effect can be measured. To examine this, the study develops an original metric, the Attention-Volatility Elasticity (AVE), and applies it across three distinct 2024 market shockwaves: the GameStop meme-stock rally, the Indian Union Budget, and U.S. presidential election-related uncertainty. The GameStop analysis reveals a 667% increase in volatility above its baseline during the event window, alongside an extraordinary surge in trading volume. Google Trends data also show a strong positive association between search interest and absolute daily returns. Comparing these episodes highlights an important distinction: digital attention can intensify and accelerate market reactions, but its effects operate alongside fundamental, institutional, and political information. The findings suggest that in increasingly digital markets, attention is not merely a by-product of price movements-it can become a powerful amplifier of them.

detail.abstract: Changes in international market access reshape agricultural incentives, but their consequences for native vegetation depend on adjustments across trading partners, competing land uses, and production locations. We examine how trade integration and tariff rivalry affect land conversion in South America under contrasting socioeconomic and climate conditions. A recursive dynamic computable general equilibrium model is linked to a spatial model of conversion in the Amazon, Cerrado, Gran Chaco, and Pantanal through 2040. We compare European Union-Mercosur tariff preferences alone and in combination with tariff rivalry involving China and the United States. Total conversion reaches about 398,000 km2 under SSP1 and 557,000 km2 under SSP3, but the trade-induced increment is larger under SSP1, at 14,200 km2 compared with 6,600 km2 under SSP3. In SSP1, 88% of the trade increment falls in the Amazon and Cerrado. The agreement alone produces a similar concentration under SSP3, while rivalry shifts part of the effect toward the Chaco and reduces additional conversion by about 3,200 km2. Trade also accelerates conversion on land that would otherwise be converted later, with a median shift of one year. Growing land demand is accommodated mainly through expansion of aggregate supply, while trade primarily changes which activities expand and where conversion occurs. These results show that bilateral agreements cannot be evaluated independently of the wider trade environment and that long-run assessments may miss near-term conversion accelerated by policy changes.

detail.abstract: High-stakes public decisions increasingly place algorithmic benchmarks alongside human judgment, changing not only who decides but the form that discretion takes. We examine how this relationship shapes public evaluation. Three randomized survey experiments embedded in a four-wave panel in China investigate AI-assisted judicial sentencing and its governance. In the main experiment (N = 2,336), AI recommendations received more favorable evaluations when judges retained substantive discretion. A follow-up experiment holding the offense and benchmark constant shows that AI increased perceived reasonableness when discretion mitigated punishment but reduced it when discretion aggravated punishment. An exploratory governance experiment further suggests that formal constraint and procedural transparency shape different dimensions of institutional evaluation. Together, the findings establish human–AI configuration as a distinct object of public evaluation: algorithmic guidance is judged in relation to the substantive role retained for human discretion. AI-assisted decision-making thus recasts a classic problem of administrative discretion under algorithmic governance.

detail.abstract: Does a central bank's outstanding forward position change how U.S. monetary policy shocks move its exchange rate? Mark-to-market losses and rollover costs on a net short dollar position reduce central bank's net worth and its capacity to lean against depreciation. Using Federal Reserve policy shocks orthogonalized to public macro-financial information, this paper shows that a given tightening shock depreciates Indian rupee more when the inherited forward position is larger. This amplification peaks 17 trading days after the FOMC announcement and is strongest for contracts maturing in one to twelve months, consistent with a rollover channel. It operates as a regime shift rather than a dose response and appears only above a threshold near zero net exposure where a one-standard-deviation shock depreciates the rupee by 0.9 percentage points. The forward position itself accumulates reactively—one percentage point of past depreciation predicts a $55.8 billion larger net short position across the three preceding announcements—creating a self-reinforcing cycle. Forward commitments thus act as a central-bank financial accelerator, creating contingent liabilities that standard reserve adequacy metrics do not observe. The exchange-rate consequences depend on the inherited stock of forward positions as much as on spot intervention flows.

detail.abstract: Modern industrial supply chains operate under conditions of geopolitical uncertainty, infrastructure constraints, and nonlinear operational risks. Energy-intensive petrochemical projects are particularly vulnerable because their economic performance depends on continuous availability of upstream feedstock, transportation infrastructure, and demand balancing mechanisms. This paper studies the application of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to improve resilience and economic performance in the Tengiz–Sileno ethane corridor in Kazakhstan. The Sileno gas-chemical complex is a strategic petrochemical project designed to produce approximately 1.25 million tonnes of polyethylene annually. Its production depends on ethane supplied from the Tengiz field through a gas separation complex and two 210-km pipelines. The research develops an integrated artificial intelligence decision-support framework combining a physics-based industrial simulator, a Deep Q-Network (DQN) controller, and a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) forecasting model. The simulator incorporates pipeline pressure dynamics, hydrate risks, emergency venting, buffer inventory, import constraints, and regional demand requirements. The proposed system was tested through 100 simulation episodes covering 365 operating days. The best-performing DQN configuration generated approximately +$91 million annual P&L compared with approximately −$1.1 billion under a random operational strategy. Reinforcement learning eliminated simulated downtime completely and reduced operational uncertainty. The TFT forecasting model achieved a MAPE of 2.14% and RMSE of 1.65 mcm. The contribution of this research is the development of a physics-grounded DRL framework that connects industrial operational decisions with measurable financial outcomes. The framework demonstrates how artificial intelligence can support resilience planning in critical energy infrastructure.

detail.abstract: We study optimal consumption and investment with asymmetric proportional costs on changes in consumption utility in an incomplete market driven by a fast stochastic-volatility factor. For general smooth utility, the averaged-market problem admits an explicit dual integral representation: two utility-independent thresholds determine the marginal-utility inaction region, while utility curvature enters through the transformation to wealth. The resulting reflected feedback strategy has a value expansion through the square-root timescale correction, with an error of the order of the timescale parameter. Under smooth power-tail conditions and a Sharpe ratio bounded away from zero, a gradient-preserving dual supersolution gives an optimality gap of the same order over all admissible strategies. Under additional local marginal regularity, nondegeneracy, and matching assumptions, a conditional boundary theorem identifies a canonical marginal layer, its invariant-mean displacement, and the transfer from profile error to trigger error. Numerical cell solutions show that factor-dependent trigger oscillations can greatly exceed the invariant-mean correction and persist at zero correlation. Infinite downward-adjustment cost yields consumption ratcheting, with risk tolerance proportional to wealth above the perpetuity cost of current consumption. The large-penalty limit is nonuniform: values converge at fixed feasible states, but finitecost consumption-decrease triggers approach a level strictly below the ratcheting solvency floor. Exact first-passage formulas and reproducible calculations quantify adjustment timing, endogenous risk aversion, wealth-equivalent rigidity costs, and volatility effects.

detail.abstract: We study finite-horizon reversible investment when the economic state follows a geometric Brownian motion with compound-Poisson jumps and remaining capacity is liquidated at maturity. Cobb-Douglas homogeneity reduces the marginal problem to a one-dimensional parabolic integro-differential double-obstacle problem. We establish Sobolev regularity and smooth fit, and prove that both free boundaries are continuously differentiable, with higher regularity under additional assumptions on the jump density. Integrating switching values over capacity layers recovers the original value function and verifies an optimal capacity policy: reflection between moving boundaries with projection after jump overshoots. Numerical experiments separately assess discretization, jump-integration, and domain errors and examine the effects of jump risk and adjustment prices.

detail.abstract: Do state minimum-wage increases affect SNAP participation? While earnings gains can lift family income above eligibility thresholds, lost hours and unemployment can push families onto the program. Prior studies on this question disagree on the sign and rely exclusively on state-panel two-way fixed effects (TWFE). Using minimum wage increases of at least $1 during 2000-2019, we estimate stacked event studies comparing each increase with states whose effective minimum wage remained unchanged during the same period. We show nearly half of the implicit comparisons in the TWFE design are contaminated by already-treated states, and correcting for this reverses their positive finding. Across the full population, we find no meaningful effect on either the extensive margin of participation or the intensive margin of benefit amounts. Restricting to families most likely to be near program eligibility, using a demographic screen built from pre-period data, participation rises modestly but the effect remains statistically insignificant. The response is largest in the first year after an increase, before fading, and pre-trends are flat. Reweighting households by their likelihood of treatment yields a similar pattern.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a time-varying signature asset model for structural credit. We represent the logarithm of the discounted firm value as a finite linear functional of the time-augmented Itô signature, with deterministic loadings that vary with the horizon. We derive sufficient coefficient restrictions under which the exponential specification is a strictly positive Q-local martingale. We embed the process in a fixed-boundary first-passage model, so that CDS spreads, equity values, and equity option prices are generated by the same latent firm-value dynamics. Using 52,639 daily CDS curves, we find that our model substantially improves calibration across maturities. It also delivers the lowest pooled errors in a cross-market validation using equity implied volatilities, with the strongest gains among high-yield firms.

detail.title: The Minimum Wage and Informality Model in Albania

detail.abstract:
This study examines the relationship between minimum wages, labour productivity, informality, and employment in Albania over the period 2015–2025 by combining econometric analysis, counterfactual simulation, and regional comparison. The theoretical framework is based on the function LM = f(MW, INF, PROD, FORMC, LABS, EMIG) and integrates data from INSTAT, the Ministry of Finance, the Social Insurance Institute, OECD, the World Bank, and ALTAX. The empirical analysis employs Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regressions, alternative time-trend specifications, distributed-lag models, instrumental-variable estimation (IV/2SLS), and a counterfactual simulation assessing the impact of increasing the statutory minimum wage from ALL 40,000 to ALL 50,000 in 2026.

The findings indicate that historical evidence does not reveal a statistically significant relationship between minimum wage increases and unemployment. However, when minimum wages grow faster than labour productivity, the risk of expanding informality increases, particularly in low-productivity sectors. The counterfactual simulation estimates that the informal economy could expand by approximately 1.1–3.0 percentage points depending on alternative elasticity assumptions, while sectoral evidence identifies agriculture as the most vulnerable sector to informality pressures. The study also highlights the relevance of the Kaitz Index and the minimum wage–productivity relationship as key structural constraints for wage-setting policies.

Despite limitations arising from the small sample size and the absence of official time-series data on informality, the study proposes an evidence-based policy package including productivity-linked minimum wage indexation, reductions in labour formalization costs, sector-specific transition mechanisms, and stronger formalization policies prior to further administrative increases in the minimum wage.

title: DeepD Enables Efficient Genome Modeling and Controllable Long-Context Sequence Generation Across Domains of Life
affiliations: China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, BioMap Research, China Agricultural University, BioMap Research, BioMap Research, China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, China Agricultural University, University of Oxford, Yazhouwan National Laboratory, BioMap Research and China Agricultural University

detail.title: DeepD Enables Efficient Genome Modeling and Controllable Long-Context Sequence Generation Across Domains of Life
detail.abstract: Genome foundation models hold great potential for biological research, but modeling diverse complex genomes and generating controllable genome-scale sequences remain challenging. We present DeepD, a phylogeny-informed sparse mixture-of-experts model operating at single-nucleotide resolution with a 1-million-token context and reduced active computation. Pretrained on unselected whole genomes across all domains of life, DeepD learns genic and intergenic features and supports cross-species sequence-to-function prediction. DeepD performs well in protein fitness and disease-variant effect prediction in human, including BRCA1 and BRCA2, with particular strength in promoters and transcription-factor binding sites. Expert routing captures exon–intron boundaries, transposable elements, and distal cis-regulatory elements. DeepD generates experimentally validated maize core promoters with specified strengths. Its Context–Anchor–Body strategy generates complete yeast chromosomes and megabase-scale Arabidopsis segments, preserving gene structure and order while introducing natural-range variation. DeepD thus unifies accurate prediction with controllable genome-scale generation, advancing the predictive and generative design of complex genomes.

detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the welfare effects of price parity clauses (PPCs) when platform commissions differ. PPCs are shown to lower the weighted posted price under convex commission pass-through, but need not increase consumer surplus. Because commissions are transfers rather than technological costs, PPCs eliminate the consumption misallocation induced by platform-specific pricing and can increase total welfare, even when their consumer-surplus effect is negative. We provide sufficient conditions, in terms of demand elasticity and curvature, under which PPCs increase consumer surplus and total welfare.

title: Public Financial Management and the Implementation of Health Financing Reform: A Conceptual Contribution to Addressing the Missing Link
affiliations: , World Health Organization (WHO) - World Health Organization Cameroon and World Bank

detail.title: Public Financial Management and the Implementation of Health Financing Reform: A Conceptual Contribution to Addressing the Missing Link
detail.abstract: Public financial management (PFM) systems play a critical role in determining whether health financing reforms are implemented effectively and contribute to progress toward universal health coverage (UHC). However, health financing analyses have often treated PFM as an external constraint rather than as a fundamental determinant of reform feasibility, implementation, and performance. This paper examines how PFM institutions, rules, and processes interact with the core health financing functions of revenue raising, pooling, and purchasing. Drawing on a critical review of health financing and PFM frameworks, a structured synthesis of the literature on PFM in health, and illustrative country experiences, we identify the mechanisms through which PFM shapes the implementation of health financing reforms. The analysis demonstrates that budget formulation, classification, approval, execution, reporting, and oversight influence the predictability, flexibility, efficiency, and accountability of public spending for health. Rigid line-item budgeting, fragmented funding arrangements, delayed fund releases, limited provider financial autonomy, and weak integration of financial and performance information can undermine reforms intended to expand coverage and strengthen financial protection. Evidence from Peru, Kyrgyzstan, and Burkina Faso illustrates that the effectiveness of health financing reforms depends on the alignment between health financing objectives and PFM arrangements. We argue that strengthening collaboration between ministries of health and finance, adapting budget structures to support output-oriented spending, improving budget execution, and reinforcing performance-informed accountability are essential for translating health financing reforms into sustainable progress toward UHC.
