detail.abstract: Modern clinical research has produced striking advances in both Alzheimer's disease and cancer: the first disease-modifying Alzheimer's therapies, and an accelerating shift toward biomarker-gated precision oncology. Whether these advances reflect the global populations who carry the burden of these diseases, however, has rarely been measured directly rather than assumed. This monograph investigates that question using an original, purpose-built dataset: 400 interventional trials (200 per disease) randomly sampled from ClinicalTrials.gov, coded against a six-category exclusion-criteria taxonomy and scored using TREI-AC, an adaptation of the Trial Representation Equity Index built specifically for this comparison. Across the sample, 99.5% of Alzheimer's disease trials and 97.8% of cancer trials had no site in a country classified as low- or lower-middle-income by the World Bank; a two-tier comparison against disease-burden data shows trial-site presence in these countries running roughly 44 to 54 percentage points below their share of global disease burden for both conditions. Comorbidity and prior-treatment exclusion criteria were significantly more common in cancer trials than in Alzheimer's disease trials. In contrast, biomarker or imaging diagnostic requirements present in 15 to 16% of trials in both diseases structurally gate a meaningful share of research access behind infrastructure much of the world lacks. A dedicated case study of India-sited trials further distinguishes between an extractive pattern, in which a country functions only as a recruitment site within externally designed trials, and a domestic-research pattern largely disconnected from that same pipeline. Building on these findings, the monograph traces the same structural gap through diagnosis, treatment, affordability, pharmacovigilance, regulatory science, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence across the clinical research lifecycle, before proposing a ten-pillar Equity-by-Design framework and a disease-specific research agenda aimed at closing the gap this evidence documents. The central argument is that a therapy's value cannot be judged solely by whether it succeeds in the trial that produced it, if that trial was never positioned to reflect how it would perform for most of the people who will eventually need it.

detail.abstract: Learned representations have transformed the measurement of unstructured data in economics. We extend it to relational data, showing that Temporal Graph Networks encode economically meaningful behavior in dynamic corporate ownership networks. Using a high-resolution Italian ownership graph anchored on 5,700 judicially confiscated firms, we train a TGN that is never supervised on confiscation to produce time-varying firm embeddings, and we summarize their geometry with an Infiltration Proximity Index (IPI): a real-time measure of how densely a firm's latent neighborhood is populated by firms whose confiscation is already legally known. We validate the index along three dimensions. It forecasts confiscation out of sample up to four years ahead, with a higher area under the ROC curve than the full set of firm-level financial variables at every horizon and for every classifier, and with far fewer missed confiscations at the cost of flagging more firms that are never confiscated; the geometry it summarizes places firms confiscated only later closer to firms already confiscated at the time of measurement; and it responds coherently to local changes in ownership. We then use the index to date firms' transitions into a high-risk regime in a staggered difference-indifferences design. Around the dated transition, firms display sharp scale expansion, rising liabilities and receivables, cost reallocation, and persistent illiquidity, with only temporary profit gains, patterns consistent with firms operating as conduits for financial flows rather than as profit maximizers.

detail.abstract: Relying on a micro-level dataset of US firms' inflation expectations, we document that firms in industries with larger Domar weights and more flexible prices have more accurate inflation forecasts. To explain these patterns, we develop a rational inattention model of price-setting firms within a production network. In equilibrium, firms' inflation forecast accuracy depends on their attention to marginal costs, the comovement between their marginal cost and aggregate inflation, and the change in the marginal cost. When calibrated to US input-output data, the model replicates the cross-sectoral relationship between forecast accuracy, Domar weights, and price flexibility. Quantitatively, we find that production networks endogenously increase nominal rigidity. This channel accounts for about 30 percent of the networks' attenuation of the inflation response to monetary shocks, deepening the standard flattening of the Phillips curve from input-output linkages.

title: Governing Access to Foundation Models: From Platforms to Infrastructures

detail.title: Governing Access to Foundation Models: From Platforms to Infrastructures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Foundation models are becoming critical inputs for businesses, governments, and society at large. Yet access to these technologies is governed primarily through private ordering, with foundation model providers unilaterally determining who may access their models, for what purposes, and under what conditions. This article argues that this governance architecture creates a public law gap by leaving the governance of access to a critical resource without public law safeguards. It identifies two resulting risks: an allocative risk, whereby providers may distribute access according to commercial considerations, creating a capabilities divide; and a normative risk, whereby providers may privilege downstream applications aligned with their own interests, thereby shaping the direction of AI innovation. To address these concerns, the article develops a tentative blueprint for model access governance. It argues that foundation models combine characteristics of both infrastructures and platforms but do not fit neatly into either regulatory tradition. Rather than transplanting existing regimes, it proposes a tailored public law framework that draws on both while adapting them to the distinctive governance challenges posed by foundation models.

title: The Meandering Path of Modeling Bicycle Route Choice

detail.title: The Meandering Path of Modeling Bicycle Route Choice

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.

detail.abstract: The amount and quality of active transportation infrastructure directly influence how much people cycle. However, we still lack quantitative tools to predict shifts in trips and mode choice as a result of investments in cycling infrastructure, which results in opinion- rather than evidence-based debates about the value of infrastructure. In this work, we model bicycle route choice, a key element in modeling cycling demand. Unlike motor vehicles which are sensitive mainly to distance and travel time, cyclists frequently detour from the shortest path to access safer and more pleasant routes. We combine over 3000 GPS cycling trajectories from the Toronto Household Activity-Travel Survey with road network, cycling network, and land use attributes to estimate bicycle route choice parameters. We systematically evaluate the impact of several modeling thresholds that have been arbitrarily chosen in previous works and show that results are more stable at large choice set sizes and when circuitous trips are removed. We quantify cycling infrastructure and road geometry with Level of Traffic Stress (LTS), a widely-used rating system for cycling comfort. LTS is correlated with cycling mode choice and segment-level cycling counts but has rarely been applied in bicycle route choice modeling. We estimate route choice parameters using a discrete choice modeling framework and compare two formulations of the model using either LTS or its underlying road class features to evaluate LTS as a route choice predictor. We find consistent patterns between LTS and road class, finding in the LTS model that cyclists prefer LTS 1 and LTS 2 and avoid LTS 4 compared to LTS 3, and finding in the road class model that cyclists prefer infrastructure relative to no infrastructure and prefer medium and local roads over major roads.

detail.abstract: Ethereum's Dencun upgrade introduced a separate fee market for rollup data availability. For Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, and zkSync Era, observed blob burn was 97.63% below a same-inclusion-block calldata benchmark on the recorded physical representation during March 15-April 12, 2024. Nine congestion days account for 99.9986% of that burn; outside them, burn was approximately 5.11 x 10-7 of the benchmark. Decoded payload calldata accounted for 83.78% of pre-period Layer 1 expenditure. Receipts independently reproduce sampled blob burn and separate post-period execution burn, tips, and an aggregate residual. Quantity comparisons require a narrower definition: zkSync's dense encoded blobs reveal provisioned capacity, not unpadded pubdata. Excluding zkSync, pooled bytes per Layer 2 transaction fell 10.81% and the fixed-composition index fell 6.91%. Including zkSync under a documented minimum-packing assumption gives a pooled increase between 3.71% and 9.48% and a fixed-composition decline between 6.29% and 18.56%, conditional on the measured posting universe. The seven-day direction is not identified for the four-chain cohort. These results distinguish charges on specified representations from workload and composition. They do not identify causal savings or compression improvements.

title: How Much Confounding Would It Take? Sensitivity Analysis for Directional Dependence Diagnostics in Time Series
affiliations: New York University

detail.title: How Much Confounding Would It Take? Sensitivity Analysis for Directional Dependence Diagnostics in Time Series

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Directional dependence diagnostics infer that one time series drives another from an asymmetry between forward and backward residual dependence, but an unobserved state tracked nonlinearly by both series produces the same asymmetry. This paper provides a sensitivity analysis. For a Gaussian persistent state with Gaussian measurement noise, a relative-entropy argument bounds the directional index by a quadratic in the root-mean-square nonlinear loading, with a computable constant. Inverting a lower confidence bound gives a robustness value, the smallest loading a no-channel explanation would need; an upper bound gives a ceiling on what any sample could certify. We prove consistency and primitive conditions for independent event samples, and show how to pool strata validly. Across 2,000 Fed, ECB, and Bank of England communication events, the equity index is confined to ±0.0007 and the ceiling stays below 0.006: residual-dependence asymmetries of this kind cannot establish the direction of monetary transmission.

title: Agriculture-Based Economic Liberalism in Nineteenth Century Coastal West African Economic Thought

detail.title: Agriculture-Based Economic Liberalism in Nineteenth Century Coastal West African Economic Thought

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no interests to declare.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no funding from any actor.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the prioritisation of agriculture-based economic liberalism in nineteenth century African economic thought, and argues that this prioritisation was an endogenous response to local conditions rather than a derivative echo of contemporaneous European debates between mercantilism and free trade. Drawing on coastal West African writers such as Ottobah Cugoano, Olaudah Equiano, James Horton, Carl Reindorf, Hilary Teague, Attoh Ahuma, Edward Blyden, John Mensah Sarbah and Casely Hayford, alongside the presidential addresses of Liberia's J.J. Roberts, Stephen Benson and Daniel Warner, and the writings of James Payne and Martin Delany, the paper identifies six recurring grounds on which writers placed agriculture ahead of commerce and industry: a slave-trade baseline that agricultural exports could displace; a native agricultural baseline of low productivity that called for improvement; the vulnerability created by over-investment in the entrepot trade; the resulting dependence on imported staple foods; a moral and environmental aversion to industrial and mercantile life; and an expectation that agricultural commerce, once linked by roads and railways, would knit African and other societies together in peaceable exchange. The paper traces these arguments through the baselines that writers reacted against, the moral and environmental case some of them built on top of these baselines, and the case, most fully developed by Payne and Delany, for agriculture as the springboard from which manufacturing and other industries could later emerge. It closes by considering the political and economic consequences of this orientation in nineteenth century Africa, and by situating agriculture-based economic liberalism as one of three broad responses, alongside conservatism and developmentalism, that African writers formulated to the pressures of the long nineteenth century.

title: LUSim: An LLM-Driven Spatial-Equilibrium Simulator for Urban Planning
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, Nanyang Technological University, Nanyang Technological University (NTU) - Division of Economics,  and Nanyang Technological University (NTU)

detail.title: LUSim: An LLM-Driven Spatial-Equilibrium Simulator for Urban Planning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Nan
declarations.funderStatement: Nan

detail.abstract: Quantitative ex-ante urban-policy evaluation has historically relied on closedform spatial-equilibrium and low-dimensional discrete-choice models that constrain analysis to homogeneous agents and fixed-form parametric utilities, and thereby to smooth proportional responses around the calibrated baseline. Integrating large language models into multi-agent simulation alleviates these constraints, but existing LLM-driven platforms lack the market-clearing mechanism and externally calibrated parameters that quantitative policy evaluation requires. We present LUSim (LLM-driven Urban Simulator), a multi-agent simulator in which heterogeneous households choose residence and workplace through a large language model and clear housing and labour markets inside an externally calibrated general-equilibrium city, with structural decision rules as baselines under identical conditions. We simulate a new rapid-transit line on a 96-zone Berlin instance calibrated from Ahlfeldt et al. (2015). The structural engines, which can only reweight the calibrated city in proportion, concentrate their response at the new stations, whereas with LLM-driven households approximately eight times as many relocate and the gains shift to peripheral districts. To test which engine predicts real urban change, we initialise every engine on the divided Berlin of 1986, let it predict the reunified city, and score, by criteria fixed in advance, its prediction of which districts gain or lose residents, jobs, prices, and wages against the changes observed by 2006. The simulation with LLM-driven households predicts these changes better than every structural baseline, also with district names withheld so that it cannot rely on memorised history, and the contrast persists across a second rail corridor, a zoning policy that expands floor space, and a second model family. We interpret these results as evidence that LLM-driven decision rules, disciplined by market clearing in a calibrated environment, predict urban change beyond the reach of structural models.

title: Removing Fuel Subsidies: Anatomy of Bolivia's 2025-2026 Energy Price Reform

detail.title: Removing Fuel Subsidies: Anatomy of Bolivia's 2025-2026 Energy Price Reform

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency, commercial entity, or not-for-profit organization.

detail.abstract: Bolivia eliminated its generalized gasoline and diesel subsidies in December 2025, after more than two decades of virtually unchanged retail prices. This paper explains the mechanism through which the subsidy was removed and examines two early outcomes of the reform. First, registered fuel sales declined, particularly for diesel, and the empirical results show that these changes were associated with the narrowing of the fuel price differential between Bolivia and Peru. Second, revenues from the 18 percent oil royalty increased substantially despite lower domestic production, mainly because the reform raised the value recognized for domestically produced crude oil. The paper also provides an inside view of the implementation process after the subsidy was removed, including some of the problems that emerged as firms, consumers, public institutions, and the government adjusted to the new price structure. The Bolivian experience shows that removing a subsidy and establishing a new pricing system are two different tasks. Once prices were adjusted, the government still had to deal with fuel supply, foreign exchange, sectoral responses, and the effects of higher fuel prices on its own institutions.

title: What Drives the Brazilian Retail Sales Index? A Bottom-Up Aggregation of Time Series Components

detail.title: What Drives the Brazilian Retail Sales Index? A Bottom-Up Aggregation of Time Series Components

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author states no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The author received no funding or scholarship for this research, including from the institution where he is enrolled as a Master's student.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines how the economic activities in the Brazilian Monthly Trade Survey (PMC) have contributed to the aggregate retail sales volume index throughout its history. Our primary contribution is the quantification of activity-level trend, seasonal, and irregular components of the PMC restricted index. This is achieved by combining Restricted Least Squares weight recovery with independent Prophet-based decompositions for each of the eight retail activities, which are then aggregated through a bottom-up approach. The recovered weights for the 2022 base year match IBGE's officially published figures, and estimated weights prior to 2022 are consistent with the documented revisions, replicating the aggregate index almost exactly.

Supermarkets emerge as the main driver of the retail index's trend, anchoring the aggregate's long-run evolution given their structural weight and relative stability. Pharmaceuticals, meanwhile, stand out as the only activity with uninterrupted trend growth over the sample. Seasonal behavior is most intense in Books & Stationery and Apparel, though their contributions to the aggregate end up diluted by smaller weights in both cases. During the 2020–2021 period, the initial negative shock is concentrated in Apparel and Others, April 2020's collapse is driven predominantly by external disturbances, and the recovery that followed reflected autoregressive propagation instead.

A forecasting exercise over the last 24 observations confirms reasonable out-of-sample predictions, and bottom-up aggregation of activity-level forecasts improves accuracy relative to the direct aggregate-level Prophet benchmark. Despite not being optimized for forecasting performance when compared to other approaches such as X-13-ARIMA, our results are consistent with the paper's primary objective of stable and interpretable structural decomposition.

title: Two Measures, Opposite Trends: Remittance Receipt in Mexican Household Surveys, 2008-2026

detail.title: Two Measures, Opposite Trends: Remittance Receipt in Mexican Household Surveys, 2008-2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing personal or financial interests. The author is the founder of Juncture Policy, an independent research platform; no organization had any role in the design, analysis, interpretation, or writing of this note.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses only publicly available, de-identified secondary data (INEGI ENOE microdata and Banco de Mexico aggregate series). No human subjects were recruited, consented, or contacted, and no personally identifiable information was accessed.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or financial support from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was conducted as unfunded independent research.

detail.abstract: Household surveys that ask about private transfers rarely separate support sent from abroad from the broader category of economic support a household may receive. Mexico's National Survey of Occupation and Employment (ENOE) contains both items. This note documents that the two move in opposite directions over 2008-2026, and that the difference is large enough to change substantive conclusions. Among adults aged 50 to 70, receipt measured by the broad item rose from 19.0 percent in 2008 to 33.0 percent in 2026, while receipt measured by the abroad-specific item fell from 3.12 percent to 1.60 percent. In the first quarter of 2026, 35,562 households with a member aged 50 to 70 reported broad support against 1,788 reporting support from abroad, a ratio of about twenty to one. The broad item includes non-contributory pensions and other domestic transfers; the abroad-specific item tracks remittance receipt. Research using ENOE transfer items should measure remittances with the abroad-specific item and should respect the survey's amplified-quarter schedule, in which the extended battery is absent, not all zero, in several quarters.

title: The Weights of the World: How Chinese and American Large Language Models Frame Political Legitimacy

detail.title: The Weights of the World: How Chinese and American Large Language Models Frame Political Legitimacy

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I am an independent researcher and I have no affiliation with any organization and I have no conflict of interests about the topic of study. I also have funder or no team at the moment.
declarations.funderStatement: This study was self-funded.

detail.abstract:
Many have researched ideology in large language models, often through forced-choice style surveys and measured as a position on a scale. This is the field’s single largest research design and its most cited methodology. The resulting ‘bias score’, deviating to the right or left, cannot show whose interests is supported through ideological, linguistic/discursive framing of the models. On the other hand, the body of research that treats models’ outputs as discourse has yet to address the relations between conditions of production and framings. In this paper, building on the concept of “discourse” in critical linguistics, I design a quantitative content analysis framework to not only identify the model’s explicit ideological position, but to capture the ideology in implicit framings across 120 responses from the Chinese DeepSeek V4 Pro and the American GPT 5.5 and 5.6 Sol to explore whether there is a relationship between ideological leaning of the models and the social, political, and economic conditions in which they were produced. These models were asked, in ten draws each, whether a head of state holding real power should be chosen through competitive popular elections and then, on the same conversation history, to assess the legitimacy of the heads of state of China and the United States.

The result indicates a novel finding: models can agree explicitly, while diverging significantly in framing. In the first prompt (the theoretical prompt, before mentioning any country), both models argue that a head of state with real power must be elected to be legitimate, but at the same time they differ substantially in their framing score, a gap of 3.30 points between DeepSeek V4 Pro-0423 and GPT 5.5, which is the largest gap in the study. Upon prompting the models regarding the legitimacy of the Chinese president, the divergence becomes explicit, with DeepSeek supporting the legitimacy of the Chinese head of state based on its own framing in the previous prompts, and GPT models openly arguing against it. DeepSeek also judged the American president's legitimacy weak in three draws, where neither American model did so once. The second finding of this study, however, tells us a totally different story. A later build of DeepSeek V4 Pro reproduced none of this. It never found China's head of state legitimate, and its framing gap from GPT-5.6 Sol was never substantial. This finding shows that ideological divergence can exist even between different builds of a model. Overall, this paper attempts to turn our attention from bias scores to the power relations these models serve by showing how models could support the same claim, but frame it in a politically different way, through comparing DeepSeek and GPT models, two family of models from two competing powers of the world.

title: Influence Maximization in Social Networks Using Discrete Cooperative Coevolutionary Whale Optimization Algorithm
affiliations: Guangxi Minzu University and Guangxi University for Nationalities

detail.title: Influence Maximization in Social Networks Using Discrete Cooperative Coevolutionary Whale Optimization Algorithm
detail.abstract: Influence maximization aims to select a limited set of seed nodes to maximize information diffusion in social networks. To balance diffusion performance and computational efficiency, this paper proposes a community-based discrete cooperative coevolutionary whale optimization algorithm (DCCWOA). The network is first partitioned by Louvain, and retained communities are treated as cooperative components for seed-subset optimization. Within each component, WOA serves as the main evolutionary search mechanism, providing global exploration and exploitation for candidate seed subsets. During this process, DCCWOA further addresses three specific challenges: context-dependent component evaluation, redundancy in continuous-to-discrete decoding, and local suboptimality in the discrete seed space. Accordingly, multi-context evaluation, redundancy-aware decoding, and discrete exchange neighborhood search are incorporated to improve evaluation reliability, reduce neighborhood overlap, and refine discrete solutions, respectively. Experiments on eight real-world networks show that DCCWOA achieves competitive influence diffusion performance and computational efficiency, obtaining high-quality seed sets with reasonable computational cost.

title: Factors Influencing Oil Palm Fruit Production and Income in Ondo State, Nigeria: A Gender Analysis
affiliations: Olusegun Agagu University of Science and Technology and Olusegun Agagu University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Factors Influencing Oil Palm Fruit Production and Income in Ondo State, Nigeria: A Gender Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The Authors declared that there are no conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: The research was approved by the Olusegun Agagu University of Science and Technology research ethical committee
declarations.funderStatement: TETFUND Nigeria

publicationDetails.detailsText: Egyptian Journal of Agricultural Research, volume 104, issue 3, 2026[ 10.21608/EJAR.2026.510695.1815] [undefined]

detail.abstract: Increased production of oil palm fruits is a sine qua non to farmers' income. Most times, smallholder oil palm farmers cannot increase output owing to production-associated challenges. It is not certain whether males and females were affected differently in the study area. Hence, this study determined the factors influencing oil palm production and income along the gender line. Using a multistage sampling procedure, 113 male and 67 female oil palm farmers were sampled from purposively selected local government areas and communities. An interview schedule was used for data collection. Mean, frequency, percentages and linear regression were used for data analysis. Males and females were aged 52.18±10.57 and 48.61±7.99 years, respectively. Most males (65.5%) and females (79.1%) were married. Over 65.0% of both genders had either primary or secondary education. Significant factors influencing oil palm fruit production among males were age, marital status, hired labour, farm size, and years of experience. Among females, age, formal education, household size, duration in community, farm size, and engagement in processing significantly influence production. Overall, age, marital status, formal education, household size, duration in community, years of experience, farm size, hired labour and engagement in processing significantly predict production. Factors significantly influencing income include oil palm fruit output/quantity and engagement in processing among males, formal education and engagement in processing among females, and oil palm fruit output/quantity and engagement in processing overall. Conclusively, an increase in access to more land for both genders would increase output, which would invariably contribute positively to income.

title: Industrial Policy and the Design of WTO Reform: Lessons from the EU's 2026 Reform Agenda
affiliations: Bocconi University - Department of Law and Université Paris II - Panthéon-Assas

detail.title: Industrial Policy and the Design of WTO Reform: Lessons from the EU's 2026 Reform Agenda

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Contemporary industrial policy combines instruments, objectives and cross-border effects that WTO law addresses through distinct rules and institutional functions. The European Union's July 2026 reform package provides a revealing setting in which to examine the implications for WTO reform. This article first reconstructs the connections the EU draws among substantive disciplines, transparency, remedies, State enterprises, foundational principles, development and governance, while distinguishing those connections from the legal choices the package leaves unresolved. It then shows that this pattern reflects a broader tension between economically integrated State intervention and the differentiated legal architecture of the WTO. A single industrial-policy programme may encounter that architecture through deficiencies in information, legal coverage or reach, contested allocations of policy space, or ineffective enforcement. Their economic connection does not make these problems legally equivalent or the corresponding forms of reform interchangeable. Institutional adaptation can improve the operation and coordination of existing obligations; changes in coverage, jurisdictional reach, policy space or remedial entitlements require substantive agreement. Industrial subsidies and State enterprises test this account in different settings: subsidies principally require the recalibration of an established regime, while State enterprises raise the antecedent question of the regulatory perimeter itself.

title: Ecosystem resilience as a public good: Nash equilibria can be Pareto-efficient
affiliations: and University of Freiburg - Department of Environment and Natural Resources

detail.title: Ecosystem resilience as a public good: Nash equilibria can be Pareto-efficient

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or relationships with other people or organizations that could inappropriately influence or bias the work reported in this manuscript.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported in part by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) for financial support under grant no.\ 01LC2326C

detail.abstract: We analyze ecosystem resilience as public self-protection for risk-averse users. Conventional wisdom has it that public-good allocation is a prisoners' dilemma with an inefficient equilibrium: there are incentives to free-riding and, consequently, underprovision of the public good. We show that, in contrast, for privately provided public self-protection Nash equilibria can be Pareto-efficient-namely in corner allocations. The underlying reason is that individual expected utility is not necessarily concave in the contributions to the public good, which may lead to corner solutions with unconventional properties. In particular, if the individuals' degree of risk-aversion is high or ecosystem elasticity is highly negative the allocation problem becomes a coordination game with two equilibria-an inefficient one and a Pareto-efficient one at the right corner which features individual incentives to full private provision of the public good. Our results suggest new policy approaches for the governance of ecosystem resilience.

title: Can Zero -Shot Large Language Models Forecast Gold Prices? An Empirical Evaluation

detail.title: Can Zero -Shot Large Language Models Forecast Gold Prices? An Empirical Evaluation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Forecasting gold prices is essential for investment decision-making and risk management, yet it remains unclear whether recent zero-shot large language models (LLMs) can generate reliable numerical forecasts without task-specific training. This study evaluates the forecasting performance of three state-of-the-art zero-shot LLMs-DeepSeek-V4-Pro, GLM-5.2, and NVIDIA Nemotron-3 Ultra-and compares their performance with conventional statistical and deep learning approaches using daily gold price data from 2015 to 2025. The empirical results show that zero-shot LLMs provide competitive forecasting performance despite requiring no model fine-tuning. Among the evaluated models, DeepSeek-V4-Pro achieved the strongest overall performance, producing the lowest forecasting errors in terms of MAE and MAPE and significantly outperforming most competing approaches in pairwise statistical comparisons. Robustness analyses further demonstrate that its forecasting performance remains relatively stable across different market conditions, including periods characterized by structural changes. These findings provide empirical evidence that reasoning-oriented foundation models represent a promising approach for financial time series forecasting and highlight their potential to complement conventional statistical and deep learning models in commodity price prediction.

title: BRICSCOIN: Initial Distribution and Dynamic Injection Rules for a Non-Pegged, No-interest, Unanimous, Supranational Settlement Currency
affiliations: University of Yaounde II and University of Belgrade

detail.title: BRICSCOIN: Initial Distribution and Dynamic Injection Rules for a Non-Pegged, No-interest, Unanimous, Supranational Settlement Currency
detail.abstract: Abstract: We build a five-country open-economy Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian (HANK) Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium model to study BRICSCOIN, a proposed supranational settlement instrument for Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. BRICSCOIN is minted only by unanimous agreement of a five-member Issuing Council, verified through a tamper-evident distributed ledger, and carries no peg, no reserve backing, and no convertibility promise: it functions purely as a bilateral settlement asset held on central bank balance sheets. We embed this institutional design into the external block of an otherwise standard multi-country incomplete-markets model and use it to answer two design questions the institution itself leaves open.

title: When Bad News Breeds Bias: Cross-country Evidence from Households' Inflation Expectations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Central Bank of Cyprus and University of Cyprus

detail.title: When Bad News Breeds Bias: Cross-country Evidence from Households' Inflation Expectations
detail.abstract: Utilizing a large household-level dataset of inflation expectations for twelve euro-area economies, we attempt to assess the formation and accuracy of inflation expectations following major disruptions of the macroeconomy which we identify during the period from 2004:1 to 2025:2. We find that the arrival of such adverse events tends to increase the degree of inaccuracy in inflation expectations. We also find that this happens because inflation expectations tend to go up in response to these adverse shocks relative to the 12-month ahead inflation realizations, which offers direct evidence of households overestimating inflation. This is consistent with overreaction of inflation expectations in response to inflationary news and with inflation-as-a-bad behavioral patterns in response to adverse non-inflationary shocks. We infer that such behavioral forces appear to have played an important role in the formation of inflation expectations in the euro-area following adverse shocks during the past two decades.

title: Robust and Anisotropic Continuous Tensor Recovery via Structural Topology and Nonconvex Residual Reweighting
affiliations: Anhui Polytechnic University, Jiangnan University, Jiangnan University, Jiangnan University and Anhui Polytechnic University

detail.title: Robust and Anisotropic Continuous Tensor Recovery via Structural Topology and Nonconvex Residual Reweighting
detail.abstract: Continuous tensor recovery has emerged as a novel modeling paradigm due to Implicit Neural Representation (INR). However, existing methods usually adopt isotropic coordinate fitting, ignoring the anisotropic topology of visual tensors. Also, they lack an explicit mechanism to suppress the gradient contribution of extreme residuals, making the learned continuous field vulnerable to severe corruptions. Thus, we propose a Robust and Anisotropic Continuous Tensor Recovery (RACTR) framework. Firstly, to improve coordinate fitting, anisotropic Grouped Canonical Polyadic (GCP) topology is designed to represent tensor-valued signals as structured separable neural fields. This design couples strongly correlated modes while preserving mode-specific variations. Secondly, on this structured topology, we introduce a generalized nonconvex residual objective. It induces a residual-gradient influence reweighting mechanism, where extreme residuals receive vanishing gradient influence during optimization. Thirdly, we provide theoretical analysis to clarify the structural and optimization properties of the proposed framework.  Finally, extensive experiments on benchmarks demonstrate that RACTR consistently shows strong robustness and achieves superior performance in severe degradation cases.  Code will be available at https://github.com/Yaoliang1614/RACTR once accepted.

title: Water rights and regulatory risk: Insights from a policy intervention
affiliations: and University of Chile

detail.title: Water rights and regulatory risk: Insights from a policy intervention
detail.abstract: We study how drought affects the price of perpetual water rights when the government can temporarily reallocate water during scarcity. Using Chilean transactions from 2000 to 2019, we exploit the 2008 introduction of scarcity decrees and instrument decree exposure with the hydrological rule the regulator uses. We separate two opposing effects. In areas without government intervention, a one-standard-deviation increase in drought raises prices by 17.1 percent, consistent with water rights providing a hedge against scarcity. In areas exposed to the policy, prices fall by an additional 22.4 percent. The two effects are of similar size and opposite sign, so the average response to drought is close to zero while both channels are large. Our results show that the state's power to reallocate water can offset the value of a water right as a hedge, and that the relevant tradeoff in designing water markets is between flexibility in emergencies and the credibility of the entitlement.

title: Fairness as Equity, Honesty and Justice: An Exercise in a Multilingual Analysis of the DMA

detail.title: Fairness as Equity, Honesty and Justice: An Exercise in a Multilingual Analysis of the DMA

declarations.declarationOfInterest: In accordance with the ASCOLA principles, the author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: The SCiDA project is a Joint Research Project funded by DFG and AHRC.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Forthcoming in Journal of Competition Law and Economics

detail.abstract: Like any other piece of EU legislation, the Digital Markets Act (DMA) is a multilingual legal instrument. However, its interpretation is often confined to the English-language discourse of competition law. This paper argues that this monolingual focus contradicts the CJEU's fundamental principle of the equal authenticity of language versions, which states that no single language version should be relied upon in isolation. A key concept in the DMA’s regulatory framework is “fairness”, a notion that remains semantically elusive. Through a comparative linguistic analysis of nine of the official language versions of the DMA, this study reveals significant variability in how “fairness” is translated. It suggests that these lexical choices reflect not only stylistic differences, but also distinct normative shifts towards notions of equity, honesty or justice. Ultimately, this paper addresses a gap in the existing literature by providing a systematic, multilingual investigation. It posits that the autonomous and uniform application of the DMA requires a teleological interpretation that embraces linguistic diversity.

title: Population Aging and Fiscal Sustainability in Resource-Rich Economies: The Case of Chile
affiliations: Adolfo Ibanez University, Adolfo Ibanez University and Inter-American Development Bank

detail.title: Population Aging and Fiscal Sustainability in Resource-Rich Economies: The Case of Chile
detail.abstract: Emerging economies face long-run fiscal sustainability challenges associated with demographic change and the productive capacity of commodity sectors. Population aging can weaken labor supply growth, constrain tax bases, and increase age-related public expenditures, while declining productivity in non-renewable sectors may further limit fiscal capacity and economic growth. This paper develops a semi-structural macro-fiscal model to analyze the long-term implications of population aging for economic growth, fiscal sustainability, and public debt dynamics in resource-rich economies. The model integrates demographics, labor markets, sectoral production, fiscal revenues, age-related public expenditures, and government debt within a unified deterministic and stochastic simulation framework. It is applied to Chile, given the speed of its demographic transition, the importance of consumption taxation, and the central role of mining in macroeconomic and fiscal performance. The results indicate that demographic aging generates persistent fiscal pressures through both expenditure and revenue channels. Rising pension and health spending increase primary expenditures as a share of GDP, while slower labor force growth constrains output growth and tax bases. Under current policy settings, these forces lead to a gradual but sustained increase in public debt over the long run. Stochastic simulations show substantial dispersion in debt trajectories due to uncertainty surrounding age-related expenditures. Policy simulations suggest that higher labor force participation mainly improves fiscal sustainability through stronger revenues, while increases in statutory retirement ages affect both revenues and pension expenditures, generating larger fiscal improvements. Nevertheless, these reforms mitigate but do not fully offset the long-run fiscal consequences of demographic change.

title: oTrunity: A Reusable oTree-Unity Connection Layer for 3D and Virtual-Reality Economic Experiments
affiliations: and

detail.title: oTrunity: A Reusable oTree-Unity Connection Layer for 3D and Virtual-Reality Economic Experiments

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no conflict of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Xu Zhang acknowledges funding support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 72203054), the Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation of Guangdong Province / Guangdong Basic and Applied Basic Research Foundation (No. 2025A1515010549), the Yangcheng Scholars Research Project of Guangzhou (No. 2024312031), the Guangzhou Municipal Science and Technology Project (No. 2025A03J3807), and the Research on HKUST(GZ) Practices (ROP) in 2025 (No. HKUST(GZ)-ROP2025040).

detail.abstract: Many economic experiments require participant-facing environments in which spatial relations, embodied action, or co-present social cues form part of the treatment. For researchers using oTree, moving beyond a browser page creates a recurring integration problem: participant identity, roles, state transitions, decisions, page progression, and payoffs must remain aligned when the participant-facing interface is implemented as a standalone 3D or immersive Unity client. We present oTrunity, a connection layer that keeps the economic protocol under oTree control while allowing researchers to change the participant-facing Unity client. For turn-based decisions, researchers specify decision fields and wait rules in an experiment configuration, allowing the same connection layer to be reused across experiments rather than rebuilt for each task. We validate the connection layer using fresh-clone checks, archived Windows Desktop runs with one Unity client and a mock partner, and a dual-headset Quest Pro/PICO 4 Trust run. Across these cases, terminal oTree records and archived logs verify registration, participant-specific state exchange, decision submission, page progression, and final payoff calculation. Together, these tests show that the same connection layer can be reused across turn-based 3D and VR economic experiments in which decision fields and wait rules are specified through the experiment configuration.

title: Hidden History: Volume II

detail.title: Hidden History: Volume II
detail.abstract:
This work presents a historical forensic analysis and systemic framework investigating the hidden administrative operating systems of global human governance. Volume II documents the concrete case studies of global population management, tracing how centralized infrastructure was adapted across succeeding empires. 

The focus of this independent investigation is entirely on structural architecture: the creation of institutions, the incentives behind regulatory decisions, the frameworks that preserve centralized control, and the historical consequences produced by those tracking structures. By examining the continuous transmission chain running from ancient Near Eastern legal and financial bookkeeping systems straight into modern central banking, state registries, and institutional networks, this monograph outlines the operational mechanics of state legibility and corporate population management.

title: Confucian Values and the Geographic Concentration of Family Recycling Firms: Evidence from Geo-Spatial Analysis and Field Investigation in Shandong, China
affiliations: ESSCA School of Management

detail.title: Confucian Values and the Geographic Concentration of Family Recycling Firms: Evidence from Geo-Spatial Analysis and Field Investigation in Shandong, China

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: The author declares that ESSCA funded this research.

detail.abstract: Approximately 25% of China's registered recycling firms are concentrated in Shandong Province, which accounts for only 7.28% of national GDP (location quotient = 3.41). This striking geographic disproportion raises the question of whether cultural rather than regulatory factors can explain the emergence and concentration of environmentally oriented industries. This paper investigates whether Confucian values-frugality, family solidarity, and collective well-being-explain this pattern in Shandong, the historical heartland of Confucianism. We combine macro-level geo-spatial analysis of 44,758 registered recycling firms and Buddhist and Taoist temple locations across China with micro-level qualitative fieldwork in Zhaojialing Village, Sishui County, including in-depth interviews and two firm case studies. Recycling firm locations show negligible spatial overlap with Buddhist or Taoist temples, while Shandong exhibits a pronounced concentration. Field evidence identifies three Confucian mechanisms: family-based trust that substitutes for formal contracts; deep-rooted 1 frugality norms that motivate spontaneous waste collection and monetisation; and collective responsibility extending employment to elderly workers. These findings suggest that culturally compatible, community-embedded recycling models can reconcile economic development with environmental protection through institutional complementarities rather than coercive regulation alone. Cultural values create initial conditions while fiscal incentives sustain scale-up; neither is sufficient independently. This offers an alternative to the "pollute first, clean up later" paradigm with implications for policy design in developing economies.

title: Unemployment Assistance, Benefit Duration and Employment Transitions among Older Workers: Evidence from an Age-Based Eligibility Reform
affiliations: University of Alcala, University of Alcala and University of Alcala

detail.title: Unemployment Assistance, Benefit Duration and Employment Transitions among Older Workers: Evidence from an Age-Based Eligibility Reform
detail.abstract: This article examines how a change in unemployment assistance eligibility affected the exit of older workers from the unemployment benefits system in Spain. In March 2019, the eligibility age for an unlimited unemployment assistance benefit was reduced from 55 to 52, extending entitlement by up to three years for unemployed individuals aged 52–54 who had exhausted their unemployment insurance benefits. This reform creates a quasi-experimental setting that identifies the causal effect of extending potential benefit duration on unemployment-to-employment transitions among older workers. Unlike previous studies that examine reforms restricting eligibility, we analyze a policy that expanded access to long-term unemployment assistance. Using data from the Spanish Public Employment Service and estimating a duration model with individuals aged 49–51 as a control group, we find that the reform significantly reduced transitions from unemployment to employment among eligible workers, thereby substantially increasing the expected duration of unemployment assistance receipt.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we design a stock-recruitment framework to examine non-cooperative conservation decisions made by players exploiting a common-pool renewable resource, such as a shared fish stock. The players face two sources of uncertainty. First, the resource population is subject to growth uncertainty caused by environmental variability like fluctuations in ambient temperature. Moreover, the biological growth function may undergo a permanent downward shift at an uncertain future date. We capture this regime shift risk through a hazard process within a discrete-time framework. Despite their impacts on management, the extent to which both types of uncertainty affect fishing communities is a matter that has surprisingly received little attention. Here we derive Markov Perfect Nash equilibria and show that each player's harvest responses to stock growth uncertainty may change qualitatively when a stock-dependent hazard of regime shift is introduced. The harvest effect of regime shift risk may change qualitatively when growth uncertainty is allowed. Escapement may be monotonic or not in the variance of growth uncertainty. We identify scenarios in which competition to extract the resource gives rise to novel equilibrium outcomes relative to the optimal management case.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an open economy model with asymmetric information to explain cross-country heterogeneity in the transmission of government spending shocks. Using panel data for 41 countries, we find that a positive government spending shock strongly stimulates consumption and depreciates the real exchange rate in countries with countercyclical fiscal policy, whereas in countries with procyclical fiscal policy, the crowding-in effect on consumption is weaker and the real exchange rate appreciates. To account for these patterns, we build an open economy New Keynesian model in which fiscal policy conveys information about economic conditions. A change in government purchases reveals the government’s assessment of the state of the economy, leading private agents to form misaligned beliefs about economic fluctuations. Crucially, this signaling effect depends on a country’s fiscal cyclicality. Evidence from professional forecasts supports this information channel.

detail.abstract: We study an investor who chooses consumption, portfolio investment, and an irreversible retirement time. Employment incurs the felicity penalty u(κc), with 0 < κ < 1, which disappears at retirement. The investor may borrow against deterministic labor income, subject to the natural solvency condition. Stock returns depend on a rapidly meanreverting stochastic factor. For general smooth utility, the constant-investment-opportunity benchmark is characterized by the inverse marginal utility and one scalar retirement equation. Its portfolio rule is expressed in terms of the investor's indirect risk tolerance. We derive the first-order stochastic-volatility correction to lifetime utility and prove that both the value error and the utility loss of the benchmark strategy are bounded by a constant multiple of the fast timescale parameter, under stated power-tail and discountedmoment conditions. These conditions allow nonconstant relative risk aversion. Economic results characterize retirement comparative statics, consumption and portfolio changes, the wealth value of employment flexibility, and the benchmark retirement-time distribution. Numerical experiments with non-CRRA preferences illustrate these mechanisms and test the expansion with two-dimensional policy-evaluation equations. Separately, under explicit local compactness, nondegeneracy, and matching hypotheses, we prove a first-order expansion of the optimal retirement boundary. Its coefficient combines an explicit outer displacement with the boundary of a nonlinear Bellman cell. A flux identity separates a correlation contribution from a nonnegative local portfolio-improvement term; at zero correlation, a nonconstant squared Sharpe ratio strictly raises a specified weighted mean of the first boundary correction. The value theorem does not require these additional boundary hypotheses.

title: Does Family Caregiving Complement Formal Care? Daughters and Parental Survival After a Severe Health Shock
affiliations: University of Copenhagen - Copenhagen University,  and University of Chicago

detail.title: Does Family Caregiving Complement Formal Care? Daughters and Parental Survival After a Severe Health Shock

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no relevant or material financial interests that relate to the research described in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: Matteo Saccarola acknowledges financial support from the NBER Fellowship in Behavioral Macroeconomics and the Fisher Center for Real Estate and Urban Economics.

detail.abstract: We study how informal family caregiving and formal care interact after severe parental health shocks, and whether they operate as substitutes or complements. Using Danish administrative data, we compare parents of only children who experience a stroke at the same age and differ only in the gender of their child. Before the stroke, parents of daughters and parents of sons follow similar health trajectories, with comparable levels of pre-existing conditions and healthcare utilization. After the stroke, a survival gap opens and grows, and parents of daughters are 1.5 percentage points more likely to be alive by year five. Over the same period, daughters adjust more than sons along several margins: they become more likely to live near their parents, less likely to be married, and have fewer children, consistent with greater involvement in informal caregiving. Crucially, parents of daughters use more physical rehabilitation, an elective type of formal care that requires sustained engagement. Rather than crowding out formal provision, daughters appear more likely to help parents navigate and use professional services. Informal and formal care can therefore operate, at least in part, as complements in the response to severe health shocks.

title: Calling Capitalism and Class in the United States: From Reconstruction and the Gilded Age to the Present

detail.title: Calling Capitalism and Class in the United States: From Reconstruction and the Gilded Age to the Present

detail.abstract: This article explains how American capitalism repeatedly transformed rather than displaced the moral language of calling. Beginning with Reconstruction and the Gilded Age, it traces how disciplined labor, self-command, thrift, and achievement were detached from Calvinist theology and reembedded in corporations, schools, professions, credit systems, welfare institutions, and digitally mediated workplaces. It develops an institutional account of moralized inequality: institutions distribute unequal resources and opportunities, then classify unequal outcomes as individual merit, responsibility, or failure. The analysis distinguishes property, organizational authority, expertise, income, wealth, employment security, debt exposure, and institutional dependence, while showing how race, gender, citizenship, education, occupation, and locality convert historically unequal resources into apparently individual merit. Calling persists as a contested moral infrastructure of capitalism. The central question is whether institutions that demand effort, commitment, and self-investment can justify the unequal security, authority, wealth, and recognition that follow.

title: Electric vehicles as power storage may spur the energy transition
affiliations: and Norwegian University of Life Sciences

detail.title: Electric vehicles as power storage may spur the energy transition
detail.abstract: Using electric vehicles (EVs) as power storage is referred to as vehicle-to-grid (V2G). To our knowledge no study has yet analyzed how V2G may affect the electricity market in the longer run. Thus, in this paper we ask: What are the effects of V2G for the electricity market when we consider that widespread V2G adoption will affect incentives to invest in renewable capacity? We construct a model with stochastic intermittent renewable production: conditions can be either good or bad. V2G will generally increase electricity prices when conditions are good and decrease prices when conditions are bad. Despite the two opposing effects, we show analytically that increasing the share of EV owners with V2G lowers the expected price of electricity. Hence, electricity consumers with inelastic demand are likely to benefit from increased adoption of V2G. The reason is that investments in renewable energy are spurred as their production weighted price increases. Finally, we calibrate the model to the German electricity market in 2035 and provide some illustrative, quantitative results. In a perfect market equilibrium with no price distortions about one third of the EV owners adopt V2G. This induces an increase in electricity production from renewables by nearly two percent due to higher investments, and a significant increase in the total surplus from the electricity market.

title: Prices or implied volatilities? Choosing the loss function in machine learning option pricing

detail.title: Prices or implied volatilities? Choosing the loss function in machine learning option pricing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

keywords: out-of-sample pricing accuracy JEL Classification: C45

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the importance of the loss function in machine learning option pricing by asking whether a model should be trained on pricing errors or on implied-volatility errors. Both choices appear in the literature, usually without justification, and a meta-analysis of the field shows an increasing share of studies training on implied-volatility errors, whilst pricing accuracy remains the criterion on which their models are judged. We answer the question empirically by estimating the same machine learning model under two loss functions that differ only in the space where the error is measured, using 8.67 million S&P 500 index-option observations priced out of sample from 1997 through 2025. The price-space loss lowers pooled pricing RMSE by 25.3%, nearly twice what the network itself contributes over the parametric benchmark, and attains a lower error in every sample year and on the implied-volatility criterion that its rival optimizes. Conditional predictive ability tests show that the advantage varies with contract vega but not with market volatility, so it follows from the loss function rather than the sample period. The training space is therefore a first-order design choice, and researchers who price options with machine learning are better off measuring the error where the model will be judged.

detail.abstract: Tokenized financial assets can be natively transferable and programmable, but the relationships around them remain commonly coordinated through provider-controlled accounts. This paper studies when a position can persist as the common object of accepted claims and service mandates as its uses or operating providers change. We define shared authority: bounded powers held by separately identified actors over a continuing position, with relevant state transitions coupled to accepted commitments. Technical continuity becomes institutional portability within a declared domain only when a qualified outsider recognizes that state and changes an economic decision without requiring the relationship to be reconstructed. The paper establishes three consequences of the mechanism. First, in a sequential financing economy with finite dated resources, we bound owner value across all policies subject to a specified repayment-source restriction and construct a fully funded arrangement that strictly exceeds the bound under stated conditions. Second, we characterize compatible specialist entry, voluntary formation and transferable service value around inherited claims. Third, a stock-lending application connects advance acceptance to executable opportunities and derives quantities, rents and valuation in an established equilibrium. The results identify when authority design expands the useful financial relationships supported by existing capital and how the resulting benefits are divided.

detail.abstract: This research focusses on how recent clauses of Bilateral Investment Treaties (BITs) affect foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in the selected Asian developing economies, particularly South Asian developing nations, between 1985 and 2023. Existing research has focused on the existence of BITs; the current study extends the reflections by measuring the influence of the recent clauses of treaties, which include fair and equitable treatment (FET), expropriation protection, most-favoured-nation (MFN) treatment, free transfer of funds, and investor-state dispute settlement (ISDS). The study aims to find a possible positive influence on investor decisions and investment flows to those developing economies due to recent clauses of BIT. Moreover, the paper also examines the impact of the International Centre of Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) decisions to establish, whether, improved international legal safeguards lead to increased investment confidence and also strengthens investment inflows. The methodology of the study is based on a balanced panel data and includes descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, panel unit root and co-integration tests, fixed and random-effects regressions. Analytical procedures that detect anomalies in the data such as heteroscedasticity, autocorrelation, and cross-sectional dependence issues are also carried out. The dynamic panel GMM model is also used to deal with endogeneity and FDI persistence. The findings of the study indicates that revised BIT clauses, and particularly those that increase legal certainty, integrity of dispute settlement, and protection of investments, have a positive impact on FDI inflows. The effect of this is enhanced by the ICSID membership that minimises investor risk. The findings demonstrate that Asian developing economies should further modernise BIT clauses and enhance institutions to maintain and increase FDI inflows.

title: Money Cop
affiliations: Cornell Law School, European Corporate Governance Institute and University of Michigan Law School

detail.title: Money Cop

detail.abstract: The Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions are the subject of intense academic scrutiny. There is also a rich parallel literature examining the Federal Reserve's governance, independence, and role as a lender of last resort. Yet often neglected within this literature is the fact that the Federal Reserve is also a federal law enforcement agency: one armed with a formidable arsenal of enforcement powers. This paper reports the findings of a comprehensive survey of Federal Reserve enforcement actions. Drawing on 350 actions brought between 1995 and 2025, this survey reveals several key enforcement patterns. First, while the majority of enforcement actions by number target community banks, the bulk of the monetary penalties stem from a small handful of actions against large international banks. Second, only about one third of these actions are brought under the Federal Reserve's core safety, soundness, and stability powers, with the remainder brought under a hodgepodge of federal laws governing flood insurance, money laundering, trading misconduct, and consumer protection. Third, while enforcement patterns do not vary significantly between Democratic and Republican administrations, there was a material increase in both the average number of enforcement actions and the size of monetary penalties in the decade following the global financial crisis. Lastly, we find no statistically significant share price reaction to the announcement of enforcement actions, with the notable exception of a strong negative reaction for the largest banks. We similarly find no evidence of depositor flight in response to enforcement news. The paper concludes by exploring the implications of these findings for Federal Reserve governance and independence, the regulatory sine curve, the role of market discipline in bank regulation, and the optimal design of enforcement policy.

detail.abstract: Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 on markets in crypto-assets (MiCAR) sketches a crisis management framework for issuers of asset-referenced tokens (ARTs) and e-money tokens (EMTs), built around recovery plans (Article 46) and the novel instrument of redemption plans (Article 47), applied mutatis mutandis to EMT issuers via Article 55. This paper examines how that framework interacts — and eventually collides — with the Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive (BRRD), the second Electronic Money Directive (EMD2), the Deposit Guarantee Schemes Directive (DGSD) and unharmonised national insolvency law. We show that the applicable crisis regime fragments along the legal form of the issuer (credit institution, electronic money institution, or other authorised legal person), producing inconsistent creditor outcomes for economically identical tokens. The paper’s central claim is that token holders live under what we term the “Damocles sword of bail-in”: because EMT reserves are, in significant part, mandatorily deposited with credit institutions (Article 54 MiCAR; Article 7 EMD2), the resolution of a deposit-taking bank can transmit write-down losses to token holders who have no contractual relationship with, and often no knowledge of, that bank.

detail.abstract: Anomaly returns concentrate around information releases, suggesting mispricing that is corrected as news arrives. We replicate 94 accounting-based anomalies with accounting data lagged by up to five years. Alpha decays slowly: median monthly CAPM alphas are 36 basis points at the four-month lag and 28 with year-old data, robust out of sample and positive internationally. An equal-weighted book of year-old factors earns 19 basis points monthly (𝑡 = 4.9); the four-month-minus-twelve-month spread earns 8 (𝑡 = 6.0) and is shrinking. The evidence limits explanations in which returns vanish once information is public and is consistent with a persistent characteristic premium.

title: An Active-Learning-Based Method for Rapid Detection of Cochlear Dead-Region Boundaries over a Continuous Frequency Range
affiliations: Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University and Tsinghua University - School of Medicine

detail.title: An Active-Learning-Based Method for Rapid Detection of Cochlear Dead-Region Boundaries over a Continuous Frequency Range
detail.abstract: Accurate localization of cochlear dead-region boundaries is important for individualized hearing rehabilitation. Conventional threshold-equalizing noise (TEN) testing provides results only at discrete frequencies, whereas psychophysical tuning curves (PTCs), although capable of locating boundaries, are time-consuming and may be affected by off-frequency listening through both flanking regions in mid-frequency dead regions. This study proposes a combined TEN–PTC active-learning framework. Continuous TEN screening is first performed using Gaussian-process modeling and Bayesian Active Learning by Disagreement (BALD), after which Active PTC locally refines candidate boundaries. For dead regions with two boundaries, band-limited TEN is additionally presented on the non-target side to suppress competing off-frequency listening pathways. A total of 300 virtual participants were generated using a Moore–Glasberg-inspired hearing-loss model. The proposed method achieved an overall median relative boundary error of 3.6% and a mean estimated test duration of 6.4 min, compared with 26.4 min for conventional TEN plus Fast PTC and 117.8 min for clinical dense PTC. It also produced more stable estimates for island and multiple dead regions. Validation on a custom audiometer showed mean absolute output errors below 0.7 dB for pure tones, PTC narrowband maskers, and TEN(HL). In one participant with hearing loss, the proposed method identified a candidate high-frequency dead-region interval and yielded a boundary estimate consistent with standard TEN(HL) and Fast PTC findings. These results support the proposed framework as an efficient approach to automated continuous-frequency cochlear dead-region detection and boundary estimation.

detail.abstract: We study how timestamps affect dynamic disclosure. At a random date, a sender privately obtains hard evidence about an evolving binary state and chooses when to disclose it. With timestamps, the unique equilibrium features immediate good-evidence disclosure and timestamp-dependent bad-evidence delay. Without timestamps, high priors relative to impatience generate a stock of undisclosed good evidence, which is stochastically purged before permanent transparency. High impatience yields immediate good-evidence disclosure, while bad evidence can be arbitrarily delayed and disclosed in bursts. Timestamps prevent pretending old good evidence is fresh and certify bad evidence is old, accelerating good-evidence disclosure and facilitating bad-evidence disclosure.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Recommendations and Competition

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Recommendations and Competition
detail.abstract: We study how algorithmic recommendations affect product-market competition. We embed recommender systems, trained on sparse and noisy feedback, in a model of consumer search and price competition. Recommendations create personalized prominence: consumers start searching from products predicted to match their tastes. This improves matching and reduces search costs, but also raises equilibrium prices. Prices increase through front-loading of high-value consumers, reliance on informative recommendations, and reduced price salience under directed search. Due to the higher prices, consumer surplus may fall despite better matches. We also show that manipulated recommendations can intensify competition and limit the profitability of self-preferencing.

detail.abstract: This article examines the promises made by John Dramani Mahama and the National Democratic Congress (NDC) ahead of Ghana's 7 December 2024 general election and tests those promises against the documented record of governance between the administration's inauguration on 7 January 2025 and August 2026. It draws on independent fact-checking projects (notably GhanaFact's Promise Meter), IMF Article IV and Extended Credit Facility (ECF) reviews, Bank of Ghana and Ghana Statistical Service data, parliamentary budget statements, and on-the-record reactions from organised labour (TUC), business associations (AGI, Chamber of Commerce, ACCI), farmer and cooperative bodies (PFAG, GCCFA), and independent policy analysts. The analysis finds a genuinely mixed record: real and independently verifiable macroeconomic stabilisation (falling inflation, a rebuilt cedi, a primary fiscal surplus, and an upgraded debt-distress rating) sits alongside slower, partial, or contested delivery on flagship social and structural promises-the 24-Hour Economy, free first-year tertiary fees, agricultural revival, and anti-galamsey enforcement. It also interrogates a structural feature of Ghanaian (and broader West African) electoral politics: the tendency for manifesto commitments to be produced as persuasive political instruments rather than as costed, evidence-based policy proposals, and the consequences this has for accountability, fiscal planning, and public trust. The article does not take a partisan position on the government's performance. It sets out the evidence, presents the range of expert and stakeholder views, and identifies open questions that citizens, journalists, legislators, and researchers should continue to probe.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of Distressed Debt Exchanges (DDEs), which accounted for more than two-thirds of all Broadly Syndicated Bank Loan and High Yield Bond defaults in 2024 and 2025. Examining 284 DDEs from 2009-2022, we find that over 50% of DDE firms experience a second negative event-bankruptcy, missed interest payment, or a subsequent DDE-rising to almost 60% for the most recent cohort. Median recovery rates rise from 54.5% at the initial DDE to 62% at a subsequent DDE, which we interpret as a Bayesian market update reflecting firms' propensity to restructure repeatedly rather than liquidate. We develop an equilibrium model of the creditor's trilemma: sell, hold out, or tender. For small, price-taking creditors, selling at the median market price strictly dominates the other two options, while distressed investors who buy the securities earn positive returns. For large creditors, market illiquidity eliminates the sell option, reducing the problem to a binary choice. We derive a closed-form threshold showing that holding out is optimal only in a narrow range. The resulting prisoner's dilemma among large creditors, combined with illiquidity and bankruptcy risk, explains why over 90% of creditors accept the exchange despite the apparent advantage of selling. Our framework offers a structural explanation for the recent rise of coercive Liability Management Exercises and shows that DDEs typically postpone rather than resolve financial distresstwo-thirds of DDE firms exhibit deteriorating Z-Scores within one year.

detail.abstract: We study a dynamic model of shareholder trading and voting. The model features a population of small investors and a large fund with heterogeneous preferences over ESG policies. We characterize both the term structure and the limiting distributions of shareholdings and corporate policy. Our results show that (i) it might be difficult to learn about a fund's preference for pro-social policy from static snapshots of its trading and voting; the dynamic term structure needs to be examined. (ii) moderately pro-social investors tend to hold shares in more pro-social firms and can prevent a highly demanding fund from moving a firm's policy as far as it would prefer. Overall, the paper provides a dynamic framework for understanding how trading, voting, and heterogeneous ESG preferences jointly shape corporate policy.

title: Economy as a System of Actions: From Natural Economy to Market Self-Centralization

detail.title: Economy as a System of Actions: From Natural Economy to Market Self-Centralization
